cards.title: Client `ctx.connection.api` face removed entirely; history/transcript reads rerouted
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A1-30 · Client `ctx.connection.api` face removed entirely; history/transcript reads rerouted

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins consuming `ctx.connection.api.*` (e.g. `sessions.history`, `agentPresets`)
- **Touchpoints**: #3
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: alpha.1 removed the old apiProxy mirror face on `ctx.connection`; client calls throw. **If the call site silently swallows the error in a catch, the UI renders "forever blank" instead of an error** — a smoke that only asserts no-crash cannot catch it. The successor Remotes (`session/page` / `session/follow`) enforce the subagent address for `origin:'subagent'` sessions: ordinary `{ kind: 'session' }` requests are rejected with `session/agent-busy`; the paging `throughSeq` must not exceed the current cursor, and plain `page` paging cannot reach the last page.
- **Migration recipe**: Branch by session origin first. For ordinary sessions, move history reads to `session/page|follow`. For subagent-origin sessions (side chat, delegated threads), transcript reads have **no usable host RPC** — supply them through the plugin's own host routes instead: live threads read `agent.session.events` (AgentRegistry `create/get`), cold threads read `sessionPersistence.inspect`, with server-side seed cutting (e.g. at the `session/end-seed` boundary) plus `afterSeq` deltas, and the client fetches through the plugin's public routes. Once the client no longer consumes it, also remove `connection` from the `inject` list and the type mirror — leave no dead face.
- **Verification**: The live and cold (after host restart) paths return consistent transcripts; `afterSeq` deltas do not resurrect the seed; `session/list` shows subagent child sessions; with the route deliberately broken, the UI shows an error state rather than blank.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 connection/client/api.ts (old face now only re-exports protocol types)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1/packages/client/connection/src/client/api.ts) · [alpha.1 APIProxy→Remote architecture note](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-unary-apiproxy-remote-migration.md)
- **Field note** (2026-08-30, dsh-better-sidebar, macOS, npm 0.1.2-alpha.2 real machine): the side-chat transcript polling was missed in the migration and the errors were swallowed by catch, so on alpha.1+ hosts the tab rendered an empty transcript forever while smokes stayed all green; v0.18.0-alpha.0 fixed it with its own `sidechat.events` route. Design: see [sidechat-tab-design §10](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar/blob/main/docs/plans/2026-08-20-sidechat-tab-design.md).

---

cards.title: `dsh-subagent` descriptor format version 2 → 3 (stamped by the host package constant)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A1-31 · `dsh-subagent` descriptor format version 2 → 3 (stamped by the host package constant)

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Plugins that construct subagent seed/persisted descriptors or assert the shape of the `subagent/descriptor` event (`snapshotSubagentDescriptor` consumers)
- **Touchpoints**: #3
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: `SUBAGENT_DESCRIPTOR_VERSION` goes from 2 to 3; the descriptor's `version` field is stamped by the host package's snapshot function, so test assertions on the plugin side that hardcode the literal `version: 2` fail (the plugin runtime itself is unaffected — it does not write version).
- **Migration recipe**: Follow the package-exported constant in assertions — `import { SUBAGENT_DESCRIPTOR_VERSION } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'` — instead of hardcoding a literal; build seeds uniformly through `snapshotSubagentDescriptor`, and plugins do not assemble version themselves.
- **Verification**: After upgrading devDependencies, the relevant unit tests pass; the seed event `subagent/descriptor` has `version === SUBAGENT_DESCRIPTOR_VERSION`.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 descriptor.ts (= 3)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1/packages/subagent/subagent/src/descriptor.ts) · [rc.2 descriptor.ts (= 2)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2/packages/subagent/subagent/src/descriptor.ts)
- **Field note** (2026-08-30, dsh-better-sidebar): after devDeps 0.1.1-rc.1 → 0.1.2-alpha.2, the only failing seed assertion was this one; switching to follow the constant made everything green.

---

cards.title: `IWorkspaces` navigation methods moved to `ctx.uiWorkspace`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A1-32 · `IWorkspaces` navigation methods moved to `ctx.uiWorkspace`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that call `ctx.workspaces.connectWorkspace`, `startSession`, `pickDirectory`, `listDirectory`, or `createDirectory`, or that read `workspaces.list` snapshot fields `baselinesReady` / `recentWorkspaceId`
- **Touchpoints**: #3; indirectly #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: After the Client Runtime is unbundled, `ctx.workspaces` still exists as the Workspace Controller list/CRUD face, so install and typecheck can stay green while navigation throws (`connectWorkspace is not a function`). `baselinesReady` and `recentWorkspaceId` disappear from the Workspace snapshot (replaced by `phase`). Treating an empty `items` array while `phase` is still `pending` as "no workspace yet" is a false answer during boot.
- **Migration recipe**: Keep list and Workspace CRUD on `ctx.workspaces` (`IWorkspaces` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-controller/client`). Move navigation and directory UI to `ctx.uiWorkspace` (`UiWorkspace` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace/client`):

  | rc.2 `ctx.workspaces` (aggregated Client Runtime) | 0.1.2 owner |
  |---|---|
  | `list` / `create` / `rename` / `delete` / `insertBefore` / `insertSessionBefore` / `archiveSession` | `ctx.workspaces` (Workspace Controller) |
  | `connectWorkspace` / `startSession` | `ctx.uiWorkspace` |
  | `pickDirectory` / `listDirectory` / `createDirectory` | `ctx.uiWorkspace` |
  | `openPath` | not on either remaining face; Host path open is `ctx.remote.session.openWorkspacePath` (see [API-01](api-migration-0.1.2-alpha.2.md)) |
  | snapshot `baselinesReady` | `workspaces.list.phase === 'ready'` **and** `sessions.list.phase === 'ready'` |
  | snapshot `recentWorkspaceId` | gone; resolve the current session's workspace first, else the latest session `updatedAt` (fallback workspace `createdAt`) — or call `uiWorkspace.startSession()`, which does this |

  Also:

  - Add `'uiWorkspace'` to the client `export const inject` service list so the plugin waits for the host-mounted service instead of throwing. Do **not** add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` to `dsh.client.inject` unless this plugin's client bundle actually imports that package; the web host already mounts it.
  - If the source names `IWorkspaces` / `UiWorkspace`, those owning packages must be direct type/dev/peer dependencies ([DSH-0.1.2-A1-25](#dsh-0.1.2-a1-25--deepseek-aidsh-client-runtime-package-removed-client-symbols-migrated-by-domain)).
  - Do not keep calling the old methods on `ctx.workspaces` just because API-01 says ordinary UI uses `ctx.workspaces` — that sentence applies to the list projection and Workspace CRUD, not to navigation.

- **Verification**: `skipLibCheck: false` typecheck shows no leftover `connectWorkspace` / `pickDirectory` on `IWorkspaces`; a real web cold boot has no pending `uiWorkspace`; one connect and one directory-pick path succeed after both list snapshots report `phase === 'ready'`.
- **Source**: [rc.2 aggregated `IWorkspaces`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2/packages/client/runtime/src/client/contract/workspaces.ts) · [alpha.1 Workspace Controller `IWorkspaces` (no navigation)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1/packages/api/workspace-controller/src/client/service.ts) · [alpha.1 `UiWorkspace` / `uiWorkspace` service](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-workspace/src/client/navigation.ts) · [alpha.1 Workspace snapshot `phase` (no `baselinesReady` / `recentWorkspaceId`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1/packages/api/workspace-controller/src/client/model.ts)
- **Field note** (2026-08-28, [dsh-desktop-safe-market](https://github.com/bruc3van/dsh-desktop-safe-market) 0.2.16 → 0.3.0, Web Client): a marketplace plugin that called `workspaces.connectWorkspace` / `pickDirectory` and gated on `baselinesReady` / `recentWorkspaceId` broke when the Client Runtime split. List/CRUD stayed on `ctx.workspaces`; navigation moved to `ctx.uiWorkspace`. Ready-state became the conjunction of workspace `phase` and session `phase`; recency is derived from the current session, then `updatedAt` (the same algorithm the host `UiWorkspaceService` still uses).

---

*Host UI/performance changes without cards do not mean "definitely no API impact"; they only mean the official material declares no
plugin migration action. When a real plugin is found to be affected, add a card backed by primary-source evidence.*

cards.title: Restore `SessionEvent.ignorable` for third-party persisted events
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A2-01 · Restore `SessionEvent.ignorable` for third-party persisted events

- **Type**: fix
- **Applies to**: Plugins that produce third-party persisted SessionEvents, and persistence/reload/transport integrations
- **Touchpoints**: #2
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: alpha.1 could not retain the marker on external informational events; now that alpha.2 restores it, old adapters that keep dropping the marker will make first-party readers reject Sessions containing unknown events.
- **Migration recipe**: Producers should write `ignorable: true` only for informational events whose semantics an old reader can omit without affecting reconstruction; the marker is not a consumer-side filtering directive, and events remain in loaded events after reload. What alpha.2 restores is the retention semantics of envelope/persistence/reload/transport; the public live `Session.append(...)` still has no `ignorable` parameter, so ordinary plugins with only this API should mark the producer seam as a capability gap rather than faking a public entry via cast. JSONL, SQLite, API transports, and the generated catalog must preserve the field as-is; unknown events without the marker remain required-on-read. The SQLite provider accepts only schema 20, does not auto-migrate schema 19, and rejects other schemas; back up/export, or rebuild per the provider documentation, before upgrading.
- **Verification**: In manual envelope/seed setups, or in tests that own a persistence seam, unknown events with `ignorable: true` still exist in loaded events after reload and old readers can omit their semantics; unknown required events are rejected; a plain `Session.append` should not be documented as supporting the field; schema 19 is rejected, and a rebuilt schema 20 boots.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2) · [retain ignorable external session events decision](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-30-retain-ignorable-external-session-events.md) · revert of [DSH-0.1.2-A1-02](v0.1.2-alpha.1.md)

---

cards.title: Remote failures become `RemoteError` instances; error codes gain namespaces
NPM packages trim unneeded peer dependencies
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A2-03 · NPM packages trim unneeded peer dependencies

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Plugin packaging, installation, and dependency graph maintenance
- **Touchpoints**: None (packaging/distribution surface)
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: Upstream moved some internal edges to dependencies/devDependencies based on runtime ownership, keeping peers only for Cordis or identity-sensitive exports; standalone TypeScript consumers that directly reference the moved-out type packages may need to declare those dependencies explicitly.
- **Migration recipe**: Also look at the opposite direction: alpha.2 adds peers as well (`dsh-session-projection` and others), see [DSH-0.1.2-A2-08](v0.1.2-alpha.2.md). First choose the single package manager the repository currently uses, per its lockfile; verify in an isolated directory with a frozen lockfile or equivalent mode. Check which type/runtime packages the plugin actually imports and add direct dependencies; delete an override only after proving item by item that it exists solely for a pruned peer. Do not switch package managers or rewrite a second lockfile.
- **Verification**: Installation and typecheck succeed; no new peer/missing-package errors related to the target upgrade; the dependency graph and packed artifacts change only as expected.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 release notes, "Bug fixes"](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2)
- **Field note** (2026-08-30, dsh-tui dependency tree measurements): Two pitfalls bypass the normal "add a direct dependency" check: ① `legacy-peer-deps=true` makes npm skip the alpha.2 official CLI's peer `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-group` (top-level import of `dsh-app-boot`), leaving the npx cache tree incomplete and the CLI failing at startup with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — installing/rebuilding the CLI tree requires a clean npmrc; ② `dsh-subagent` declares `@deepseek-ai/dsh-util-time` in `optionalDependencies`, but `lib/index.js` imports it unconditionally at the top level — npm skips the optional, and it only crashes at runtime, while static install and typecheck both pass. The verification checklist should include a dependency-tree cold boot, not just successful installation.
- **Field note** (2026-08-31, Web Client plugin source migration): A packed package's `devDependencies` are not passed to consumers; ui-chat's `.d.ts` references declarations such as `dsh-client-store`, UI primitives, and session/commands/conversation. With `skipLibCheck: true` enabled, a missing package may not be reported at the dependency declaration but instead turns `ctx.useChat` selectors/callbacks into implicit `any`. During migration, temporarily enable `skipLibCheck: false` to find all declaration owners, then add the packages actually consumed as direct dev/peer dependencies; see [API-10](api-migration-0.1.2-alpha.2.md#api-10--web-client-runtime-unbundling-keyed-chat-snapshots-and-command-attachment-parameters).

---

cards.title: Fix empty client graph for `dsh web` on Node.js 24.0–24.11.1
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A2-04 · Fix empty client graph for `dsh web` on Node.js 24.0–24.11.1

- **Type**: fix
- **Applies to**: Startup wrappers and CI matrices that added workarounds for this Node range, such as forcing Node 22 or skipping `dsh web`
- **Touchpoints**: #7
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: Node 24.0–24.11.1 reports major 24 but still carries the v1 internal loader; alpha.1's `vendor/loader` judged v2 by major version, with the `resolveSync` arguments reversed, so the `dsh web` process starts but `__DSH_BOOT__.entries` is empty and HMR cannot find the entry. alpha.2 instead probes the loader shape via `getOrCreateModuleJob` / `getModuleJobForImport`. `engines.node` is `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` on both tags — unchanged, so do not look for differences in engines.
- **Migration recipe**: Remove only branches with evidence of specifically bypassing this defect (forcing Node 22, skipping `dsh web`, probing the loader by major version); keep other Node compatibility constraints. The verification matrix must include versions inside the failure window, not just latest/LTS.
- **Verification**: Cold boot at least on Node 24.9, which official CI uses (failure window 24.0–24.11.1), on the fixed Node 24.12 or current 24.x, and on a supported Node 22 LTS; when the plugin involves HMR, verify HMR on all three tiers.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 release notes, "Bug fixes"](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2) · [alpha.2 vendor/README item 19](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/vendor/README.md) · [alpha.2 loader shape probing](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/vendor/loader/src/internal.ts) · [alpha.2 CI pins Node 24.9](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/.github/workflows/ci.yml)

---

cards.title: Plugin inventory returns optional Agent Preset grouping
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A2-05 · Plugin inventory returns optional Agent Preset grouping

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Host/Web Client plugins that consume `pluginInventory/list` or validate `PluginInventorySnapshot` strictly
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #5
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: `PluginInventorySnapshot` gains an optional `agentPresets`; `AgentPresetPluginGroup`, `AgentPresetPluginRow`, and `PresetPluginEnablement` are also exposed. Consumers with closed schemas or that reject unknown fields may fail.
- **Migration recipe**: Parse `agentPresets` as an optional field, keeping the old entries view when it is absent; do not rebuild the whole object in a way that drops future fields. When presets need to be displayed, render from trust, rows, and `boolean | 'conditional'` enablement.
- **Verification**: The field may be absent when no preset roster exists; with a roster present, multiple preset/conditional rows parse; the old entries behavior is unchanged.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 PluginInventorySnapshot types](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/packages/host/plugin-inventory/src/types.ts) · [alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2)

---

cards.title: Client Remote adds fixed Host facts `$host.home/isLoopback`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A2-06 · Client Remote adds fixed Host facts `$host.home/isLoopback`

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Web Client integrations that previously called `host.describe` or need the Host home/loopback state
- **Touchpoints**: #3
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: alpha.1 had only generation-ready frames and per-domain queries, with no `ctx.remote.$host`; the alpha.2 client face adds plain values `home` and `isLoopback`.
- **Migration recipe**: In alpha.2, read `ctx.remote.$host.home` (may be `undefined` before the first ready frame) and `ctx.remote.$host.isLoopback`. `$host` is not a store — it has no subscriptions or generation counter; to react to reconnects, listen for `connection/reset` instead of polling it.
- **Verification**: Check `home` before and after ready; verify the boolean against loopback/non-loopback connections; the reconnect path is driven by `connection/reset`.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 API gateway README](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/packages/api/gateway/README.md) · [alpha.2 APIProxy→Remote note](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-unary-apiproxy-remote-migration.md)

cards.title: `sessionProjections` becomes a required inject and peer for multiple tool packages
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A2-08 · `sessionProjections` becomes a required inject and peer for multiple tool packages - **Type**: breaking - **Applies to**: Hosts that do not use the full shipped bundle and compose their own profiles, mounting `dsh-tool-todo`, `dsh-tool-subagent`, `dsh-agent`, `dsh-agent-loop`, `dsh-terminal-bash`, and similar packages individually; plugins that list these packages as peers - **Touchpoints**: #3 - **Action level**: required-if-hit - **Symptoms**: In alpha.2, `dsh-tool-todo`'s `inject` changes from `['tools']` to `['tools', 'sessionProjections']` (`src/index.ts:23`), and `dsh-tool-subagent`'s to `['tools', 'subagents', 'systemPrompt', 'sessionProjections']` (`src/index.ts:43`); `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection` is added as a peer of `dsh-agent`, `dsh-agent-loop`, `dsh-tool-subagent`, `dsh-terminal-bash`, and others. When the composition has no session-projection service, these entries stall at `pending (waiting for service: sessionProjections)`. - **Migration recipe**: Users of the shipped bundle are unaffected: `dsh-base` alpha.2 already mounts `session-projection` (`cordis.patch.yml:138`) and `session-projection-cache`. For self-composed profiles, add a `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection` line before these packages; when a plugin lists the above packages as peers, add the `dsh-session-projection` peer as well. This is the opposite direction that [DSH-0.1.2-A2-03](v0.1.2-alpha.2.md) does not mention — adding a peer is more dangerous than pruning one, because a missing peer shows up not as a typecheck error but as a runtime pending. - **Verification**: `dsh --profile

--dump-config` shows no pending lines; cold boot and run one message → tool → response round. - **Source**: [alpha.2 tool-todo `inject`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/packages/todo/tool-todo/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 tool-subagent `inject`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `dsh-agent` package.json (new peer)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/packages/core/agent/package.json) · [alpha.2 base composition session-projection lines](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) ---

cards.title: `dsh-settings` drops the runtime `settingsNamespace` export; namespaces are validated at compile time
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A2-10 · `dsh-settings` drops the runtime `settingsNamespace` export; namespaces are validated at compile time

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Host-side plugins that register/read/write settings namespaces (`ctx.settings.register/update/get`) and test doubles that mirror this seam
- **Touchpoints**: #3
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `import { settingsNamespace } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings'` fails to compile on alpha.2 with TS2724 (no exported member) — typecheck fails after upgrading devDependencies. The runtime exports are now only `SettingsConflictError` / `SettingsProvider` / `redactSecrets` / default; the helper was still present in alpha.1 and earlier.
- **Migration recipe**: Namespace validity checking has moved to compile time via the template literal type `SettingsNamespaceInput` (lowercase letter at the start + `[a-z0-9-]` suffix; `SettingsNamespace` is a brand type): on the host side, pass namespace **literal constants** directly to `register/update/get` (compliant literals compile as-is) and stop calling the runtime conversion helper; in test doubles, construct `SettingsConflictError` with an `as SettingsNamespace` brand conversion.
- **Verification**: Typecheck passes after upgrading devDependencies; unit-test the namespace register/read/write/listen paths; read and write once on a real host settings panel.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 settings/src/index.ts (SettingsNamespaceInput, no settingsNamespace export)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/packages/settings/settings/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 settings/src/index.ts (export still present)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.1/packages/settings/settings/src/index.ts)
- **Field note** (2026-08-30, dsh-better-sidebar, devDeps 0.1.1-rc.1 → 0.1.2-alpha.2): After the upgrade, all typecheck failures came from this single semantic change (two call sites: the host side and the smoke-test double); the fix passes constants directly plus the brand conversion, see [PR #472](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar/pull/472).

---

*Host UI/performance changes without cards only mean the official material declares no plugin migration action; they do not prove the absence
of API or behavior impact. When a real plugin is found to be affected, add a primary source and reproducible verification.*

cards.title: New capability: plugin settings card via `settings.plugin.item` keyed slot
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A3-01 · New capability: plugin settings card via `settings.plugin.item` keyed slot

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that want an in-page card in the official Settings → Plugins panel (a `settings.plugin.item` keyed slot whose key equals the plugin's settings namespace)
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #5
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: none for existing plugins — the surface is additive; adopting it changes where users edit plugin options (in-page card vs raw `<dshHome>/settings.yaml`) and how the plugin's Node half exposes the option list.
- **Migration recipe**: register the plugin's settings namespace through the Node half (`settings` service, same-named namespace the plugin already uses), then have the client render a card into `settings.plugin.item[key = namespace]`; the card reads/updates via the declared schema instead of ad-hoc files; keep the full option list available in `settings.yaml` for advanced knobs and document which subset the card shows; changes apply live (saved state is re-read by the running plugin — no restart).
- **Verification**: open Settings → Plugins, find the plugin's card, toggle/change a field, and confirm the running plugin reacts without a web restart; verify the packed client artifact contains the card entry, not just the source.
- **Source**: [alpha.2/alpha.3 plugin-owned settings surface design](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-12-plugin-owned-settings-surface.md) · [whale-girl 4fe5792 — settings card integration](https://github.com/vlln/whale-girl/commit/4fe5792c6f873c6b3a29dd12198ba47a397e17f3) · [dsh-loop 488b574 — per-tool dynamic settings registration](https://github.com/vlln/dsh-loop/commit/488b574c1603320cc078024ea5ee2aea9a3ceff6)
- **Field note** (2026-08-31, whale-girl): the first integration implemented a high-frequency subset of 7 fields (show-on-page, size, opacity, wandering, sleep delay, feed/play reply pools) as two new client modules (settings-card 298 lines, settings-form 165 lines) plus 148 lines of tests and an 81-line decision record; the packed `lib/client.js` grew 543 lines total. A companion integration in dsh-loop ([488b574 — per-tool dynamic settings registration with a self-drawn switch](https://github.com/vlln/dsh-loop/commit/488b574c1603320cc078024ea5ee2aea9a3ceff6)) — two plugins adopting the same public seam independently is the strongest available evidence that the seam is stable enough to shape plugins around.

cards.title: optional SQLite Session-persistence provider removed — retained databases need an older build to export
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A3-02 · optional SQLite Session-persistence provider removed — retained databases need an older build to export - **Type**: breaking - **Applies to**: host profiles and deployments that explicitly mounted the optional SQLite session-persistence provider (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-sqlite` as a composition row or direct dependency), or that keep Session databases written by that provider. Consumers of the separate `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-query-sqlite` (derived FTS search index) or the generic `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-sqlite` KV provider are not affected — those packages stay. - **Touchpoints**: #2, #4 (deployments routing session persistence through the removed provider and keeping its database files) - **Action level**: required-if-hit - **Symptoms**: at 0.1.2-alpha.3 the package and its schema resources are gone from the official tree. A composition row that names the provider can no longer resolve, and databases written by the removed provider are **not opened or migrated** by current builds — session history stays in the files but is unreadable until it is exported from a build that still ships the provider. JSONL (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`) is the sole first-party implementation of `ctx.sessionPersistence`. - **Migration recipe**: (1) scan the profile composition and `--dump-config` output for any row or dependency referencing `session-persistence-sqlite` and remove it (shipped profiles never selected the provider); (2) **before** upgrading, export retained logical Sessions with a build that still contains the provider (the decision note's own words: "use a build that still contains that provider and export the logical Session before upgrading") — the new build will not open or migrate them; (3) confirm the authoritative store after upgrade is JSONL via `ctx.sessionPersistence`; do not point the Session-query SQLite provider at the old database as if it were persistence — it is a disposable derived index, not an authoritative store. - **Verification**: `dsh --profile

--dump-config` shows no sqlite persistence row; a session create → message → replay round trip persists through JSONL; a retained legacy database receives no migration or salvage writes, and its content is only available through the pre-upgrade export. - **Source**: [JSONL-only session persistence decision note (pinned dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3/.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-08-30-jsonl-only-session-persistence.md) · [provider package.json still present at dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2/packages/session/session-persistence-sqlite/package.json) · [alpha.3 release notes (SQLite Session persistence backend removed)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3) · [dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3) · backfill record: [v0.1.2-rc.1.md](v0.1.2-rc.1.md) "Backfill candidates" (SQLite removal was uncarded until this card) ## Corridor finding: no breaking changes for default profiles; one opt-in removal + one additive capability - **Scale**: 117 commits between the two tags, mostly web client (turn rail, session projection) and session work. - **Per-package verification** — every runtime API surface third-party plugins touch, compared at the two tags: - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (defineTool / register / ToolDefinition), `credentials`, `llm`, `agent`, `settings`, `host/webserver` (`WebRoute`), `vendor/cordis`: only `package.json` version bumps, no source changes. - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection`: the host RPC face plugins use (`rpc.ts` handle / intercept) is unchanged; its client-side transport (`src/client/connection.ts`) has one non-plugin-face change — a stalled transport-ready wait now logs a warning instead of aborting the connection generation. - `bundle/web-app` patch layer adds one built-in row, `session-turn-outline` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-turn-outline`), for the whole-log turn rail. The row is bundle-internal; third-party plugin loading is unaffected. - **Additive capability (this PR)**: the web client's Settings → Plugins panel gains a `settings.plugin.item` keyed-slot seam so plugins can render an in-page settings card. This is additive — no existing plugin face breaks (the batch re-validation below ran with zero code changes) — and is recorded as DSH-0.1.2-A3-01 for plugins that want the richer surface. Recorded by vlln plugin migrations (whale-girl, dsh-loop) as an independent addition to the corridor file that originally carried no cards. - **npm channels**: the `alpha` dist-tag now resolves to `0.1.2-alpha.3`; `latest`/`next` still resolve to `0.1.1-rc.2`. - **Batch re-validation**: the 17 omdsh-dev plugin repositories passed typecheck/tests/build and a real-harness tool smoke against a source checkout of `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3` with **zero code changes**. The only defect found (a `session_health` stats input check) is plugin-internal and unrelated to this edge. - **Conclusion**: for shipped and default profiles this edge stays a no-op for breaking migration; deployments that opted into the removed SQLite Session-persistence provider have one breaking removal — export retained Sessions from an older build first and drop the provider row ([DSH-0.1.2-A3-02](v0.1.2-alpha.3.md)). The additive settings-card seam is documented above as DSH-0.1.2-A3-01 for plugins that want the richer surface.

cards.title: The `report` subagent tool package is gone; `send_message` replaces it
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A4-01 · The `report` subagent tool package is gone; `send_message` replaces it

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile wrappers / bundle patches / agent presets that list `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-report` or the `tool-subagent-report` id; plugins and prompt material that tell a continuable child agent to call `report`
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `packages/subagent/tool-subagent-report` no longer exists at alpha.4, and the base bundle dropped both its `cordis.patch.yml` row and its `package.json` dependency. A profile or patch layer that still inserts the package fails to resolve it at boot; a prompt that instructs a child to "call `report` when done" refers to a tool that is not registered. Parent ↔ child follow-up traffic now goes through the bidirectional `send_message` tool of `tool-subagent-control` (the child addresses its parent, the parent addresses its direct continuable child).
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. `grep -rn 'tool-subagent-report\|subagent-report' <profile dir> <plugin repo>` — remove every insert/override row and manifest dependency that names the package (at alpha.3 the base bundle listed it at `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:376-377`; the `agent-team-profile` and `agent-presets` layers referenced it too).
  2. Rewrite prompt/system-prompt material: "report back with `report`" → "send follow-ups with `send_message` (`agentId` = your direct parent or direct continuable child)". The tool schema is in `packages/subagent/tool-subagent-control/src/index.ts:29-44` at alpha.4; do not invent extra parameters.
  3. If a plugin enumerates the child's tool layer by name (a capability filter), check that the filter still lets the child's structured-output tool through — the alpha.4 comment at `packages/core/tools/src/index.ts` was rewritten to say the delegation runtime registers only the structured-output tool into the child's layer.
- **Verification**: boot the profile against `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4`; the plugin inventory (Settings → Plugins → Plugin list) shows `tool-subagent-control` enabled and no `tool-subagent-report` row; a continuable child agent can answer a parent follow-up through `send_message`.
- **Source**: [alpha.4 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4) ("`send_message` … replacing the one-way `report` tool") · package removal in [compare dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4) (`packages/subagent/tool-subagent-report/` deleted; `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml` and `packages/bundle/base/package.json` drop the row/dependency) · `packages/subagent/tool-subagent-control/src/index.ts:29` at `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4`

cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A4-02 · `@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-python` is renamed to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-code-runtime-python`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile wrappers / packaging that depend on the Python code runtime package by name

cards.title: `Session.events` is removed; read the log through `seq` / `eventAt()` / `snapshotEvents()` / `ownEvents()`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A4-03 · `Session.events` is removed; read the log through `seq` / `eventAt()` / `snapshotEvents()` / `ownEvents()`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: host-plane plugins and persistence/transport integrations that read a `Session` object's event log (`session.events`, `session.events.length`, `session.events[i]`, `session.events.at(-1)`, spread copies)
- **Touchpoints**: #2 (persistent events), #3 (Remote `history` requests)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `Session` no longer has an `events` getter at alpha.4. TypeScript fails with "Property 'events' does not exist on type 'Session'"; untyped JavaScript reads `undefined` and then throws on `.length` / index access. The replacement API is read-on-demand: `session.seq` is the current log length (a `SessionLogOffset`), `session.eventAt(seq)` returns one accepted, deeply frozen event, `session.snapshotEvents(fromSeq?, toSeqExclusive?)` materializes a frozen snapshot of a half-open range (the complete snapshot is cached until the next append), and `session.ownEvents()` returns the events this session appended itself (excluding the fork-inherited prefix).
- **Migration recipe**: old → new ledger —
  - `session.events.length` → `session.seq`
  - `session.events[i]` → `session.eventAt(SessionSeq(i))` (validates the number; see A4-04)
  - `session.events` (whole log) → `session.snapshotEvents()`
  - `session.events.slice(a, b)` → `session.snapshotEvents(SessionLogOffset(a), SessionLogOffset(b))`
  - "events written by this session, not by the fork parent" → `session.ownEvents()`
  - Remote face: the `history` request's `atSeq` is now validated as a non-negative **safe** integer and rejected with `gateway/bad-request` ("atSeq must be a non-negative safe integer") — `packages/api/session-controller/src/commands.ts:193` at alpha.4; `SessionPromptRequest` itself is unchanged (`requestId` / `sessionId` / `mode` / `content` were already required at alpha.2).
  - Do not cache the array returned by `snapshotEvents()` across appends when you need live data; re-read `seq` and call again.
- **Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` of the plugin against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session` at `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4` passes with no `events` access; a runtime read of a live session through the new API returns the same event count as the projection/turn count shown in the web client.
- **Source**: [alpha.4 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4) ("Replace `Session.events` with on-demand read APIs") · `packages/core/session/src/index.ts:588-629` (`eventAt` / `snapshotEvents` / `ownEvents` / `isOwnSeq` / `get seq`) and `packages/core/session/README.md:54` at `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4` · `packages/api/session-controller/src/commands.ts:193` at `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4`
- **Field note** (2026-09-02, macOS, source checkout `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4`): none of the seven plugins in the verified fleet (a 13-tool Cordis tool plugin with raw wire clients, a cron plugin, three link-installed tool plugins, `dsh-better-sidebar@0.18.0-alpha.0`, `@omdsh-dev/dsh-genui@0.9.6`) read `Session.events` directly, so the ledger above is source-derived, not field-hit. Plugins that only go through `defineTool` / the Remote wire needed no change.

cards.title: `SessionSeq` / `SessionLogOffset` become branded numbers; `seedLength` becomes `isSeeded` + `inheritedEventCount`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A4-04 · `SessionSeq` / `SessionLogOffset` become branded numbers; `seedLength` becomes `isSeeded` + `inheritedEventCount`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: host-plane plugins that create agents or sessions with seeded/forked logs (`CreateAgentOptions`, `CreateSessionOptions`, `RestoredSessionOptions`), projection definitions (`ProjectionDefinition.init`), and any code that carries sequence numbers as plain `number` into `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent` types (`AgentState.openTurnStartSeq`, `lastStepStartSeq`, `lastStepBoundary.seq`, `SessionEventWindow.startSeq/endSeq`)
- **Touchpoints**: #2, #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `SessionSeq` and `SessionLogOffset` are now `BrandedNumber` types with constructor functions of the same name (`SessionSeq(value)` / `SessionLogOffset(value)`) that throw `TypeError` on anything but a non-negative safe integer. Plain `number` no longer type-checks where a seq or offset is expected; `null` seq slots use `OptionalSessionSeq` (`SessionSeq | null`) and cursors use `SessionSeqCursor` (`SessionSeq | -1`). The agent/session metadata field `seedLength?: number` is gone: fork seeding is now `meta.isSeeded?: boolean` plus a top-level `inheritedEventCount?: SessionLogOffset` (the exact inherited prefix length). `ProjectionDefinition.init` receives `(header, inheritedEventCount: SessionLogOffset)`.
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. Wrap every seq/offset you construct: `SessionSeq(n)` for event positions, `SessionLogOffset(n)` for lengths/boundaries (both exported from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types`). Values you receive from the host are already branded; pass them through untouched.
  2. `meta: { seedLength: n }` → `meta: { isSeeded: true }, inheritedEventCount: SessionLogOffset(n)` on `CreateAgentOptions` / `CreateSessionOptions`; `RestoredSessionOptions` requires `inheritedEventCount`.
  3. Projection definitions: change `init(header, seedLength)` to `init(header, inheritedEventCount)` and treat the second argument as a `SessionLogOffset`.
  4. Where you compared `openTurnStartSeq !== null` or `lastStepBoundary.seq`, the comparisons still work (branded numbers are numbers at runtime); only the declared types need updating.
- **Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` against the alpha.4 packages; at runtime, `SessionSeq(-1)` and `SessionLogOffset(1.5)` throw `TypeError`, and a freshly forked session in the same process shows `session.inheritedEventCount === session.firstLiveSeq` (for a resumed session the two differ: `firstLiveSeq` is the full stored log length while `inheritedEventCount` keeps the original fork cut).
- **Source**: [alpha.4 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4) ("Distinguish `SessionSeq` and `SessionLogOffset` with strong types; developers should pay attention to compatibility") · `packages/core/session/src/types.ts:29-62` (`SessionSeq`, `SessionLogOffset`, `SessionSeqCursor`, `OptionalSessionSeq`) · `packages/core/agent/src/index.ts:76-94` (`isSeeded`, `inheritedEventCount`, `seedLength` removed) · `packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts:62` (`init(header, inheritedEventCount: SessionLogOffset)`) · `packages/api/session-controller/src/commands.ts` fork path (`isSeeded: true`, `inheritedEventCount: cut`) — all at `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4`
- **Cross-reference**: extends [DSH-0.1.2-A1-27](v0.1.2-alpha.1.md#dsh-012-a1-27--session-content-reads-now-go-through-the-sessionbinding-durable-event-window) (the durable event window introduced at alpha.1): the window's `startSeq` / `endSeq` are `SessionSeq` from alpha.4 on.

cards.title: The `ptc` preset no longer publishes the general `workflow` tool
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A4-05 · The `ptc` preset no longer publishes the general `workflow` tool

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: profile wrappers / presets derived from the shipped `ptc` preset; prompt material that tells a PTC-mode agent to use `workflow`
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: in Web PTC mode the model no longer sees a `workflow` tool by default; `run_code` is the single model-authored orchestration surface. The `tool-workflow` row in `packages/preset/agent-presets/presets/ptc/agent.cordis.yml` is kept only as engine infrastructure for `ralph` (comment at lines 235-236) and is disabled for the model. Other presets are unchanged — the shipped `Standard mode` preset still lists `tool-workflow` as enabled (verified live, see the verification record).
- **Migration recipe**: if your preset extends `ptc` and relied on `workflow`, either re-enable `tool-workflow` in your own preset layer or rewrite the instructions around `run_code`; if your preset does not extend `ptc`, nothing changes. Do not "fix" this by editing the shipped preset file — override in your profile layer.
- **Verification**: open Settings → Plugins → Plugin list, switch the session preset selector to the PTC preset: `tool-workflow` shows as disabled while `workflow-worker-thread` and `tool-ralph` stay enabled; the upstream test "omits the general workflow tool only from PTC while retaining Ralph infrastructure" encodes the same expectation.
- **Source**: [alpha.4 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4) ("Stop exposing the general-purpose `workflow` tool by default in Web PTC Mode") · `packages/preset/agent-presets/presets/ptc/agent.cordis.yml:233-237` at `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4` (unchanged row at alpha.3 had no such restriction) · preset description change in the same file ("默认不提供 workflow 工具")

cards.title: The base bundle enables `web_fetch` by default
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A4-06 · The base bundle enables `web_fetch` by default

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: profile wrappers built on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` (Python SDK, Headless, ACP, custom profiles) that previously relied on `web_fetch` being off unless a preset enabled it; products with a stricter network policy
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: `tool-web` in the base bundle now carries `config: { fetch: true }` (`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:461-464`), so agents in non-web products get `web_fetch` alongside `web_search` without any preset opting in. A deployment that assumed "no outbound fetch unless enabled" now has one.
- **Migration recipe**: profiles that must not fetch override the row in their own patch layer (`- id: tool-web` with `config: { fetch: false }`); profiles that previously enabled fetch per preset can drop that override. Treat this as a policy review item, not a code change.
- **Verification**: boot the profile and list the model-facing tools of a new session (Plugin list → `tool-web`, or a first prompt asking the agent to enumerate its tools): `web_fetch` is present when you expect it and absent when you overrode it; the upstream bundle test now expects `{ fetch: true }`.
- **Source**: [alpha.4 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4) ("Enable `web_fetch` by default for the Python SDK, Headless, ACP, and custom Profiles") · `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:461-464` at `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4` and the bundle test expectation flip `fetch: false` → `fetch: true` in the [compare view](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4)

---

## Corridor verification record

What was checked for this edge, so a later migration can start from here instead of re-diffing.

- **Scale**: 297 commits between `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.3` (`dd6322d604`, 2026-08-31) and `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4` (`4e84901e64`, 2026-09-01); 2371 files changed. Most of the volume is the web client (settings UI, model catalog, turn navigation), session internals, and a repository-wide deletion of per-package `invariant.ts` files (internal assertion helpers — not an exported plugin face).
- **Per-package verification** — runtime API surfaces third-party plugins import, compared at the two tags:
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` (`defineTool` / `register` / `ToolDefinition`): one comment block rewritten in `src/index.ts` (child layer wording after the `report` removal), no signature changes.
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `vendor/cordis`, `credentials-local`, `settings-file`, `host/webserver` (`WebRoute`), `typert/*`: only `invariant.ts` deletions and version bumps.
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`: the changes carded above (A4-03, A4-04).
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent`: `seedLength` → `isSeeded` / `inheritedEventCount`, seq fields branded (A4-04).
  - Remote wire (`packages/api/session-controller`): `SessionPromptRequest` unchanged; `history` `atSeq` validation tightened (A4-03); `gateway/stream-server.ts` has a 19-line internal change with no contract change. An unauthenticated `POST /api/agentPreset.list` still answers 401 (the alpha.1+ probe signature from [pre-flight.md](pre-flight.md) step 1.5 holds).
- **npm channels** (measured 2026-09-02): `alpha` = `0.1.2-alpha.4`; `next` = `0.1.1-rc.2`. `latest` is `0.1.1-rc.2` only for the umbrella package `@deepseek-ai/dsh`; the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` sub-packages still have `latest` at `0.0.1-rc.1` / `0.1.0-rc.6`, so install sub-packages with an explicit version or the `alpha` tag.
- **Real-host validation** (macOS, three long-running web hosts on one `$DSH_HOME`, source checkout switched from alpha.2 to alpha.4 through a `~/.dsh/source/current` symlink flip, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` + `pnpm run build` in a fresh worktree, 1m37s):
  - Step 0 ghost check ([scripts/ghost-host-check.mjs](../scripts/ghost-host-check.mjs)) on all three hosts before the flip: memory and disk agreed (alpha.2). After the flip every host was restarted immediately — with a tsx-from-source host, leaving a process running across the flip is exactly the ghost the check exists for.
  - After restart, each host: ghost check "process is newer than the checkout's last change" (alpha.4), unauthenticated probe 401, and a live session through a dual-cohort raw wire client (`session/create` → `session/prompt` with client-minted `requestId` → `remote.mux` `session/follow` → `turn/end`; `tokenUsage` projection frame present; zero unrecognised frame types). First-boot logs: zero errors, no persistence/schema messages (the session store had already been migrated by alpha.2).
  - Plugin fleet loaded unchanged: a 13-tool Cordis tool plugin (imports `cordis`, `dsh-tools`, `dsh-llm`, `dsh-commands`), a cron plugin, three link-installed tool plugins, `dsh-better-sidebar@0.18.0-alpha.0`, `@omdsh-dev/dsh-genui@0.9.6` — all "Enabled" in Settings → Plugins → Plugin list; the web client reports `0.1.2-alpha.4-4e84901` and its console shows zero errors after load and after opening Settings. The plugin's own test suite (13 suites) exits 0 both before and after the switch, with **zero code changes**.
  - A full tool-chain run of the tool plugin against the alpha.4 host (a writer-seat session driving `emit_preset` → `emit_app` → `preview_app` → `verify_app` → `deploy_app` through the host's own tool faces, two checkpoint questions answered over `$events`): every stage passed, 417 s wall clock, zero tool errors.
  - Windows real-host validation (2026-09-02, source checkout at `4e84901e64`, Windows 11 host): the 17-plugin omdsh-dev fleet (eleven tool plugins, the tariff channel plugin with an agent-inbox reminder, security/session tooling, the toolkit aggregate) loaded unchanged with **zero code changes** — all six cards (A4-01 … A4-06) grep zero hits across the fleet. Every tool smoke-passed on the alpha.4 host (tariff, api_balance with a live credential, calculator, csv, diff, encoding, json, markdown, regex, schema, stat, time, security_audit, session_health, plugin_check); the alpha.2-era token/cookie channel contract also held on this host.
- **Not verified here**: the Python SDK / Headless / ACP products (A4-06 is source-derived); a plugin that actually reads `Session.events` or seeds forks (A4-03 / A4-04 recipes are derived from the tag's source and README, not from a field hit); client-plane plugins were checked for load and console cleanliness only, not exercised feature by feature.
- **Conclusion**: for tool plugins that stay on `defineTool` and the Remote wire, alpha.3 → alpha.4 is a restart-only edge. Session-log readers, fork seeders, projection authors, and profiles that pin `tool-subagent-report` / the Python runtime package name have real work (A4-01 … A4-04). Defaults moved for `workflow` (PTC only) and `web_fetch` (base bundle) — review, don't patch.

cards.title: `DomainSpec.compatibleVersions`: per-record reads and the legacy bootstrap accept vouched-for older versions
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A5-01 · `DomainSpec.compatibleVersions`: per-record reads and the legacy bootstrap accept vouched-for older versions

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: host-plane and author-migrated plugins that persist their own state through the storage-domain API (`defineDomain` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain`, opened through the storage service's `DomainFacility.open`); Cordis plugins that consume the storage service catalog (the `DomainSpec` / `KvUnitDescriptor` declarations); profile wrappers that route storage domains to a backend
- **Touchpoints**: #4
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: nothing changes unless a spec declares the field. On a `per-record` layout a stored document whose version stamp is not the unit's current `version` is FOREIGN and reads as absent — the silent-discard contract is unchanged. With `compatibleVersions` declared, the json per-record backend accepts documents stamped with any listed version, and the one-time legacy whole-unit bootstrap (`<root>/<name>.json`, the pre-per-record layout) accepts a legacy file whose `unit.version` is in the set. Writes always stamp the current `version`, `single`-layout reads stay exact-version, a stamp outside the set is still foreign, and `defineDomain` rejects entries that are not non-negative integers strictly below `version` (`packages/storage/storage-domain/src/spec.ts:117`).
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. When you bump a domain's `version` and old records still parse under the new zod schemas — declare the fields old records lack as optional — list the old version(s): `compatibleVersions: [3, 4]`. Old-stamped documents then decode as current on read; the first write after such a read re-stamps them current.
  2. When the old shape cannot be tolerated, do not list it: `per-record` silently discards the stale documents and `single` rejects, exactly as before. Compatibility is a declaration the owner vouches for; authoritative data keeps the default.
  3. Backend reach: the tolerance is implemented by the json per-record backend and its legacy bootstrap only. A backend without `compatibleVersions` support (the sqlite storage backend implements neither this nor `backupRecord`) keeps strict-version semantics — check what your profile routes the domain to before relying on the declaration.
- **Verification**: `defineDomain({ version: 5, compatibleVersions: [4] })` passes while `[5]`, `[-1]`, and `[1.5]` throw; open a json per-record unit whose documents are stamped `4` → the records load, stamped `3` without the declaration → absent; after `putRecord` the document file is stamped `5`; a legacy whole-unit file stamped `4` bootstraps when listed and is left alone (unit reads empty) when not.
- **Source**: [compare dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5) · `DomainSpec.compatibleVersions` and the `defineDomain` validation at [spec.ts:56,117](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/spec.ts#L56) · `KvUnitDescriptor.compatibleVersions` at [backend.ts:73](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/storage/storage/src/backend.ts#L73) · accepted-stamp reads and the bootstrap version gate at [per-record-unit.ts:105,123](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/storage/storage-json/src/per-record-unit.ts#L105) and [format.ts:114](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/storage/storage-json/src/format.ts#L114) · rationale and upgrade matrix in the implemented architecture note [2026-09-02-projcache-cross-version-read-compat.md](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-02-projcache-cross-version-read-compat.md)
- **Field note** (2026-09-03, Windows 11, npm packages `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage*` at both tags): reproduced at the storage layer, see the [corridor verification record](#corridor-verification-record).

cards.title: `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` + optional `KvUnit.backupRecord`: salvage a schema-failing record instead of refusing the whole domain open
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A5-02 · `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` + optional `KvUnit.backupRecord`: salvage a schema-failing record instead of refusing the whole domain open

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: plugins whose domains hold disposable derived data — caches, projections, indices that a cold read can rebuild from an authoritative source; backends/units that keep one movable document per record (the json `per-record` layout)
- **Touchpoints**: #4
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: nothing changes unless a spec declares the policy. The default (absent `invalidRecords`) is unchanged: a stored table record that fails its zod schema at `open` rejects the whole domain with `invalid-record` (`DomainError`), and the global slot always rejects. With `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'`, the domain layer moves the failing record's document aside through the optional `KvUnit.backupRecord(table, key)` — the json per-record implementation renames it to `<key>.json.bak.<YYYYMMDDHHmm>`, keeping the bytes for inspection and never reading them again — logs the concrete failure (domain, table, key, destination, zod cause), and continues the open with the record absent. A backend without `backupRecord` (the `single` layout, row stores, sqlite) falls back to the rejecting default, so the declaration is inert there. At alpha.5 only the host's own `session_projcache` domain declares the policy.
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. Declare `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` only for domains whose records are disposable derived data; authoritative data must keep the default reject-loud path.
  2. Confirm the backend the profile routes the domain to implements `KvUnit.backupRecord`; otherwise keep the default, because the declaration would not change behavior.
  3. Plan the rebuild: after a salvage the record is absent until the owning flow writes it again (the host's cache cold-refolds and checkpoints). Same-minute backups of the same key overwrite each other — the newer bytes win; distinct keys and minutes never collide.
- **Verification**: with the policy declared and a schema-failing record present, `open` resolves, the document is renamed to `*.json.bak.*` on disk, `loadAll` shows the key absent, a later `putRecord` recreates the record fresh, and the log names domain/table/key/destination/cause; without the declaration — or with a backend that has no `backupRecord` — the same unit rejects with `invalid-record`.
- **Source**: [compare dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5) · `DomainSpec.invalidRecords` contract at [spec.ts:67](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/spec.ts#L67) · the open-path salvage at [storage-domain/src/index.ts:131](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/storage/storage-domain/src/index.ts#L131) · `KvUnit.backupRecord` contract at [backend.ts:123](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/storage/storage/src/backend.ts#L123) · json rename implementation at [per-record-unit.ts:238](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/storage/storage-json/src/per-record-unit.ts#L238) · release notes [dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5) · rationale in [2026-09-02-projcache-cross-version-read-compat.md](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-02-projcache-cross-version-read-compat.md)
- **Field note** (2026-09-03, Windows 11, npm packages at `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5`): reproduced at the storage layer, see the [corridor verification record](#corridor-verification-record).

cards.title: Host fix: upgrading a 0.1.1-rc.2 / 0.1.2-alpha.3 home to alpha.4 could refuse the boot or drop session titles; alpha.5 reads all three `session_projcache` generations
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.2-A5-03 · Host fix: upgrading a 0.1.1-rc.2 / 0.1.2-alpha.3 home to alpha.4 could refuse the boot or drop session titles; alpha.5 reads all three `session_projcache` generations

- **Type**: fix
- **Applies to**: hosts upgraded across the 0.1.1-rc.2 / 0.1.2-alpha.3 / 0.1.2-alpha.4 on-disk generations — anyone upgrading an existing `$DSH_HOME` (registry install or source checkout) rather than starting fresh; plugin authors whose users reported "the app will not start" or "session titles are gone from the list" after upgrading to alpha.4
- **Touchpoints**: none (host persistence surface)
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: two failure shapes on alpha.4 when an already-used home was upgraded. (1) From a v3 home (shipped by 0.1.1-rc.2, single-file `storages/session_projcache.json`): the per-record bootstrap migrated the legacy file without checking its `unit.version`, stamping the old records with v5 into the new tree; the domain open then rejected them (`invalid-record` — the lineage fields `isSeeded` / `inheritedEventCount` were required at alpha.4) and the whole domain refused to load, so the plugin tree failed at boot. Because the bootstrap wrote before validation ran, the first boot permanently "poisoned" the new tree: every later boot saw a non-empty tree, never took the legacy path again, and the home stayed unusable. (2) From a v4 home (shipped by 0.1.2-alpha.3, per-record): v4 documents were silently discarded by the strict version-stamp check, and SessionList is a cache-only zero-I/O read, so the list served rows without projections and titles only reappeared as each session was individually reopened.
- **Migration recipe**: upgrade the host to alpha.5 — no plugin code change is required for any of these symptoms. The host's `session_projcache` domain now declares `version: 5, compatibleVersions: [3, 4]` with the two lineage fields optional, so: pristine v3 single-file homes bootstrap and serve titles immediately; "poisoned" v5-stamped-lineageless documents self-heal (they parse under the optional schema and their content is the real pre-upgrade cache data); v4 documents read directly. Stale rows of forked (seeded) sessions still fail the identity match — `identityMatches` normalizes absent lineage to the unseeded shape at [session-projection-cache/src/index.ts:372-381](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/index.ts#L372) — and are discarded to a cold rebuild, the safe side. Deployment caveat: a profile that routes this domain to the sqlite backend gets none of the tolerance (strict-version semantics), because sqlite implements neither `compatibleVersions` nor `backupRecord`; shipped compositions route it to json. Plugin-side corollary: this edge is the host itself applying the storage-domain vocabulary now available to plugins — cross-reference [DSH-0.1.2-A5-01](#dsh-012-a5-01--domainspeccompatibleversions-per-record-reads-and-the-legacy-bootstrap-accept-vouched-for-older-versions) and [DSH-0.1.2-A5-02](#dsh-012-a5-02--invalidrecords-backup-and-skip--optional-kvunitbackuprecord-salvage-a-schema-failing-record-instead-of-refusing-the-whole-domain-open).
- **Verification**: boot the host against `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5` on homes of all four shapes (pristine v3, poisoned v3, v4, fresh): the app starts and the SessionList RPC returns the recorded titles verbatim. Upstream's archived-fixture recovery tests do exactly this through the real storage stack: [tests/fixtures.spec.ts](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/session/session-projection-cache/tests/fixtures.spec.ts) plus `tests/fixtures/v3-single-unit.json`, `v4-session-doc.json`, `v5-lineageless-doc.json`, and `v5-session-doc.json` (media archives produced by the real released builds).
- **Source**: [release notes dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5) ("Fix an issue where upgrading from 0.1.1-rc.2 or 0.1.2-alpha.3 could prevent the app from starting or make session titles disappear from the list") · implemented architecture note [2026-09-02-projcache-cross-version-read-compat.md](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-02-projcache-cross-version-read-compat.md) (problem, three generations, upgrade matrix, alternatives) · projcache domain declaration and identity normalization at [session-projection-cache/src/index.ts:372-381](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/session/session-projection-cache/src/index.ts#L372) · fixture tests at [fixtures.spec.ts](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5/packages/session/session-projection-cache/tests/fixtures.spec.ts) · [compare dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4...dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5)

---

## Corridor verification record

What was checked for this edge, so a later migration can start from here instead of re-diffing.

- **Scale**: 6 commits between `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.4` (`4e84901e64`, 2026-09-01) and `dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.5` (`db6bdc3576`, 2026-09-02); 280 files changed, of which 252 are `package.json` version bumps from `0.1.2-alpha.4` to `0.1.2-alpha.5`. Real source changes are confined to the storage layer (`storage-domain`, `storage`, `storage-json`), `session-projection-cache`, the `tool-cordis` API catalog, and documentation (storage subsystem docs plus the implemented architecture note) — see the per-package list below.
- **Per-package verification** — runtime API surfaces third-party plugins import, compared at the two tags:
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`, the Remote wire (`packages/api/*`), `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`, and the preset files: no source changes — only version bumps. Nothing from the alpha.4 cards (A4-01…A4-06) changed again on this edge.
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-json`: the changes carded above (A5-01, A5-02).
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection-cache`: the host-side instance of both capabilities plus the identity-match normalization (A5-03).
  - `tool-cordis` `api-catalog.ts`: the `SERVICE_API`/`TYPE_API` entries for `DomainFacility.open`, `DomainSpec`, `KvUnit`, and `KvUnitDescriptor` were updated to carry the two new fields and the optional `backupRecord` member (descriptive for catalog consumers; no catalog schema change).
- **npm channels** (measured 2026-09-03): `alpha` = `0.1.2-alpha.5` for the umbrella `@deepseek-ai/dsh` and for sub-packages (sampled `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`); `next` = `0.1.1-rc.2`. `latest` is `0.1.1-rc.2` only for the umbrella package — sub-packages still have `latest` at `0.0.1-rc.1` / `0.1.0-rc.6`, so install sub-packages with an explicit version or the `alpha` tag.
- **Storage-layer reproduction** (Windows 11, 2026-09-03, npm packages `@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage*` at `0.1.2-alpha.4` vs `0.1.2-alpha.5`, isolated temp homes, one scenario script run against each cohort's installed packages): alpha.4 reproduced both failure shapes — under a v5 per-record descriptor, documents stamped 3/4/9 all read as absent and the unit has no `backupRecord` member; a v3 whole-unit home opened under a strict v5 schema rejects with `invalid-record` (the unguarded bootstrap migrates and poisons), and the same home still rejects when the (unknown at alpha.4) salvage declaration is present. Alpha.5 on identical inputs: documents stamped 3 and 4 read while the stamp-9 document stays foreign; a write re-stamps the current version; `backupRecord` is present and moves `k3.json` to `k3.json.bak.<timestamp>` with the bytes kept, the key absent on the next load, and recreatable by `putRecord`; the strict-schema v3 home now opens with the record absent (bootstrap version gate — no poisoning); the tolerant home with `compatibleVersions: [3, 4]` opens with the legacy record present; and the `invalidRecords: 'backup-and-skip'` home opens with the failing document moved to `legacy.json.bak.<timestamp>`.
- **Real-host validation**: performed on `dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1`, which is alpha.5 plus the version-bump commit — see the record in [v0.1.2-rc.1.md](v0.1.2-rc.1.md#real-host-validation-macos-2026-09-03). Relevant to this edge: a `$DSH_HOME` that had already been through alpha.2 → alpha.4 booted with cached session titles present and **zero** `*.json.bak.*` files, i.e. the new salvage path was armed but not triggered; the previous generation's projection-cache records were read as compatible.
- **Not verified here**: a full host boot with the web client's SessionList (the A5-03 verification section above relies on the upstream archived-fixture recovery tests); Linux hosts; a profile that routes `session_projcache` to the sqlite backend.
- **Conclusion**: for plugins that stay on `defineTool`, the Remote wire, presets, or client UI, alpha.4 → alpha.5 is a restart-only edge with zero code changes. Plugin storage-domain authors gain two optional capabilities (`compatibleVersions` read tolerance, `backup-and-skip` salvage for disposable derived data); adopters must confirm their backend implements them. Hosts upgrading an existing rc.2/alpha.3-era home had real boot/title bugs on alpha.4 and should move to alpha.5 (A5-03). As on earlier edges (rollup R-11), the release notes under-describe the change: they announce only the boot/title fix, while the two storage-domain capabilities exist only in the tag's source — which is why every card above is pinned to the tag rather than to the notes.

cards.title: v0→v1 migrator refuses 0.1.2-alpha.x session logs (`replayState` `kind`)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-01 · v0→v1 migrator refuses 0.1.2-alpha.x session logs (`replayState` `kind`)

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Host plane. Any deployment upgrading from 0.1.2-alpha.x with real session history to 0.1.3-alpha.1; any plugin/integration that reads session logs across this boundary inherits the same refusal through the persistence layer.
- **Touchpoints**: #2, #4
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the 0.1.3 Web UI shows
  `Failed to load history: failed to observe session "session-<id>": @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v0-to-v1 refuses this format v0 Session: assistant/chunk 95 chunk replayState has unexpected member "kind"; source v0 artifact remains unchanged (raw log: …)`.
  What looks like "slow loading" before the failure is the migration scan itself (40 s+ for
  a ~16 MB log, no progress or error surfaced while it runs).
- **Migration recipe**: none available yet. Do not hand-edit v0 logs — the migrator is
  fail-closed and leaves the source artifact unchanged, so nothing is corrupted, but the
  session stays blocked. Until an upstream fix or an official rewrite path exists, keep a
  0.1.2-rc.1 installation available for reading old logs (rc.1 loads them natively — it has
  no v0→v1 migrator on this path).
- **Verification**: after an upstream fix lands, open a previously refusing session on
  0.1.3; message and tool-card counts must match the 0.1.2-rc.1 rendering of the same log.
- **Source**: measured 2026-09-05 on the release-tarball build `0.1.3-alpha.1-9523542`; the
  refusal string reproduced on two sessions (15.7 MB / 19 MB logs, refusing at chunks
  ~95/~94) out of a 6-session real-history batch (same writer family, all refused). Full
  evidence chain (build identity, CDP timing, raw refusal strings, three-leg attribution):
  [upstream-0.1.3 adaptation audit, pinned](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex04130/dsh-forge/8ab0b148b2382b2a33158039fd10d7625b4e145a/docs/audits/upstream-0.1.3-adaptation-audit.md)
  (§0/§7/§7.5). Official writer coordinates: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` `toPiReplayState()`
  in the installed 0.1.3-alpha.1 tree (`response.kind: "pi-ai"`, `version: 2`) — this
  version is distributed via the release-tarball channel and is not on npm
  (`latest`/`alpha`/`next` = 0.1.2-rc.1/alpha.5/0.1.2-rc.1, registry checked 2026-09-06);
  re-verify against the official tag once it is published.
  Comparison control: the same batch loads natively on 0.1.2-rc.1 (no migration face) and
  in the 0.1.2-alpha.3 writer home.

Root cause (observed shape) — the refused member is written by official core, not plugins.
Three-leg proof, measured 2026-09-05:

1. **Plugin negative scan**: zero hits for `replayState` / `assistant/chunk` writes across
   all local plugin sources (dynamic plugins, profile plugins, community plugins).
2. **Official writer**: the pi-ai adapter `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` constructs the
   replay envelope itself in `toPiReplayState()` — `response.kind: "pi-ai"`, `version: 2`
   (installed tree, official package).
3. **Older writer generation layered in the append-only log**: the refused
   `assistant/chunk` events carry
   `replayState: {kind: "pi-ai", version: 1, api: "openai-completions", …}` — `kind` at the
   top level with `version: 1`, emitted by the pre-alpha.4 writer generation and preserved
   verbatim in the append-only log. The 0.1.3 `dsh-session-format-v0-to-v1` migrator
   validates `replayState` against a single-generation schema, so it rejects the layered
   older-generation member and refuses the whole session (fail-closed; the source v0
   artifact stays unchanged — good safety behavior, but the net result is a hard block on
   history).

```json
{"type":"assistant/chunk","seq":95,"data":{"turn":1,"step":1,"chunk":{"type":"finish","reason":{"kind":"tool-calls"},"replayState":{"kind":"pi-ai","version":1,"api":"openai-completions","provider":"…","model":"…","responseModel":"…","responseId":"…","stopReason":"toolUse","blocks":[…]}}}}
```

`replayState.kind` at the top level with `version: 1` marks the older writer generation; the
current official writer nests `kind` inside `response` with `version: 2`.

- **Field note** (2026-09-05, reporting deployment): performance contrast on the same
  15.7 MB session — 0.1.2-alpha.3 opens it in ≈3.0 s (headless CDP measurement); 0.1.3
  spends 40–200 s scanning before refusing, with an undifferentiated "Loading history…"
  state. Expected behavior: accept the writer-family discriminator (or provide a documented
  0.1.2→0.1.3 log rewrite path), and surface per-session migration progress/failure
  promptly instead of an indefinite loading state.

---

cards.title: cross-version `resume` on 0.1.2-alpha.3 logs reports `cursor behind the last applied entry`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-02 · cross-version `resume` on 0.1.2-alpha.3 logs reports `cursor behind the last applied entry`

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Host plane. Deployments on 0.1.3-alpha.1 resuming a session whose log was
  written by 0.1.2-alpha.3 (fresh log — distinct from the refused-history case in
  DSH-0.1.3-A1-01).
- **Touchpoints**: #2
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: resuming such a session on 0.1.3 reports
  `cursor behind the last applied entry (gateway/internal)`; the resumed turn does not
  start.
- **Migration recipe**: none yet. Do not retry blindly — the error surfaces as a
  `gateway/internal` failure; only retry when the operation is confirmed idempotent. Keep
  the 0.1.2 line available for resuming these sessions until an upstream fix or a
  documented resume-migration path exists.
- **Verification**: after an upstream fix, resume the same session on 0.1.3; the resumed
  turn must append to the log and stream a reply without the cursor error.
- **Source**: measured 2026-09-05 on the same release-tarball build
  `0.1.3-alpha.1-9523542`; single observed case (fresh 0.1.2-alpha.3-written log) — scope
