cards.title: Windows install fails on the `fs-ext` native build; the runtime never calls `flock` on Windows
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 · Windows install fails on the `fs-ext` native build; the runtime never calls `flock` on Windows

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile wrappers / packaging; any Windows machine without Visual Studio
  Build Tools upgrading to 0.1.3-alpha.1
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging/install surface)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `pnpm install` exits 1. `fs-ext@2.1.1` runs its `node-gyp configure build`
  install script and fails with `gyp ERR! find VS … You need to install the latest version of
  Visual Studio (including the "Desktop development with C++" workload)`. `fs-ext` is a pinned
  dependency of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` and is statically imported from
  `src/lease.ts`, so `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` cannot skip it — the module must exist
  and load.
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. Confirm the platform path first: on Windows, `lease.ts` takes `acquireLockHandleWin32`
     (a named kernel semaphore via `CreateSemaphoreW`) and holds "never a file lock or
     handle"; `flock` is only the POSIX branch. The native module is dead code on Windows.
  2. Add a pnpm patch (the repository already patches native packages this way, e.g.
     `patches/node-pty@*`): rewrite the install script to run `node-gyp` only on non-Windows,
     and give the entry a pure-JS `flock` fallback (warn once, no-op). Linux/macOS keep the
     native build.
  3. Register the patch in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`patchedDependencies` and `allowBuilds`)
     and re-run `pnpm install`.
  Do not install Visual Studio just for this, do not patch upstream, and do not rely on
  `--ignore-scripts` alone.
- **Verification**: `pnpm install` completes; `require('fs-ext')` loads and the flock callback
  path warns once instead of throwing; `dsh web --no-open` boots and answers HTTP 200.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1)
  (`d347e70`): `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/package.json` pins `"fs-ext": "2.1.1"`;
  `src/lease.ts` statically imports `flock` from `fs-ext` and routes Windows through
  `acquireLockHandleWin32`; `src/win32.ts` carries the named-semaphore bindings ·
  single-host field report (Windows 11 without MSVC, 2026-09-07)

---

cards.title: profile boot installs the outbound HTTP(S)/ALL_PROXY policy before the first plugin mounts (`dsh-http-proxy`; `$DSH_HOME/.env` may declare proxy names)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-04 · profile boot installs the outbound HTTP(S)/ALL_PROXY policy before the first plugin mounts (`dsh-http-proxy`; `$DSH_HOME/.env` may declare proxy names)

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: host deployments and profile wrappers behind corporate proxies (or that
  set `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`all_proxy`/`no_proxy`); plugins issuing outbound
  `fetch()`/`globalThis.fetch` requests inside the host tree; launcher scripts and CI that
  previously set `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`.
- **Touchpoints**: none (host network/environment surface; #7 only when a spawned
  subprocess must inherit the policy).
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `runProfile` now calls `installProxyFromEnvironment(...)` on the launcher's
  environment snapshot **before any entry mounts** and disposes the policy at shutdown
  (`apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts` at `dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1`); the launcher gains the new
  runtime dependency `@deepseek-ai/dsh-http-proxy`. Effect: outbound traffic on
  `fetch()`/`globalThis.fetch` (LLM requests, web_search, MCP over HTTP, sandbox SDK
  lanes) honors the proxy environment — lowercase variable names win, `ALL_PROXY` covers
  both schemes, HTTPS falls back to the HTTP proxy; loopback destinations (`localhost`,
  `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0`, v4-mapped) always connect direct; invalid values
  (SOCKS/PAC/unresolvable/unsupported scheme) print a per-variable warning to stderr and
  that scheme falls back to direct — startup is never blocked. Values are resolved from
  the exported environment and then from `$DSH_HOME/.env`; `dsh-app-boot` now lets the
  **home-layer** `.env` declare proxy names (`HOME_LAYER_PROXY_NAMES`), while a
  project/invoking-directory `.env` still refuses them (bootstrap-only rule, pre-existing
  at rc.1). Child processes inherit the policy through `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` on Node
  ≥22.21/24+; code-runtime/workflow workers and OTLP telemetry intentionally stay direct.
  Previously Node's `fetch` ignored the proxy environment, so proxy users saw direct
  connections.
- **Migration recipe**: proxy users export the variables or declare them in
  `$DSH_HOME/.env`, restart the profile, and verify egress (LLM call + web_search) now
  crosses the proxy; drop now-unneeded workarounds that injected custom dispatchers or set
  `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` for profile boots. Plugin authors: do not construct bare undici
  `Agent`/dispatchers for host-tree requests — they bypass the policy; where a custom
  transport is unavoidable, consult the `dsh-http-proxy` README at the target tag (E2B SDK
  integrations use its `proxyRouteFor`). When no proxy should apply, leave the variables
  unset or set `no_proxy` explicitly.
- **Verification**: with a recording local proxy configured, a headless/session request
  appears in the proxy log and a loopback target does not; a bogus proxy value prints the
  `dsh: ...` stderr warning and still connects direct; a proxy declared in `$DSH_HOME/.env`
  is honored, while the same name in the invoking directory's `.env` makes the launch
  refuse with the bootstrap-only message.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `dsh-http-proxy` README (resolution order, loopback, invalid-value behavior, child-env notes)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/util/http-proxy/README.md) · [alpha.1 `profile-boot.ts` (`installProxyFromEnvironment` before first mount)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts) · [alpha.1 `dsh-app-boot` `HOME_LAYER_PROXY_NAMES`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 release notes (HTTP(S)_PROXY support)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1) · [dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1...dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1...dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1)

cards.title: session persistence moves to a lifecycle-held `SessionHandle`; `agentLoop.create()` is async with a per-session lock
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-05 · session persistence moves to a lifecycle-held `SessionHandle`; `agentLoop.create()` is async with a per-session lock

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: host/session-plane integrations that call or implement
  `ctx.sessionPersistence` (`create`/`open`/`stat`/`list`) outside the official bundles,
  out-of-tree persistence providers, code that creates agents through
  `agentLoop.create(...)` (or factories wrapping it) synchronously, and multi-process
  deployments sharing one session store.
- **Touchpoints**: #2
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence` at `dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1` adds a
  handle layer (`packages/session/session-persistence/src/handle.ts`):
  `SessionPersistence.create`/`open` return a `SessionHandle` — an `AsyncDisposable`
  per-session channel with `SessionAccess` `read` or `write`. A `write` handle is the
  session's single mutator (it also reads its own log); a `read` handle never takes
  ownership and works while another handle or process holds `write`. `close()` is the one
  teardown (idempotent; `Symbol.asyncDispose` delegates to it), and every operation on a
  closed handle rejects with `SessionHandleClosedError`. The error surface gains
  ownership errors (`SessionAlreadyOwnedError`, `SessionOwnershipLostError`,
  `SessionReadOnlyError`, `SessionAlreadyExistsError`). `AgentLoop.create(...)` becomes
  `async` (`Promise<Agent>`): creation awaits the stored-session backend
  (`createStoredSession`), appends any unstored suffix, and configured/restore startup
  paths await creation and report configured-startup failures instead of firing and
  forgetting. Release notes state the new session lock: the same session is held by at
  most one process.
- **Migration recipe**: `await` every `agentLoop.create(...)` call site (startup/restore
  paths and tests included); treat the handle as single-owner lifecycle state — acquire it
  through `create`/`open` with the access you need and release it with `close()` /
  `Symbol.asyncDispose`; never cache a `write` handle as a shared service; where another
  process may own the session, handle `SessionAlreadyOwnedError` /
  `SessionOwnershipLostError` explicitly (re-acquire `read` access or coordinate the
  owner — do not blind-retry writes); update fakes/test doubles to the handle shape and
  keep `read` handles working while a writer is active.
- **Verification**: typecheck passes after awaiting `create`; a second `write` open of an
  owned session rejects while a `read` open succeeds; an agent created with `await
  agentLoop.create(...)` runs a full turn and its log appends persist; using a closed
  handle rejects with `SessionHandleClosedError`.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `session-persistence/src/handle.ts` (new)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/session/session-persistence/src/handle.ts) · [alpha.1 `session-persistence/src/errors.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/session/session-persistence/src/errors.ts) · [alpha.1 `agent-loop` (async `create`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts) · [rc.1 `agent-loop` (sync `create`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1/packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 release notes (SessionHandle; async `agentLoop.create()`; session lock)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1)

---

cards.title: Session log format moves to v2 with a released adjacent-generation migration stack (`session-format-catalog`)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-06 · Session log format moves to v2 with a released adjacent-generation migration stack (`session-format-catalog`)

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: integrations that read stored Session logs (raw JSONL archives,
  analysis tooling) or persist session events outside the official read APIs; out-of-tree
  `ctx.sessionPersistence` providers that must store/emit the current format.
- **Touchpoints**: #2
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: at `dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1` the session tree gains
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-catalog` (new package; `src/current.ts` + generated
  tables) as the single source for the currently installed Session format, together with
  a released adjacent-generation migration stack (architecture note
  `2026-08-31-released-session-format-migrations`, present at alpha.1, absent at rc.1).
  Writer-generation semantics matter to readers: the current official writer nests
  `replayState` inside `response` (`version: 2`), while older writer generations layered
  top-level members (`kind`, `version: 1`) into append-only logs; the migrator refuses
  unknown mixed generations fail-closed — measured refusal and resume-cursor cases are
  carded separately in [DSH-0.1.3-A1-01](v0.1.3-alpha.1.md) and [DSH-0.1.3-A1-02](v0.1.3-alpha.1.md).
- **Migration recipe**: prefer the official read surface (a `SessionHandle` `read`, or the
  0.1.2 read API `seq`/`eventAt()`/`snapshotEvents()`) over hand-parsing stored
  artifacts. Tooling that must read raw artifacts should validate against the catalog's
  current/generated shapes and treat unknown or mixed writer generations as migration
  cases rather than parse errors; never hand-write session logs. Providers implementing
  persistence must store the catalog's current format.
- **Verification**: a v2-written session and an older-writer session both read correctly
  through the official APIs; a raw-artifact reader using the catalog accepts current
  artifacts and deterministically reports the refusal cases in DSH-0.1.3-A1-01/A1-02.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `session-format-catalog/src/current.ts` (new)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/session/session-format-catalog/src/current.ts) · [released session-format migrations note (alpha.1)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-31-released-session-format-migrations.md) · [alpha.1 release notes (Session format v2; adjacent-generation migration)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1) · measured refusal/resume cases: DSH-0.1.3-A1-01 / DSH-0.1.3-A1-02 (this file)

cards.title: 0.1.3-alpha.1 rides the unpublished cohort — verify on a source-launched host
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-07 · 0.1.3-alpha.1 rides the unpublished cohort — verify on a source-launched host

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: any deployment expecting to install this version from npm.
- **Touchpoints**: #7
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: the umbrella package 404s on npm (`npm view @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.3-alpha.1` → not found); `latest`/`next` dist-tags stay on 0.1.2-rc.1, so neither `npm i -g` nor registry-pinned verification can reach this version. (By 0.1.5-alpha.1 the npm `alpha` dist-tag resumed; the unpublished state is edge-specific — see the 0.1.5 corridors for the npm-side continuation.)
- **Migration recipe**: use the source-launch host recipe — `git fetch <tag>` → clean → build → `pnpm dsh web`, keeping the global npm install as the rollback.
- **Verification**: `-V` prints the tag version; the web client boots on the source-launched host; plugins load from the unchanged profile (junction installs need no sync).
- **Source**: npm registry probe 2026-09-04 ([@deepseek-ai/dsh versions](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh?activeTab=versions)); real-host source-launched verification the same day.

cards.title: Web composer/upload and tool-card surfaces churn without a client API change
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A1-08 · Web composer/upload and tool-card surfaces churn without a client API change

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: input-area plugins (anything registering into `conversation.input.*`) and tool-card renderers.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: typecheck and builds stay green but the runtime layout neighborhood moved (composer/upload rework, inline `read_image` cards), so slot placement needs a runtime look.
- **Migration recipe**: no code change required by the edge; re-verify slot placement at runtime on the source-launched host (paste image/text, open preview/viewer) before declaring support.
- **Verification**: manual runtime pass on the source-launched host: paste image/text, open preview/viewer, confirm slot placement.
- **Source**: [0.1.3-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1) ("Web 支持上传任意类型的通用文件…", "`read_image` … 在 Web 工具卡中直接渲染图片"); first-hand paste-input verification 2026-09-04.

---

## Release-notes coverage matrix (rc.1 → 0.1.3-alpha.1)

| Release-notes item | Card |
|---|---|
| Session-log writer/migrator behavior on old history | A1-01, A1-02 |
| Profile boot outbound HTTP(S)/ALL_PROXY policy | A1-04 |
| Session persistence lifecycle-held SessionHandle + lock | A1-05 |
| Session log format v2 adjacent-generation migration | A1-06 |
| Unpublished cohort / npm availability | A1-07 |
| Composer/upload rework + inline read_image cards | A1-08 |
| Windows fs-ext/MSVC | A1-03 |

## Six-plugin zero-code validation record

Windows, 2026-09-04/05, source-launched host at `0.1.3-alpha.1` (checkout `d347e70390`, clean rebuild, global npm kept at 0.1.2-rc.1 as rollback):

- Six link-installed Web client plugins crossed the edge with **zero code changes**: five rebuilt with typecheck/build/unit tests green against the 0.1.3-alpha.1 source tree; the vanilla-lib paste/composer plugin verified by a runtime pass (paste into composer, hover preview, click-through viewer) per card A1-08.
- All six released "declare support" patch versions the same day (file-trace v0.3.2 / progress v0.9.13 / whale v0.3.14 / minigames v0.3.15 / input-history v0.1.9 / paste-input v0.1.19); the profile junction installs loaded unchanged.
- Not verified here: host-plane plugins calling session persistence (cards A1-01/02 are recipe-level), the Python SDK, headless/ACP products, and the v0/v1 → v2 migration path on real legacy logs.

## Corridor status

- Eight cards for the 0.1.2 → 0.1.3 boundary. DSH-0.1.3-A1-01/A1-02 are session-log
  plane findings from one deployment's real-history upgrade trial, measured on the
  release-tarball build `0.1.3-alpha.1-9523542`; DSH-0.1.3-A1-03…A1-06 are anchored to the
  official git tags (`dsh-v0.1.2-rc.1` → `dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1`, source-tag diff);
  DSH-0.1.3-A1-07/A1-08 are the unpublished-cohort source-launch recipe and a runtime
  re-verification pass (six-plugin zero-code validation record above). This is
  still not a complete 0.1.3 API sweep.
- A1-01/A1-02 are fail-closed reader behaviors acting on official writer output. Plugin
  sources were negatively scanned (zero `replayState` / `assistant/chunk` writes) as part of
  the attribution, so the corridor edge is between official writer generations, not caused
  by third-party plugins.
- A1-03 is an install-channel finding and a single-host Windows field report; the recipe
  reuses the repository's existing native-dependency patch mechanism and leaves
  Linux/macOS builds untouched.
- A1-04…A1-06 were curated from the tag diff without a real-host cold start (Windows-only
  analysis environment); verify on a real host before treating them as `reviewed`.
- Remaining alpha.1-edge surfaces in the release notes (generic file upload, `read_image`
  inline rendering, Python SDK macOS x64 wheel) carry no plugin-facing API coordinates in
  this analysis — treat them as uncarded rather than proven-unchanged.
- npm note: 0.1.3-alpha.1 was never published to npm; npm upgrades first meet A1-04…A1-06
  at 0.1.3-alpha.2 (see the 0.1.3-alpha.2 corridor card set for that edge's own cards).

cards.title: deployment persona splits into prefix + suffix (`text`/`persona` config keys and `PERSONA_SECTION` removed)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A2-01 · deployment persona splits into prefix + suffix (`text`/`persona` config keys and `PERSONA_SECTION` removed) - **Type**: breaking - **Applies to**: profile compositions and Agent Presets that configure persona rows (`dsh-persona` / `dsh-system-prompt` rows in `cordis.patch.yml` and `agent.cordis.yml`), and any plugin or wrapper that imports `PERSONA_SECTION` (or the `deployment:persona` section name) or the old config keys. - **Touchpoints**: none (composition/config surface); #1 only for source patches that target the old section name or config key. - **Action level**: required-if-hit - **Symptoms**: on 0.1.3-alpha.2, `PERSONA_SECTION`/`deployment:persona` is gone and the persona config keys were renamed: - `dsh-persona` (packages/preset/persona) plugin `Config.text: string` → `Config.prefix: string` + optional `Config.suffix`; re-exported constant `PERSONA_SECTION` → `PERSONA_PREFIX_SECTION` / `PERSONA_SUFFIX_SECTION`; - `dsh-system-prompt` (packages/core/system-prompt) plugin `Config.persona` → `Config.personaPrefix` (+ suffix counterpart), section-order slot `DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA` → `DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_PREFIX` (+ `DEPLOYMENT_PERSONA_SUFFIX`), and section names `deployment:persona` → `deployment:persona-prefix` / `deployment:persona-suffix`; - the shipped base bundle row changed `persona: ''` → `personaPrefix: ''` (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml). A composition that still writes the old keys no longer produces the intended persona text (the text slot it targeted no longer exists), and code importing `PERSONA_SECTION` fails typecheck with a removed-member error. - **Migration recipe**: split the deployment-authored persona into the prefix (rendered before first-party guidance) and an optional suffix (rendered after it): rename `text` → `prefix` (+ `suffix`) in `dsh-persona` rows and `persona` → `personaPrefix` (+ the suffix counterpart) in `dsh-system-prompt` rows; the `complete: true` policy now means "the prefix is the complete system prompt, suppressing the suffix and every other section". Scoped sections and imports must use the two new names. Because the exact suffix config key and shadowing semantics are newer than the release note's one-line summary, re-check the target tag's types (`packages/preset/persona/src/index.ts`, `packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts`) before rewriting rows — do not guess the shape from this card. - **Verification**: `dsh --profile

--dump-config` shows the renamed rows with no validation errors; a cold start renders the prefix before first-party guidance and the suffix after it (inspect the assembled system prompt); the old-key row shape is confirmed gone, not silently ignored. - **Source**: [alpha.2 persona plugin source](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/preset/persona/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 persona plugin source (old `text` key)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/preset/persona/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 system-prompt sections](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 base bundle persona row](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) · [0.1.3-alpha.2 release notes (custom persona config split)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2) ---

cards.title: `SubprocessHandle.pid` removed from the subprocess seam (terminal handle keeps `pid`)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A2-02 · `SubprocessHandle.pid` removed from the subprocess seam (terminal handle keeps `pid`)

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins and integrations that spawn processes through the
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess` seam and read `SubprocessHandle.pid` (process
  supervision, kill-by-pid, pid-based logging or UI). Terminal flows
  (`SubprocessTerminalHandle`) are not affected.
- **Touchpoints**: #7
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `pid: number` is removed from `SubprocessHandle` in
  `packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts`; `SubprocessTerminalHandle.pid` remains.
  Code doing `handle.pid` fails typecheck (removed member) and, if it relied on the
  numeric pid at runtime (signalling, `taskkill`/`kill` by pid, reuse detection), has no
  replacement value. Termination semantics are also re-worded per provider: each
  subprocess provider documents the process range it can observe and its signalling and
  observation limits, with termination and `waitForExit` using the same managed range.
- **Migration recipe**: replace pid-based control with the handle verbs: terminate
  through the handle (the seam's documented escalation, idempotent once the managed tree
  is gone) or the spec's abort signal, and observe exit through `waitForExit` /
  collected streams. If the pid was only shown to users (for example in a process list),
  remove the column or surface provider-reported identity instead; do not re-derive a
  pid from the terminal handle for non-terminal handles — the types no longer promise
  one. Re-check `packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts` and the provider you use
  (`subprocess-local`, `subprocess-e2b`, win32) at the target tag for the exact verbs.
- **Verification**: typecheck passes without `handle.pid`; a spawn → terminate →
  `waitForExit` cycle works for each provider you support; abort-path tests cover both
  normal exit and kill escalation; UI/log surfaces that previously printed the pid show
  the new identity or nothing.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 subprocess types (no `SubprocessHandle.pid`; terminal handle keeps it)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts) · [alpha.1 subprocess types (pid present)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts) · [alpha.2 runner protocol](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/runner-protocol.ts) · [0.1.3-alpha.2 release notes (plain subprocess handle drops pid)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2)

---

cards.title: default file-editing tooling moves to `read`/`write`/`edit`; shipped base no longer mounts the `tool-str-replace-editor` row
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A2-03 · default file-editing tooling moves to `read`/`write`/`edit`; shipped base no longer mounts the `tool-str-replace-editor` row - **Type**: behavior - **Applies to**: profiles and compositions whose mounted tool set came from the shipped bundles (SDK, Headless, ACP first-party flows), and wrappers/presets that referenced the `tool-str-replace-editor` loader row by id or that document "which edit tools ship by default". - **Touchpoints**: none (default composition/tool-surface) - **Action level**: conditional - **Symptoms**: the alpha.2 shipped `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml` removes the `tool-str-replace-editor` loader row (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-str-replace-editor`, `maxOutputChars: 16000`) that alpha.1 still mounted. Release notes state the default file-editing tool adjustment: SDK, Headless and ACP use `read`/`write`/`edit` for file editing by default, while web minimal and sdk-minimal keep their defaults. The str-replace editor package itself still exists at the alpha.2 tag — only the shipped default rows moved. - **Migration recipe**: do not assume which editor tools are mounted — on the target version, dump the actual profile composition (`dsh --profile

--dump-config`) and check the mounted tool rows before writing recipes or docs that name a default editor. Custom compositions that explicitly mount `tool-str-replace-editor` keep working only while the package remains available; verify against the target tag rather than this note. If a productized flow (SDK/Headless/ACP-style) taught users a str-replace workflow, re-run it against the `read`/`write`/`edit` default set and update the flow. - **Verification**: per affected profile, dump-config lists the expected editor rows; a real edit round-trip through each affected profile's default editor tool succeeds; sdk-minimal / web-minimal behavior is unchanged where the release notes promise it. - **Source**: [alpha.2 base bundle patch (row removed)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) · [alpha.1 base bundle patch (row present)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) · [0.1.3-alpha.2 release notes (default tool adjustment)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2) ---

cards.title: CLI launcher exports `runCli()` behind an `import.meta.main` gate (Node runtime floor)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A2-04 · CLI launcher exports `runCli()` behind an `import.meta.main` gate (Node runtime floor)

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: wrappers, CI matrices and headless launchers that invoke `dsh` as a
  subprocess or import the CLI entry (`lib/bin.js`); ordinary Cordis plugins are not
  affected unless they spawn or import the CLI.
- **Touchpoints**: #7
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: in `apps/cli/src/bin.ts` (and the packed `lib/bin.js`) the top-level
  argument parsing + dispatch moved into `export async function runCli()`, invoked only
  under `if (import.meta.main)`. Command-line behavior is unchanged on supported Node
  runtimes, but: (a) importing the entry module no longer has CLI side effects — code
  that imported `lib/bin.js` for its side effects now gets an inert module plus the
  `runCli` export; (b) `import.meta.main` requires a modern Node (`≥24.2` per the
  official v24.2 blog; backported to the 22.18+ line per community tracking) — on older
  Node the main-execution branch never runs, so `dsh` produces no output and exits 0.
  Both alpha.1 and alpha.2 pack no `engines` field, so the floor is not enforced by npm.
- **Migration recipe**: pin the Node runtime your wrappers/CI use to a version that
  supports `import.meta.main` (22.18+ LTS or ≥24.2) and assert it in smoke tests: run
  `dsh --version` and require non-empty output with a non-zero exit on failure — a
  silent empty run on old Node is the failure mode to catch. Programmatic users should
  call `runCli()` explicitly instead of relying on import side effects.
- **Verification**: on the pinned Node, `dsh --version` prints and exits 0; on an old
  Node in the test matrix, the smoke test fails loudly instead of silently passing; a
  `node -e "import('@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js').then(m => console.log(typeof m.runCli))"`
  check prints `function` without running the CLI.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 CLI entry](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/apps/cli/src/bin.ts) · [alpha.1 CLI entry (top-level dispatch)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/apps/cli/src/bin.ts) · [0.1.3-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2) · tag diff `apps/cli/src/bin.ts` (`dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1...dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2`)

---

cards.title: `dsh-llm-pi-ai` bumps `@earendil-works/pi-ai` `^0.84.2` → `^0.85.1` (duplicate-instance trap for direct dependents)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.3-A2-05 · `dsh-llm-pi-ai` bumps `@earendil-works/pi-ai` `^0.84.2` → `^0.85.1` (duplicate-instance trap for direct dependents)

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that depend on `@earendil-works/pi-ai` directly (for example
  to build their own pi-ai-backed adapter), or that import from
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` internals; host deployments pinning a pi-ai version for
  vLLM thinking-budget options.
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging/dependency surface)
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/package.json` moves `@earendil-works/pi-ai` from
  `^0.84.2` to `^0.85.1` (release notes: upgrade to pi-ai 0.85.1 for new-model support;
  the adapter's catalog/config/replay/stream sources changed in the same window). A
  plugin that pins its own older pi-ai copy can end up with two pi-ai instances in one
  tree — the same duplicate-instance trap already carded for the 0.1.2 line
  ([DSH-0.1.2-A1-24](v0.1.2-alpha.1.md)).
- **Migration recipe**: if the plugin depends on `@earendil-works/pi-ai` directly,
  align its range with the host cohort (or prove the override is only serving the older
  peer before keeping it); re-run the adapter's provider/model catalog assertions against
  the new pi-ai; check that identity-sensitive exports (`instanceof`, class tokens)
  resolve to the host's pi-ai copy. Where release notes only promise "new model
  support", verify concrete catalog entries against the alpha.2 tag's
  `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/catalog.ts` rather than assuming a model list from this
  card.
- **Verification**: install/typecheck clean with a single pi-ai copy (lockfile shows one
  resolved instance); a provider round-trip (list providers → model call → replay)
  passes; any duplicate-instance symptoms (`instanceof` failures, two copies in the
  dependency tree) are gone.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 llm-pi-ai package.json (`^0.85.1`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/package.json) · [alpha.1 llm-pi-ai package.json (`^0.84.2`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/package.json) · [0.1.3-alpha.2 release notes (pi-ai 0.85.1)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2) · duplicate-instance precedent [DSH-0.1.2-A1-24](v0.1.2-alpha.1.md)

---

## Corridor verification record

Windows, 2026-09-05, host and checkout both at the edge: global npm
`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.3-alpha.2` (Node v24.14.1, `dsh --version` prints — card 04's
smoke check), checkout pinned to `dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2` (`82a5fd61a7`, rebuilt after
`pnpm run clean`), `dsh web` served from the global install.

- The same six-plugin client-UI fleet from the [alpha.1 record](v0.1.3-alpha.1.md)
  crossed this edge with **zero code changes**: all six re-ran `pnpm install` /
  typecheck / build / unit tests green against the 0.1.3-alpha.2 source tree, then
  released "declare support" versions the same day (file-trace v0.3.6 / progress
  v0.9.14 / whale v0.3.15 / minigames v0.3.16 / input-history v0.1.10 / paste-input
  v0.1.21), each tag verified by SHA on all three push mirrors before the version
  declaration was published.
- None of the five cards fired on a pure client-UI fleet — expected, since the cards'
  surfaces are persona composition, subprocess handles, tool defaults, the CLI launcher,
  and packaging. Card 05 (pi-ai bump) is the only adjacent one; the fleet carries no
  direct `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, so the duplicate-instance check was not
  exercised.
- Toolchain field notes re-confirmed on this edge: switching source-host tags without
  `pnpm run clean` resurfaces the stale-`lib/types` `MISSING_EXPORT` tsdown trap first
  recorded in the alpha.1 corridor (card 03); lightweight release tags expose the commit
  sha directly through the `git/refs/tags/<tag>` API (no `^{}` peel); and fetching a
  single tag into a shallow clone needs the explicit refspec
  `git fetch <url> 'refs/tags/<tag>:refs/tags/<tag>'` — `fetch <url> tag <tag>
  --no-tags` can fail pathspec matching on shallow clones.
- Not verified here: persona compositions (card 01), subprocess `pid` consumers
  (card 02), profiles relying on the shipped `tool-str-replace-editor` default row
  (card 03), and CLI launches on pre-`import.meta.main` Node runtimes (card 04).

---

## Corridor status

- First card set for the `dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.1 → dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2` edge, curated from
  the pinned tag diff (source-tag diff plus the published npm tarball
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.3-alpha.2`); status `draft` — the card surfaces themselves
  remain recipe-level unverified. Amended 2026-09-05: a real-host six-plugin client-UI
  crossing is recorded in the [verification record](#corridor-verification-record); it
  exercises install/typecheck/test on the edge, not the carded host-plane surfaces.
- Web-client and product changes announced in the alpha.2 notes (open-in-app entry,
  queued subagent message editing/steer UI, PTC command expansion, disconnect
  auto-recovery, chat autoscroll, settings styling, standalone feedback submission,
  Windows Python-SDK runtime crash fix, process-cleanup improvements) are not carded:
  the notes describe UI/UX and fixes without plugin-facing API changes. Host-visible
  behavioral items from the same notes that could not be pinned to source coordinates in
  this window (for example the base telemetry comment rewrite) are likewise not carded —
  treat them as uncarded rather than proven-unchanged, per the corridor rules.
- npm-visible upgrades from `0.1.2-rc.1` must fold the alpha.1 edge
  ([v0.1.3-alpha.1.md](v0.1.3-alpha.1.md) session-log cards, plus the not-yet-carded
  alpha.1 items listed in the header note above).

*Changes to host UI, performance, or non-carded surfaces do not prove the absence of API
or behavior impact. When a real plugin is affected, add a primary source and a
reproducible verification record.*

cards.title: Session log format moves to V3 (`session-format-v2-to-v3`); `EpochHeader.system` removed and upgraded sessions are not downgrade-readable
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-01 · Session log format moves to V3 (`session-format-v2-to-v3`); `EpochHeader.system` removed and upgraded sessions are not downgrade-readable

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: integrations that read stored Session logs (raw JSONL archives,
  analysis/export tooling), out-of-tree `ctx.sessionPersistence` providers, custom
  `session-format` stages, and any plugin that hand-parses session artifacts.
- **Touchpoints**: #2, #4
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` becomes `3`
  (`packages/core/session/src/types.ts`); the new package
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-format-v2-to-v3` (absent at `0.1.3-alpha.2`) is the single
  specification for this adjacent edge, and the catalog gains
  `currentVersion: 3` / `currentEncoder: releasedV3SessionFormatCodec` plus the
  `sessionFormatV2ToV3` migration. Restoring a supported released V2 Session produces a V3
  log without changing historical request meaning: system prompts are promoted into
  messages, local event references are remapped, PTC/preset vocabulary is translated, and
  envelopes are canonicalized. The original artifact is preserved, but an upgraded Session
  **cannot be read by older builds**. Related contract changes land in the same window:
  `EpochHeader.system` is removed (a `request/header` carrying `header.system` — even an
  empty string — now throws `must omit header.system; use system/message`), the V3 reader
  requires `surfaceOp` on the four surface event families, and `session-format`'s
  `sourceCut` becomes optional (validated at `finish()`).
- **Migration recipe**: read through the official surface (`SessionHandle` `read`, or
  `seq`/`eventAt()`/`snapshotEvents()`) instead of parsing artifacts by hand. Custom log
  readers must follow the V2→V3 specification: a synthetic empty `system/message` head is
  appended after the first `step/start` (sessions with no steps get no head), `'code'`
  preset references in `header.agentPreset` and `agent-preset/selected` become `'ptc'`
  (never touching `run_code`'s `code` argument or `:code:` ids), and reference remapping
  covers `sourceEventSeqs[]`, `surfaceOp.start/end`, `command/done.sourceEventSeq`,
  `compaction.*` ranges and `session/title*.messageSeqs[]`. Keep a `0.1.3-alpha.2`
  installation if old logs must still be read — downgrade reading is not supported.
  Providers implementing persistence must store the catalog's current format.
- **Verification**: a V2 session with real history restores on `0.1.5-alpha.1`; the
  original artifact remains on disk; the restored session reads correctly through the
  official APIs; a `request/header` with `system` is rejected; opening the upgraded session
  with an older build is refused. The package's own
  `packages/session/session-format-v2-to-v3/tests/*` and
  `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/tests/{v2-ptc-migration,v2-system-migration,migration-refusal,v3-event-admission}.spec.ts`
  are the behavior baseline.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `session-format-v2-to-v3` README (single specification)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/session/session-format-v2-to-v3/README.md) · [alpha.1 `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION = 3` and `EpochHeader`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/types.ts) · [alpha.1 `session-format-catalog/src/generated.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/session/session-format-catalog/src/generated.ts) · [alpha.1 `session-persistence-jsonl/src/format.ts` (V3 admission)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/format.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (Session format V3; no downgrade read)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1) · earlier format edges: [v0.1.3-alpha.1.md](v0.1.3-alpha.1.md)

---

cards.title: `ctx.agent` removed (runtime trap) — pass the Agent explicitly and declare `parentAgent`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-02 · `ctx.agent` removed (runtime trap) — pass the Agent explicitly and declare `parentAgent` - **Type**: breaking - **Applies to**: plugins/services that read `ctx.agent` or `agent.ctx.agent`, implement `AgentSetup`, or create/resume agents relying on implicit ownership. - **Touchpoints**: #3 - **Action level**: required-if-hit - **Symptoms**: `AgentRegistry` no longer registers a `ctx.accessor('agent', …)` and `ReactLoopAgent` no longer extends its context with `{ agent: this }` (`packages/core/agent/src/index.ts`, `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts`), and the `Context` module augmentation drops `agent?: Agent`. Reading `ctx.agent` now **throws at runtime** — cordis's proxy trap raises `cannot get property "agent" without inject` (`vendor/cordis/src/reflect.ts`) — not `undefined`. `AgentSetup` gains an explicit second parameter: `(agentCtx: Context, agent: Agent) => AgentSetupCommit | Promise<…> | void`, and `CreateAgentOptions` / `ResumeAgentOptions` gain `parentAgent?: Agent` ("live parent Agent for runtime ownership; omit for a root Agent"). `AgentRegistry.register()` now enters with an explicit `undefined` root instead of `ctx.agent`, which is the ownership fix: continuable subagents are no longer treated as root sessions participating in scheduled work. - **Migration recipe**: delete every `ctx.agent` / `agentCtx.agent` read. Choose one of: (a) the `AgentSetup` second parameter `(agentCtx, agent)`; (b) `ctx.agents.currentInitiator()` where an optional shape is acceptable; or (c) pass the Agent explicitly into your service methods (the new API style, e.g. `workspaceFiles.read(agent, …)`, `goals.get(agent)`). Update `AgentSetup` implementations to the two-parameter signature, and pass `parentAgent` explicitly when creating/resuming child agents (omit for roots) — do not infer root-vs-child from context nesting. - **Verification**: `rg "ctx\.agent|agentCtx\.agent"` returns nothing in your plugin; typecheck passes with the new `AgentSetup`; `dsh --profile

--dump-config` and a real boot work; create/resume with and without `parentAgent` shows the expected ownership (continuable subagents are not scheduled as roots). - **Source**: [alpha.1 `core/agent/src/index.ts` (no accessor; new `AgentSetup`, `parentAgent`, explicit root)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/agent/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `core/agent/src/index.ts` (augmentation and accessor present)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/core/agent/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 `agent-loop/src/agent.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts) · [alpha.1 cordis inject trap](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/vendor/cordis/src/reflect.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (plugin Agent API change)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1) ---

cards.title: `Inbox` becomes a type interface reachable as `agent.inbox`; the runtime class and public `hasPending`/`claim` are gone from the type surface
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-03 · `Inbox` becomes a type interface reachable as `agent.inbox`; the runtime class and public `hasPending`/`claim` are gone from the type surface

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that imported or constructed the `Inbox` runtime class from
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent`, or that relied on `hasPending`/`claim` as public queue APIs.
- **Touchpoints**: #2, #3
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `packages/core/agent/src/inbox.ts` is deleted at `0.1.5-alpha.1` and the
  package barrel no longer re-exports it, so `import { Inbox } from
  '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'` no longer has a runtime export; `hasPending` and `claim` are
  removed from the public `Inbox` interface (`packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts`
  now declares only `nextTurn`/`nextStep`/`clear`/`append`/`prepend`/`replace`/`remove`/
  `splice`). Note the failure mode is **type-level, not a runtime crash**: the driver
  implementation (`ReactLoopInbox` in `packages/core/agent-loop/src/inbox.ts`) still has
  those methods at runtime. In the same window the queue becomes projection-driven: a new
  session-projection key `inbox` (`inboxProjectionDefinition`, `stateVersion: 1`,
  consuming `agent/inbox/spliced`) is registered by the driver, and the Web queue frame is
  broadcast from `ctx.sessionProjections.onChanged` when `key === 'inbox'` instead of
  listening to `session/event` — so the projection exists only while an agent loop is
  active.
- **Migration recipe**: treat `Inbox` as a type only; access pending messages through the
  typed `agent.inbox` interface and drop imports from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent/inbox`.
  Compute pending state yourself (`nextTurn.length + nextStep.length > 0`) instead of
  calling `hasPending`, and never call `claim` — claiming is a driver-owned turn-boundary
  operation. Plugins that want the queue as data can read
  `ctx.sessionProjections.stateOf(session, 'inbox')` (wire shape `InboxWireState`); note
  the projection is absent when no agent loop is active. Test doubles can use
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop-testkit` (`createInboxStub()` / `unsupportedInbox()`).
- **Verification**: typecheck passes with no `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent/inbox` imports and no
  `hasPending`/`claim` calls; queueing a message through `agent.inbox` delivers it at the
  next-turn/next-step boundary; a client built on the `inbox` projection updates after the
  splice commits (not on the raw event) and behaves correctly when no loop is active.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `agent-loop/src/inbox.ts` (driver-owned projection, `ReactLoopInbox`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/agent-loop/src/inbox.ts) · [alpha.2 `core/agent/src/inbox.ts` (class still present)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/core/agent/src/inbox.ts) · [alpha.1 `core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts` (public Inbox interface)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts) · [alpha.1 `session-controller/src/control.ts` (queue from projection)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/session-controller/src/control.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (Inbox API change)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

---

cards.title: session event payload validation tightens (`surfaceOp` `startSeq`/`endSeq`, `SurfaceIntent` typing, `tool/result` error consistency, empty header fields, opaque wire fields)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-04 · session event payload validation tightens (`surfaceOp` `startSeq`/`endSeq`, `SurfaceIntent` typing, `tool/result` error consistency, empty header fields, opaque wire fields)

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that append or seed session events (compaction, pruning,
  replacement, custom tool/result writers), and Web Client integrations that parse
  session-wire events.
- **Touchpoints**: #2, #6
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: five validation changes land together in
  `packages/core/session/src/{types.ts,surface.ts,request-header.ts}` and
  `packages/api/session-controller/src/{types.ts,client/session-wire-event.ts}`:
  (1) `SurfaceOp` replace uses `startSeq`/`endSeq` instead of `start`/`end` — `isReplaceOp`
  only accepts the new keys, so old payloads fail validation;
  (2) surface event types move to `SurfaceIntent<K>` with a required `surfaceOp`, while
  log-only events declare `surfaceOp?: never; sourceEventSeqs?: never` — passing a
  `surfaceOp` to a log-only event is now a compile-time error;
  (3) a `tool/result` carrying `data.error` must have
  `message.content[0].isError === true`, otherwise append/seed/adopt throws (contradictory
  results are no longer silently accepted);
  (4) `request/header` must omit empty `tools: []` and `adapterDefaults: {}` ("must omit
  empty tools" / "must omit empty adapterDefaults"), enforced by `canonicalHeader()`;
  (5) `SessionWireEvent.sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` are typed as opaque `JsonValue` and a
  new client-side `assertSessionWireEvent()` validates every event in snapshot,
  notification and history lanes — unknown fields throw, and clients that hard-coded
  `surfaceOp.start/end` break.
- **Migration recipe**: rewrite replace ops to `{ op: 'replace', startSeq, endSeq }` and
  keep `sourceEventSeqs` non-empty, unique and strictly earlier than the new event. Only
  `system/message` may rewrite the protected node 0, and only when the replacement covers
  that exact node. Emit system prompts as `system/message` (never as `header.system`),
  clear empty arrays/objects from headers, and keep `tool/result.error` consistent with
  `content[0].isError: true`. On the wire, narrow `JsonValue` per event type yourself —
  the host-side `validateSessionEventData`/`validateSurfaceMetadata` are not importable
  from the client.
- **Verification**: appending a replace op with `start`/`end` is rejected; the same op with
  `startSeq`/`endSeq` succeeds; a `tool/result` with `error` and `isError: false` is
  rejected; a header with `tools: []` is rejected; a client parsing wire events with the
  new opaque fields handles unknown-field errors deterministically.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `core/session/src/surface.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/surface.ts) · [alpha.1 `core/session/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/types.ts) · [alpha.1 `session-controller/src/client/session-wire-event.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/session-controller/src/client/session-wire-event.ts) · [alpha.1 `core/session/src/request-header.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/request-header.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

---

cards.title: PTC vocabulary rename (`tool/ptc-dispatch`, plugin `tools-ptc`, `<parent>:ptc:<n>`)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-05 · PTC vocabulary rename (`tool/ptc-dispatch`, plugin `tools-ptc`, `<parent>:ptc:<n>`)

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: log readers, UI filters and analytics that select PTC/code-mode events,
  and any plugin that inspects `subCallId` or the `source.plugin` marker.
- **Touchpoints**: #2, #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the session event names `tool/code-dispatch` and
  `tool/code-dispatch-start` become `tool/ptc-dispatch` and `tool/ptc-dispatch-start`
  (`packages/core/session/src/known-event-types.ts`,
  `packages/core/tools/src/types.ts`), the emitting plugin marker
  `source.plugin: 'tools-code-mode'` becomes `'tools-ptc'` in `user/message`,
  inbox-inserted messages and `title-llm-request`, and new sub-call ids use the
  `<parent>:ptc:<n>` prefix (`packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts`). Historical ids still
  contain `:code:`, so prefix parsing must not assume one generation.
- **Migration recipe**: update event filters, dashboards and invariants to the new names
  and the new plugin marker; parse sub-call ids by suffix/generation rather than a fixed
  `:code:`/`:ptc:` prefix. Where old logs are archived, normalize both generations at read
  time (the V2→V3 migration translates the vocabulary for supported history, but raw
  archives read outside the migration still carry the old names).
- **Verification**: a PTC round-trip produces `tool/ptc-dispatch` events with
  `source.plugin: 'tools-ptc'` and `<parent>:ptc:<n>` ids; a reader handles both old and
  new generations without dropping rows.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `core/session/src/known-event-types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/known-event-types.ts) · [alpha.1 `core/tools/src/types.ts` (renamed event keys)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/tools/src/types.ts) · [alpha.1 `core/tools/src/ptc.ts` (plugin marker and sub-call id)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (PTC/preset vocabulary migration)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: `token-meter` drops `estimateSystemTokens`/`estimateHeader`; `contextBreakdown` projection stateVersion 2 → 4
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-06 · `token-meter` drops `estimateSystemTokens`/`estimateHeader`; `contextBreakdown` projection stateVersion 2 → 4

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that compute context/token usage from the `token-meter` exports
  or that persist/read the `contextBreakdown` projection.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #4
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `packages/llm/token-meter/src/estimate.ts` no longer exports
  `estimateSystemTokens(header)` or `estimateHeader(header)`; `estimateSystemMessage(message)`
  is the replacement (system prompts are priced as messages now).
  `packages/llm/token-meter/src/breakdown-projection.ts` moves the
  `contextBreakdown` projection to `stateVersion: 4` with a new state shape
  (`{nodes[], breakdown{}}` instead of flat counters), so old checkpoint rows are rejected
  as incompatible (the projection registry throws when the same key carries a different
  stateVersion).
- **Migration recipe**: replace removed exports with `estimateSystemMessage(message)`, or
  price system prompts from the `system/message` surface node; do not write a
  compatibility shim for the projection — let it rebuild, and re-check the target tag's
  `estimate.ts` / `breakdown-projection.ts` for the current shapes before persisting your
  own copies.
- **Verification**: typecheck passes with no `estimateHeader`/`estimateSystemTokens`
  imports; token/context numbers for a session with a system prompt match a manual
  surface-node calculation; a pre-upgrade checkpoint row for `contextBreakdown` is
  discarded/rebuilt rather than crashing the boot.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `token-meter/src/estimate.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/llm/token-meter/src/estimate.ts) · [alpha.2 `token-meter/src/estimate.ts` (old exports)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/llm/token-meter/src/estimate.ts) · [alpha.1 `token-meter/src/breakdown-projection.ts` (stateVersion 4)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/llm/token-meter/src/breakdown-projection.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: system prompts move into message history (`system/message`), enabling dynamic prompt updates without KV-cache invalidation
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-07 · system prompts move into message history (`system/message`), enabling dynamic prompt updates without KV-cache invalidation

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that contribute system-prompt sections, adapters that declare
  prompt handling, and clients that render or diff the prompt.
- **Touchpoints**: #2, #3
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: a new `system/message` event
  (`{ turn; step; message: SystemMessage }`) carries the system prompt as a surface node;
  the first prompt occupies node 0 and is appended even when empty. A capable route
  (`systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'`) appends changed **non-empty** prompts after the
  cached history within a continuous request sequence, so the KV cache stays valid; an
  incapable route or a new sequence normalizes the latest text onto node 0. Node 0 is
  protected: a replace covering it must itself be a `system/message` and cover exactly that
  node. `request/context` gains `systemPromptUpdate?` (appended only when
  provider/model/contextWindow/mode change), and prepared capability — not the previous
  snapshot — decides admission. New types: `SystemMessage`,
  `createSystemMessage(text, plugin)` (`''` → `content: []`), `SystemPromptUpdate =
  'in-history'`, `LlmResolvedModelInfo.systemPromptUpdate?`,
  `PreparedLlmCall.systemPromptUpdate?`. `dsh-llm-deepseek`'s catalog accepts
  `systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'`, and the pi-ai adapter's `splitSystemPrompt()`
  prefers `options.system`, otherwise the first system history message, folding the rest
  into user messages to preserve order. Two related narrowing/removal changes:
  `LlmCallConfig.system` **stays** but is re-documented for one-shot callers only —
  adapters map it to the provider's system slot ahead of `messages`, and loop-built
  requests leave it `undefined`; and `compaction-basic`'s `SummarizationInput.system` is
  **removed** — the summarization input's `messages` now begin with the derived system
  head (`packages/compaction/compaction-basic/src/{region,summarizer}.ts`), which is
  breaking for compaction plugin authors that constructed that input.
- **Migration recipe**: stop reading/writing `header.system`; emit and read
  `system/message` nodes. If your adapter can host in-history prompts, declare
  `systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'` in the model catalog (the only accepted value) and
  verify the request-reconstruction tests; otherwise the host falls back to node-0
  normalization, which is correct but rewrites the prompt. Prompt-contributing plugins do
  not need to change their section registration, but they should re-run prompt-projection
  tests because admission now depends on the prepared capability.
- **Verification**: a session with a system prompt shows a `system/message` node at 0; a
  prompt change mid-sequence appends rather than rewriting when the route is capable, and
  the cached prefix is preserved; an empty render clears active system nodes; a replace
  that targets node 0 without `system/message` is rejected.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `agent-loop/src/runtime-context.ts` (`SystemPromptProjection`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/core/agent-loop/src/runtime-context.ts) · [alpha.1 `llm/src/message.ts` (`SystemMessage`, `createSystemMessage`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm/src/message.ts) · [alpha.1 `llm-deepseek/src/index.ts` (`systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 `llm-pi-ai/src/context.ts` (`splitSystemPrompt`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/context.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (dynamic system prompt without KV-cache invalidation)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: forwarded scoped Remote events must carry their Agent directly (`TypertRemoteEventContext.agentId`)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-08 · forwarded scoped Remote events must carry their Agent directly (`TypertRemoteEventContext.agentId`)

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that forward scoped Remote events or implement custom Remote
  gateways/transports.
- **Touchpoints**: #3
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS` scoped entries now require
  `request.agent` to be present **and equal to the event carrier's Agent**, otherwise the
  forward throws `must carry its Agent directly`
  (`packages/api/remotes/src/index.ts`). `TypertRemoteEventContext` gains `agentId: string`
  and the gateway reads `source.context.agentId` instead of calling
  `typert.contexts.identifyHost()` (`packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts`,
  `packages/api/gateway/src/types.ts`).
- **Migration recipe**: attach the owning Agent to the forwarded request explicitly; do
  not rely on host identification to infer it. Update gateway/transport fakes to populate
  `agentId`, and re-run the forwarded-event waterfall tests against the new carrier check.
- **Verification**: a scoped forward with the correct Agent succeeds; forwarding without
  an Agent, or with a different Agent, throws `must carry its Agent directly`; gateway
  tests read `agentId` from the context.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `api/remotes/src/index.ts` (carrier check)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/remotes/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 `api/gateway/src/index.ts` (`agentId`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 `api/gateway/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/gateway/src/types.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: the CLI rejects `--profile desktop` (Electron-managed profile)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-09 · the CLI rejects `--profile desktop` (Electron-managed profile)

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: wrappers, CI scripts and operators who pass `desktop` (any casing) as a
  profile name to `dsh`.
- **Touchpoints**: #1
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `apps/cli/src/args.ts` adds `rejectElectronProfile()`: `desktop`
  (case-insensitive) is reserved for the Electron application and boot, `--dump-config`
  and `plugin` paths all exit 1 with
  `error: profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`
  (`apps/cli/tests/args.spec.ts` covers `desktop`/`Desktop`/`DESKTOP`). The desktop apps
  load their own profile directory through the new `loadProfileDirectory()` instead.
- **Migration recipe**: rename any local profile that used the `desktop` name, and start
  custom profiles from a shipped template with
  `dsh --profile <name> --from-default-profile <web|headless|sdk|sdk-minimal|acp>`
  (see [DSH-0.1.5-A1-10](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md)). Do not script around the rejection — it is
  intentional.
- **Verification**: `dsh --profile desktop`, `dsh --profile Desktop --dump-config` and
  `dsh plugin --profile DESKTOP …` all exit 1 with the message; a renamed profile starts
  normally.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `apps/cli/src/args.ts` (`rejectElectronProfile`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/apps/cli/src/args.ts) · [alpha.1 `apps/cli/tests/args.spec.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/apps/cli/tests/args.spec.ts) · [alpha.1 `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts` (`loadProfileDirectory`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: `--from-default-profile` initializes custom profiles; `loadProfileDirectory()` loads an app-owned profile directory
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-10 · `--from-default-profile` initializes custom profiles; `loadProfileDirectory()` loads an app-owned profile directory

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: profile authors and wrappers that ship or template profiles.
- **Touchpoints**: #1, #4
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: a new flag
  `--from-default-profile <web|headless|sdk|sdk-minimal|acp>` initializes a **new,
  non-built-in** profile at the target name: it copies the template's bundle list and
  `patchReload`, leaves dependencies and user patches empty, does not inherit a local
  profile with the same name, and claims the target directory exclusively (EEXIST
  refuses). Unknown templates or built-in names fail before creation; initialization
  commits first, so a later boot failure still leaves the profile on disk; success prints
  nothing extra. `--dump-config`/`--dump-default-config` accept the flag too
  (initialize, print, do not start). `dsh-app-boot` also exports
  `loadProfileDirectory(binName, dir, installAnchor, { userLayer? })`, which loads an
  application-owned, already-initialized profile directory without the `$DSH_HOME` lookup
  (`loadProfile` now delegates to it).
- **Migration recipe**: use the flag instead of hand-copying a profile; document that
  dependencies/patches start empty and that the directory must not already exist. Wrappers
  embedding the host (like the desktop app) can call `loadProfileDirectory()` to load a
  bundled profile; do not point it at a `$DSH_HOME` name.
- **Verification**: `dsh --profile my-web --from-default-profile web` creates the profile
  and starts; running it again refuses with EEXIST; an unknown template or a built-in name
  fails before writing; `--dump-config` with the flag prints without starting.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `apps/cli/reference/README.md` (flag behavior)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/apps/cli/reference/README.md) · [alpha.1 `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts` (`initializeProfileFromDefault`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts) · [alpha.1 `boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts` (`loadProfileDirectory`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: new file surface — `workspaceFiles` Remote, `ctx.fs.readByteRange()`, and the `/api/file` media endpoint (privacy note)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-11 · new file surface — `workspaceFiles` Remote, `ctx.fs.readByteRange()`, and the `/api/file` media endpoint (privacy note)

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that read workspace files, Host plugins needing
  ranged reads, and deployments exposing the web host to untrusted networks.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #4, #6
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: a new package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-files` provides the
  `workspaceFiles` Remote namespace (`read`/`readBytes`/`stat`/`list`/`changes`, the last
  a stream) with four gates: lstat refuses symlinks, `ctx.fs.contains(root, target)` blocks
  `..` escapes, page/window and entry limits apply, and a UTF-8 text gate rejects binary.
  Error codes: `workspace-file/{not-found,outside-workspace,too-large,not-text,not-regular-file,not-directory}`.
  Config keys: `maxBytes` (default 2 MiB), `maxLines` (5000) and `maxEntries` (2000);
  over-limit reads **fail** rather than truncate (listings may report `truncated`). A new
  file-address vocabulary ships alongside it in
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-util-workspace-path` (`FileAddress`, `fileAddressFor(sessionId, cwd,
  path)`, `parseFileAddress()`, `sessionFileAddress()`, `absoluteFileAddress()`) — build
  and parse addresses instead of concatenating paths across planes.
  `ctx.fs` gains `readByteRange(target, { offset, length }, signal?)` for windowed reads
  that neither buffer the whole file nor refuse binary — note this is an **abstract
  `FileSystem` method**: every backend (including out-of-tree implementations) must
  implement it (`fs-local` and `fs-e2b` already do), so custom FileSystem providers have a
  breaking addition to satisfy. A new authenticated endpoint
  `GET/HEAD /api/file?path=<absolute path>` (in `session-controller/src/media-references.ts`)
  serves local images for chat messages, with `Cache-Control: private, no-store`,
  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'`
  and an image byte cap; FsError codes map to 404/403/413/499.
  **Privacy note**: `/api/file` is authorized only by the connection service and the code
  comment states paths and MIME types do not restrict access — any absolute path readable
  by the host process can be served, including files outside registered workspaces (by
  design, for screenshots). Do not expose the web host to untrusted networks, and review
  it when auditing data egress.
- **Migration recipe**: use `workspaceFiles` instead of hand-rolled file routes; use
  `readByteRange` for large or binary files instead of reading whole files; if you serve
  media yourself, mirror the security headers and byte cap. When auditing privacy,
  treat `/api/file` as a read-any-path endpoint.
- **Verification**: `workspaceFiles.read` on a symlink, a `..` path, an oversized file and
  a binary file returns the documented error codes; `readByteRange` returns the requested
  window without buffering the file; `/api/file` returns an image with the security
  headers and rejects non-images with the mapped status.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `api/workspace-files/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/workspace-files/README.md) · [alpha.1 `session-controller/src/media-references.ts` (`/api/file`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/session-controller/src/media-references.ts) · [alpha.1 `extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts` (`readByteRange`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (local image display fix)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: `goal/activation-changed` event joins the Remote forward whitelist; `goals.get` becomes a Remote
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-12 · `goal/activation-changed` event joins the Remote forward whitelist; `goals.get` becomes a Remote

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: Host/Web Client plugins that observe goal activation or read goals over
  Remote.
- **Touchpoints**: #2, #3
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: `packages/api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts` adds
  `{ event: 'goal/activation-changed', mode: 'emit' }` (payload `{sessionId, goal?:
  {id, revision, activation}}`, emitted only when the activation state actually changes),
  so the event now crosses the
  gateway; `goals.get` is declared `@Remote('get')` and the tool-cordis catalog gains
  `GoalActivationChanged` plus the new `goals.get` signature. In the same window
`tool-goal` refuses a model-initiated resume of a paused goal
(`HarnessError('the model cannot resume a paused goal; the user must resume it',
'GOAL_TOOL_RESUME_PAUSED')`), so automations that resumed goals on the model's behalf now
get that error instead.
- **Migration recipe**: subscribe to `goal/activation-changed` instead of polling goal
  state where possible; call `goals.get(agent)` with the explicit Agent (see
  [DSH-0.1.5-A1-02](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md)); re-check the catalog at the target tag for the
  exact event payload.
- **Verification**: activating/pausing a goal emits the event through the Remote lane; a
  Remote client receives it and `goals.get` returns the expected snapshot.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts) · [alpha.1 `extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (goal resume authorization)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: packaging: `fs-ext` replaced by `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system`, `native/landlock-run` → `native/system`, desktop apps added
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-13 · packaging: `fs-ext` replaced by `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system`, `native/landlock-run` → `native/system`, desktop apps added

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugin packaging, install pipelines and CI matrices that build native
  dependencies or reference the native workspace layout.
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging surface); #4 for the persistence lock semantics.
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl` drops `fs-ext`/`@types/fs-ext`
  and depends on `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system`, calling
  `tryLockExclusive(handle.fd)` from `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system/flock` instead of the
  `flock(fd, 'exnb')` wrapper (`src/lease.ts`); `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `allowBuilds` no
  longer lists `fs-ext`, and the webworker-runtime's `fs-ext` shim is deleted. The native
  package `native/landlock-run` is renamed to `native/system` and gains darwin-arm64 /
  darwin-x64 platform packages (previously linux only), with the release workflow renamed
  to `node-addon-system-release.yml`. Two new apps (`apps/desktop`, `apps/desktop-host`)
  add desktop build/package scripts to the root manifest: the desktop host opens **no
  listening port**, serving the renderer over a versioned `dsh-app://` framed pipe
  (protocol version 3, request/response on FDs 3/4, control IPC on FD 5), owns
  `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`, resolves plugins from a fixed Desktop registry, and its
  `desktop.cordis.patch.yml` disables the web rows
  (`webserver`/`web-startup`/`web-runtime`/`client-hmr`/`open-in-app`/`ui-open-in-app`/
  `directory-picker`) while inserting the native pickers. `native/system` supports
  darwin-x64/arm64 (system addon only) plus the Linux Landlock launcher, targets Node-API
  v8, and its CI covers Node 20/22/24/26. `engines` and the vendored
  `@deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.2` are unchanged on both tags.
- **Migration recipe**: if your install pipeline pinned or rebuilt `fs-ext`, drop it and
  build/install `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system` instead (prebuilt platform packages now
  cover macOS and Linux); update CI paths that referenced `native/landlock-run`; treat
  the desktop apps as product-side and do not depend on their internals.
- **Verification**: a clean install on macOS/Linux no longer needs node-gyp for `fs-ext`;
  session persistence still takes an exclusive lock (two writers on one session fail as
  before); CI resolves `native/system` paths.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `session-persistence-jsonl/package.json` (no `fs-ext`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/package.json) · [alpha.1 `session-persistence-jsonl/src/lease.ts` (`tryLockExclusive`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/lease.ts) · [alpha.1 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`allowBuilds`, native paths)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/pnpm-workspace.yaml) · [alpha.1 root `package.json` (desktop scripts)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/package.json) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (macOS/Linux fs-ext build fix)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: Web Client: the `details` panel becomes `rightbar` — slot rename, `openDetails`/`closeDetails` replaced, tool-detail slot and `selectedCallId` removed, layout state/constants rewritten
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-14 · Web Client: the `details` panel becomes `rightbar` — slot rename, `openDetails`/`closeDetails` replaced, tool-detail slot and `selectedCallId` removed, layout state/constants rewritten

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that registered into the `details` slot or the
  `conversation.details.tool` slot, called `ctx.layout.openDetails()/closeDetails()`,
  imported layout constants/state types, or read `selectedCallId` / `data-selected`.
- **Touchpoints**: #5; #6 for DOM/CSS selectors that relied on the removed attributes.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the right column seat is renamed `details` → `rightbar`
  (`packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts`: `'rightbar': { kind: 'single'; scope:
  'session'; owner: RightbarOwnerProps }`, with `RightbarOwnerProps {width, viewportWidth,
  canShow}`), and the client slot catalog swaps the key. Panel actions change:
  `ctx.layout.openDetails()`/`closeDetails()` → `openRightbar(track, fullscreen)` /
  `closeRightbar()` (`src/client/service.ts`). The tool-detail seat
  `conversation.details.tool` is removed together with `DetailsToolOwnerProps`,
  `DetailsSlotProps`, `DetailsInjected`, `ToolDetailsProps`, `SelectionTarget`,
  `ChatStoreState.selection` and `openDetails`; `ui-chat`'s `DetailsPanel.tsx` and
  `ui-tool`'s `ToolDetails.tsx` are deleted. `ChatNodeOwnerProps.selectedCallId` and
  `ToolTreeProps.selectedCallId` are gone (tool rows no longer emit `data-selected`).
  `ui-layout` geometry/state are rewritten: `CENTER_MIN` 640 → 400, the
  `DETAILS_MIN/MAX/DEFAULT` triple becomes `RIGHTBAR_MIN=300`,
  `RIGHTBAR_MAX_RATIO=0.7`, `RIGHTBAR_DEFAULT_RATIO=0.45`, `LayoutState` is re-keyed to
  `{sidebar, viewportWidth, narrowExpanded, rightbar, rightbarShown, rightbarTrack,
  rightbarFullscreen, rightbarInstant}`, and `computeColumns(viewport, sidebar, rightbar)`
  returns `{sidebar, center, rightbar}`.
- **Migration recipe**: re-register panels on the `rightbar` seat (session scope) using
  `RightbarOwnerProps`; replace open/close calls with `openRightbar(track, fullscreen)` /
  `closeRightbar()`. Tool-detail replacements should become right-sidebar tab bodies: the
  keyed `sidebar.right.pane.tab` slot whose key equals a
  `SidebarRightTabDefinition.id` (see [DSH-0.1.5-A1-16](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md)). Drop
  `selectedCallId`; express selection through `ctx.sidebarRight.active()` or your own
  store. Update imports of the removed layout constants/state types to the new names, and
  re-check CSS selectors that matched `data-selected`.
- **Verification**: typecheck with no `details` / `selectedCallId` references; a real
  mount shows the right column expanding, collapsing and going fullscreen, with
  `data-rightbar-col` present and no `data-selected`; switching sessions does not leak
  right-column state; narrow layouts respect the new 400px centre minimum.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `ui-layout/src/client/index.ts` (`rightbar` seat)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-layout/src/client/columns.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/columns.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-chat/src/client/contract/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-chat/src/client/details/DetailsPanel.tsx` (deleted at alpha.1)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/details/DetailsPanel.tsx) · [alpha.1 client slot catalog](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/extensions/cordis-client-runner/src/client/slot-catalog.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (Sidebar replaces the Detail panel)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)
