cards.title: Web Client: injection-surface signatures change — `CommandContribution.description` becomes a function, composer `busyEnter`, `inspectRequestPrompt` third argument + system-prompt inspector, deliverables turn-tail surface removed
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-15 · Web Client: injection-surface signatures change — `CommandContribution.description` becomes a function, composer `busyEnter`, `inspectRequestPrompt` third argument + system-prompt inspector, deliverables turn-tail surface removed

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that contribute slash commands, inject a composer
  bar, define conversation prompt targets/chat nodes, or use the deliverables turn-tail
  surface.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: four independent signature/surface changes land together:
  (1) `CommandContribution.description` becomes `readonly description: () => string`
  (`packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/contract.ts`; the service calls
  `contribution.description()`), so passing a plain string fails typecheck;
  (2) `ComposerBarInjected.resolveSubmitMode` is removed — the send policy is exposed as
  `hooks.busyEnter: ObservableSnapshot<BusyEnterBehavior>`, the pure decision is the
  exported `resolveSubmitMode(preferred, running, gesture, steeringAvailable)`, and
  `ComposerSubmitGesture` is replaced by `BusyEnterBehavior`
  (`ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts`, `input/submission-policy.ts`);
  (3) `ctx.uiConversation.inspectRequestPrompt(previous, event)` gains a third
  `system: SystemPromptNode | undefined` argument, and a new
  `inspectSystemPrompt(previous, event)` with `SystemPromptState` /
  `SystemPromptInspector` handles the prompt now that it is a surface node
  (`ui-conversation/src/client/contract/request-inspection.ts`, new
  `contract/system-prompt.ts`);
  (4) `ui-deliverables`' `conversation.chat.turnTail` injected surface loses
  `ProducedFilesInjected` (`isLoopback`, `ensureWorkspacePathOpen`,
  `hooks.workspacePathOpen`) and the "show in folder" affordance, with its locale keys
  deleted. Note a first-party inconsistency: `TurnTailOwnerProps.openFile` is still
  `(path: string) => void` while the other owners accept `(path, options?: {line})`.
- **Migration recipe**: return a function from `description` (evaluated per menu render,
  so localization follows language switches); read `hooks.busyEnter` and use the exported
  `resolveSubmitMode` for pure decisions; pass the new third argument to
  `inspectRequestPrompt` and register a `system/message`-consuming definition for
  `inspectSystemPrompt` where you render prompt history; drop dependencies on the removed
  deliverables surface and its locale keys.
- **Verification**: switching language updates command descriptions; busy-state Enter and
  the Send button agree (and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter takes the opposite gesture); a mid-history
  prompt update renders as a "system prompt update" row rather than a duplicate; the
  deliverables turn-tail has no show-in-folder branch.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `ui-commands/src/client/contract.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/contract.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-conversation/src/client/input/submission-policy.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/input/submission-policy.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-conversation/src/client/contract/request-inspection.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/request-inspection.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-conversation/src/client/contract/system-prompt.ts` (new)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/system-prompt.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-deliverables/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-deliverables/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: Web Client: right-sidebar and resource extension points (`client-resources`, `ui-sidebar-right` tab registry, `ui-dockkit` baseline, new header-corner slot, web-app patch rows, optional `webServer`)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-16 · Web Client: right-sidebar and resource extension points (`client-resources`, `ui-sidebar-right` tab registry, `ui-dockkit` baseline, new header-corner slot, web-app patch rows, optional `webServer`) - **Type**: capability - **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that add right-column tabs or viewers, provide resource content, or run on carriers without an HTTP server. - **Touchpoints**: #5, #3 - **Action level**: optional - **Symptoms**: three new client packages and a set of new seats appear: - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-resources`: the `ctx.resources` service (`register(provider)` / `pin(address, signal)` / `source(address)`), the global standard hook `useResource

(address)` merged into `GlobalStandardProps`, the `ResourceProtocolMap` declaration-merge point, and the `dsh-resource:///…` address protocol. - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-right`: occupies the `rightbar` seat and adds the slots `sidebar.right.pane.tab` (keyed), `sidebar.right.pane.tab.title` (keyed), `sidebar.right.tab.guide` (chain) and `sidebar.right.tab.menu.item` (list), plus the services `ctx.sidebarRight` (`openResource/openTab/close/active/isExpanded/toggleExpanded/focus/split/float/dock`) and `ctx.sidebarRightTabs` (`SidebarRightTabDefinition {id, kind, patterns, priority, canOpen, title, guide[]}`; `priority` defaults to `'extension'`, which outranks `'builtin'`). - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-dockkit`: a zero-cordis React dock-layout kit added to `PLATFORM_MODULES`; its own docs call it an **internal dependency of `ui-sidebar-right`, not a stable interface** — client plugins must not redeclare it in their manifest and should not build on its API directly. Reference implementations to copy: `ui-sidebar-files` (`kind='files'`, page type) and `ui-sidebar-textpreview` (`kind='text'`, `priority:'fallback'`, `patterns:['dsh-resource://file/**']`, `canOpen=parseFileAddress!==undefined`). A new slot `conversation.session.header.corner` (single/session) renders inside the session header. `dsh-web-app`'s `cordis.patch.yml` adds five loader rows (`workspace-files`, `resources`, `ui-sidebar-right`, `ui-sidebar-textpreview`, `ui-sidebar-files`) and five dependencies. `ClientModuleRegistry.fetchBundle(request)` is public, and `client/connection` / `client/modules` make `webServer` optional (`inject=['credentials']` plus conditional route registration), so non-HTTP carriers can compose them. - **Migration recipe**: register tab kinds through `ctx.sidebarRightTabs` and render bodies into the keyed `sidebar.right.pane.tab` slot; expose content through `ctx.resources` providers with `dsh-resource://` addresses and read it with `useResource`; do not add `ui-dockkit` to your own manifest; when copying a web profile composition, add the five new rows; if you relied on `webServer` being present, use `ctx.inject(['webServer'], …)` or `fetchBundle` instead of assuming it. - **Verification**: a registered tab opens from a `dsh-resource://` link, shows its title and guide, and `canOpen` can veto; `useResource` resolves and updates on provider changes; a carrier without `webServer` still loads connection/modules; the new header-corner slot renders without breaking header padding. - **Source**: [alpha.1 `client/resources/src/client/contract.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/resources/src/client/contract.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts) · [alpha.1 `client/web/src/platform.ts` (`ui-dockkit` baseline)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/web/src/platform.ts) · [alpha.1 `bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml` (five new rows)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml) · [alpha.1 `client/modules/src/index.ts` (`fetchBundle`, optional webServer)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/modules/src/index.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1) ---

cards.title: Web Client: file links open in the right sidebar (`openFile(path, {line})` → `ctx.sidebarRight.openResource`)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-17 · Web Client: file links open in the right sidebar (`openFile(path, {line})` → `ctx.sidebarRight.openResource`)

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that implement or call the `openFile` surface of chat
  nodes, tool rows or turn tails.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #5
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: `openFile` gains an optional second parameter
  (`openFile(path, options?: OpenFileOptions)` where `OpenFileOptions = { line?: number }`,
  1-based and defaulting to the file head) and its implementation changes: instead of
  calling the host opener (`ctx.remote.session.openWorkspacePath`), `ui-chat` resolves a
  file address and calls
  `ctx.sidebarRight.openResource(fileAddressFor(sessionId, cwd, path), {params:{line}})`,
  so the file renders inside the Web right sidebar. `ui-chat` also swaps its `layout`
  injection for `sidebarRight`, and tool rows gained a `filePathLine` helper. Plugins that
  assumed "open file = OS default application" see the in-page viewer instead;
  implementers must accept the second parameter. (First-party inconsistency:
  `TurnTailOwnerProps.openFile` still takes only `path`.)
- **Migration recipe**: accept `(path, options?)` in your implementations and forward the
  line parameter; route through `ctx.sidebarRight.openResource` with the file address. If
  you need a custom viewer, register a sidebar-right tab
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A1-16](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md)) instead of replacing the opener.
- **Verification**: clicking a path link opens the right sidebar at the requested line and
  does not invoke an OS opener; a custom `openFile` implementation compiles with the new
  signature; tool rows show the line-aware link.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `ui-chat/src/client/contract/slots.ts` (`openFile` signature)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-chat/src/client/apply.ts` (sidebarRight resource open)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/apply.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-tool/src/client/tool/components/ToolRow.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/tool/components/ToolRow.tsx) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (file links open in the Sidebar)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: `tool-subagent` `apply(ctx, config, session?)` and the scoped-preset requirement for `modelSelectionSettings`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-18 · `tool-subagent` `apply(ctx, config, session?)` and the scoped-preset requirement for `modelSelectionSettings`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: compositions that mount `tool-subagent` directly (especially with
  `modelSelectionSettings`) and wrappers that pass custom arguments to its `apply`.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `apply(ctx, config, session?)` gains a third parameter, and the standing
  `modelSelectionSettings` composition now **requires** a scoped preset Context — mounting
  it elsewhere throws
  `standing 'modelSelectionSettings' requires a scoped preset Context`. Sub-session model
  inheritance now reads the Session registry instead of the Agent registry, and
  `reconcileComposedAgents()` runs at the end of `apply`
  (`packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/index.ts`).
- **Migration recipe**: mount `modelSelectionSettings` only inside a preset/Agent scope, or
  pass the session explicitly via `apply(ctx, config, session)`; re-check any wrapper that
  called `apply` with positional arguments; re-verify inheritance expectations against the
  Session registry (the allowed-model set now follows the session, not the agent).
- **Verification**: mounting `modelSelectionSettings` outside a preset scope fails with
  the documented error; inside a preset scope composed agents reconcile and inherit the
  allowed model set; the package's
  `tests/model-selection-settings.spec.ts` and `tests/continuation-inheritance.spec.ts`
  are the behavior baseline.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `tool-subagent/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `tool-subagent/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2/packages/subagent/tool-subagent/src/index.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: host environment/trust seams: directory-picker requires an explicit `ssh` fact, SSH detection moves to the launch environment, and instruction discovery stops swallowing errors
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-19 · host environment/trust seams: directory-picker requires an explicit `ssh` fact, SSH detection moves to the launch environment, and instruction discovery stops swallowing errors

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins and tests that call `resolveDirectoryPickerBackend` or build
  `DirectoryPickerEnv` / `DirectoryPickerHostFacts`; deployments that used `.env` to
  influence SSH behavior; integrations that read project instructions through
  `agent-instructions`.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #4
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: three host-side changes land together. (1) `DirectoryPickerEnv` drops
  `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` and `DirectoryPickerHostFacts` gains a **required**
  `ssh: boolean`; `resolveDirectoryPickerBackend(facts)` now reads `facts.ssh`
  (`packages/host/directory-picker-auto/src/resolve.ts`). (2) SSH detection is derived
  from the launcher's environment snapshot through `launchedThroughSsh(environment)`, now
  exported by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-launch-environment` (previously a private function inside
  `bundle/web-app`), so a project/user `.env` can no longer spoof SSH. As a consequence
  `open-in-app` resolves no local applications over SSH (`resolveLaunch` returns null and
  `resolveOpenInAppApps` returns an empty map). (3) `agent-instructions`' project-root
  discovery only treats a confirmed missing provider path (`FS_NOT_FOUND`) as absent;
  other errors (permissions, I/O) now propagate instead of silently falling back to an
  ancestor project's instructions.
- **Migration recipe**: construct directory-picker facts with
  `ssh: launchedThroughSsh(launchEnvironmentOf(ctx))` and set `ssh: true` explicitly in
  tests; remove `.env`-based SSH spoofing from deployments (choose a browse backend by
  other means, or use real SSH); handle thrown errors from instruction discovery rather
  than assuming "no instructions exist".
- **Verification**: `resolveDirectoryPickerBackend` compiles with the required fact and
  selects browse/native correctly for `ssh: true/false`; an SSH-launched session resolves
  no local apps; a permission or I/O error during project-root discovery surfaces instead
  of loading an ancestor's instructions.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `directory-picker-auto/src/resolve.ts` (required `ssh` fact)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/host/directory-picker-auto/src/resolve.ts) · [alpha.1 `directory-picker-auto/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/host/directory-picker-auto/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 `util/launch-environment/src/index.ts` (`launchedThroughSsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/util/launch-environment/src/index.ts) · [alpha.1 `host/open-in-app/src/resolver.ts` (SSH short-circuit)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/host/open-in-app/src/resolver.ts) · [alpha.1 `context/agent-instructions/src/files.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/context/agent-instructions/src/files.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.1 release notes (project-root error reporting)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1)

cards.title: upgraded npm-global profiles serve a client combo that omits newly-added bundle modules (real-host verified)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A1-20 · upgraded npm-global profiles serve a client combo that omits newly-added bundle modules (real-host verified)

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: every client plugin on a profile created under an older dsh and upgraded in place via npm (observed: npm global, Windows). Pure client-UI fleets are the visible half — one dropped module can take down every plugin's registration.
- **Touchpoints**: #5 (client bundle loading), packaging
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: after the in-place upgrade the browser reports `failed to import loader entry <id>`: the combined `/plugins/??…` script executes but never registers modules the boot roster lists — the first unregistered entry is named (an innocent one) and ALL client plugins fail to load. In the same session, chat file links throw `sidebarRight: no registered tab type claims "dsh-resource://file/…"` because the sidebar tab type never registered. The boot roster DOES list the affected modules and their `lib/client.js` artifacts exist in the npm tree — yet the combo route answers 404 for them while answering 200 for pre-existing modules at the same rev.
- **Migration recipe**: attribute before touching plugins — fetch one NEW bundle module and one OLD module at the same rev; old 200 + new 404 pins the gap to the host's artifact/rev set, not to the plugin. Then restart the host once: the observed case self-healed on a subsequent boot (the newly-added rows entered the roster and the served combo). If a restart does not heal it, roll the global package back to the previous published version and report upstream. Upstream thread with both rounds of forensics: [deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness discussion #5999](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5999).
- **Verification**: after the healing restart, the boot roster lists the new modules AND a combo fetch for one of them returns 200 with the module's code present; all previously working plugins load again.
- **Source**: real-host probes 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200/404 comparison at the same rev; npm-tree artifact file checks); [discussion #5999](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5999) (comment [18371079](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/5999#discussioncomment-18371079) adds the 0.1.5-alpha.2 round).

---

## Six-plugin real-host crossing record (2026-09-09, Windows npm-global upgraded profile)

The analysis environment used for cards A1-01…A1-19 was Windows-only with no real-host cold start. This record supplies the missing real-host half for the same edge:

- Six link-installed Web client plugins crossed `0.1.3-alpha.2 → 0.1.5-alpha.1` with **zero code changes**: typecheck / build / unit tests green against the 0.1.5-alpha.1 source tree for the five compiled plugins (file-trace 105 / progress 39 / whale 34 / minigames 203 / input-history 18 tests), the vanilla-lib paste plugin verified by a runtime pass.
- All six shipped "declare support" patch versions the same day (file-trace v0.3.9 / progress v0.9.15 / whale v0.3.16 / minigames v0.3.17 / input-history v0.1.11 / paste-input v0.1.22), each tag verified by SHA on all three push mirrors; the boot manifest confirmed all six in the client roster.
- The crossing also surfaced the real-host pitfall carded as [DSH-0.1.5-A1-20](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md): the first post-upgrade boot dropped the newly-added `ui-sidebar-*` rows from the served combo; a host restart self-healed the roster/combo mismatch. Rollback to the previous published version was verified as the escape hatch.
- Not verified here: host-plane plugins calling session persistence (cards A1-01/A1-02 are recipe-level), the Python SDK, and headless/ACP products.

## Corridor status

- First card set for the `dsh-v0.1.3-alpha.2 → dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1` edge — an unusually
  wide window (2552 changed files, +78538/−12512) curated from the pinned tag diff and the
  published npm tarball `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-alpha.1`. Status `draft`: cards A1-01…A1-19 come from the analysis environment with no real-host cold start; the [six-plugin real-host crossing record](#six-plugin-real-host-crossing-record-2026-09-09-windows-npm-global-upgraded-profile) below and card A1-20 supply that half for the client-UI fleet.
- Client-side plugin seams are carded too: the `details` → `rightbar` rework and layout
  rewrite ([DSH-0.1.5-A1-14](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md)), the command/composer/prompt-inspection
  signature changes ([DSH-0.1.5-A1-15](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md)), the new right-sidebar and
  resource extension points ([DSH-0.1.5-A1-16](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md)), and the file-open
  behavior ([DSH-0.1.5-A1-17](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md)).
- Still uncarded (listed, not carded): Toast/connection-indicator styling, drag-handle
  and ModelSelect portal fixes, `StatsLine` → `StatsPills` (import it only if you referenced
  the old export/DOM), locale-key churn beyond the carded surfaces, the optional subagent
  plugins' runtime bumps (Codex 0.153.4 / Claude Code 2.1.263), empty-message rejection
  (host-side `gateway/bad-request` in `session-controller/src/commands.ts`), project-root
  discovery error reporting, and the collapsed-thinking-summary Markdown fix.
- No action needed for these surfaces (verified unchanged, listed so they are not
  misreported as hits): `packages/shell/*` (bash/pwsh tools, `shell-env`) — code
  unchanged, tool names and parameter shapes stable; the `fs` tools (`tool-fs`,
  `tool-fs-search`, `tool-str-replace-editor`) — schemas unchanged; Agent Presets
  (`cordis`/`minimal`/`ptc`/`standard`) and their `preset.yml` — byte-identical; `engines`
  (`^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`) and all vendored versions (`cordis@4.0.2`, `schemastery`,
  loader) — unchanged; the `dsh.client` manifest schema — unchanged; `packages/sandbox/*`
  — unchanged apart from the native package rename.
- This edge adds several subsystems (desktop apps, `native/system`, and a broad client
  rewrite). Cards cover the host/core surfaces that were pinned to source coordinates;
  client-side and new-subsystem surfaces are covered by follow-up cards where they reach a
  plugin-facing seam. Treat uncarded areas as uncarded, not as proven-unchanged.

*Changes to host UI, performance, or non-carded surfaces do not prove the absence of API
or behavior impact. When a real plugin is affected, add a primary source and a
reproducible verification record.*

cards.title: `workspaceFiles` drops the `Agent` first parameter for a Typert `workspaceFileScope` lookup; client resource type, `reload`/`restat`, and `absolute` scope authorization all change
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-01 · `workspaceFiles` drops the `Agent` first parameter for a Typert `workspaceFileScope` lookup; client resource type, `reload`/`restat`, and `absolute` scope authorization all change

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Host plugins that inject or call the `workspaceFiles` service, Web Client
  plugins that consume the `file` resource (`useResource<'file'>`) or construct the file
  resource provider, and tests that mock the Remote.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #6
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the previous edge shipped `workspaceFiles.*(agent, path, …)`; at
  `0.1.5-alpha.2` the first parameter is a `WorkspaceFileScope` resolved by the Typert
  lookup `workspaceFileScope` (`packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts`:
  `static inject = ['fs','sandboxPolicy','sessions','typert']`, lookup registered next to
  the Remote). Every method changes signature and two new methods appear (`readAll`,
  `readRelated`). On the client, the `file` resource value becomes `WorkspaceFileStat`
  (the `changed` field is gone), the `WorkspaceFileResource`/`SessionLookup` exports are
  removed, `reload(address)` plus `ChangeFeed.requestRestat` and the `{kind:'restat'}`
  notice are deleted, and the provider factory is
  `createFileResourceProvider(remote, changes)` with the plugin's inject list dropping
  `sessions` (`['resources','remote','remote.workspaceFiles']`). Address handling changes
  too: an `absolute` scope address no longer authorizes a Host call and always returns
  `workspace-file/unknown-workspace`; `fileAddressFor()` routes out-of-workspace absolute
  paths through the `session` scope, `sessionFileAddress()` keeps the leading `/`, and
  `parseFileAddress()` is now handwritten prefix parsing that ignores `?`/`#` and does not
  resolve `.`/`..`.
- **Migration recipe**: on the client, pass the session id only (the lookup resolves the
  scope), stop calling `reload`/`restat` and decide staleness from `version`, and update
  types to `WorkspaceFileStat`. On the Host, inject `sessions` (plus
  `sessionPersistence` when cold sessions must resolve) and never pass an Agent; expect
  `gateway/lookup-not-found` if the lookup cannot resolve. Absolute paths must be
  addressed in the `session` scope; treat `unknown-workspace` as the documented outcome for
  `absolute`. Normalize `.`/`..` yourself before calling `parseFileAddress()`.
- **Verification**: typecheck passes with the new signatures; a session-scoped file address
  resolves through the Remote; an `absolute` address returns `workspace-file/unknown-workspace`;
  a `reload` reference no longer compiles; `createFileResourceProvider(remote, changes)`
  compiles with the two-argument call.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `api/workspace-files/src/index.ts` (scope lookup, `readAll`/`readRelated`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `client/types.ts` (`WorkspaceFileStat`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/api/workspace-files/src/client/types.ts) · [alpha.2 `client/provider.ts` (absolute scope, no reload)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/api/workspace-files/src/client/provider.ts) · [alpha.2 `util/workspace-path/src/index.ts` (`fileAddressFor`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/util/workspace-path/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `file-address.ts` (`parseFileAddress`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/util/workspace-path/src/file-address.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: file reads are no longer confined to the workspace root (`outside-workspace` now applies to listings only), with a new `maxFileBytes` cap and `readAll`/`readRelated`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-02 · file reads are no longer confined to the workspace root (`outside-workspace` now applies to listings only), with a new `maxFileBytes` cap and `readAll`/`readRelated`

- **Type**: security
- **Applies to**: Host deployments that expose file content to users through the
  `workspaceFiles` surface (previews, editors, chat file links) and any plugin that assumed
  the read path was workspace-confined.
- **Touchpoints**: #4, #3
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `locateFile` no longer calls `confine(...)`; reads follow the composed
  filesystem's read access **including paths outside the workspace**
  (`packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts`), and `workspace-file/outside-workspace` now
  applies only to directory listings. The package README states the boundary explicitly:
  the sandboxing backend fences writes and edits, not reads. A new config key
  `maxFileBytes` (default 32 MiB) caps the new `readAll`/`readRelated` methods, which fail
  with `too-large` instead of truncating; `readRelated` resolves relative paths from the
  base file's directory (including out of workspace).
- **Migration recipe**: stop treating workspace containment as the read boundary — the
  effective boundary is the composed `ctx.fs` plus the sandbox policy, so review which
  backends a deployment mounts and what read access they grant. Set `maxFileBytes`
  deliberately for the deployment (it bounds the new whole-file reads). When a plugin
  serves file content to a user, re-check that the paths it accepts are the paths you
  intend to expose; if a workflow needs containment, enforce it in the plugin rather than
  relying on the service.
- **Verification**: reading a path outside the workspace root succeeds through the composed
  filesystem, while listing a directory outside the root still returns
  `workspace-file/outside-workspace`; a read above `maxFileBytes` fails with `too-large`
  (no truncated content); the deployment's backend read policy is recorded in the
  migration notes.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `api/workspace-files/src/index.ts` (`maxFileBytes`, unconfined `locateFile`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `api/workspace-files/README.md` (reads may target paths outside the workspace)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/api/workspace-files/README.md) · [alpha.1 `api/workspace-files/src/index.ts` (confined read, for contrast)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/api/workspace-files/src/index.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: the `conversation` slot moves under the new root-scoped `main` keyed slot; global panels register through `sidebar.panellist`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-03 · the `conversation` slot moves under the new root-scoped `main` keyed slot; global panels register through `sidebar.panellist`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that registered into the `conversation` slot or that
  add a global sidebar panel.
- **Touchpoints**: #6, #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `ui-layout` replaces its single `'conversation'` slot
  (`{ kind:'single'; scope:'session-maybe' }` at alpha.1) with a root-scoped keyed slot
  `'main': { kind:'keyed'; scope:'root' }` whose **reserved `conversation` key hosts the
  Conversation**; other keys receive no Session binding. `ui-conversation` registers
  `'main.conversation'`, and a new root-scoped list slot `'sidebar.panellist'`
  (`owner: SidebarPanelIconOwnerProps`) lets a plugin contribute an icon entry
  (`id`, optional `order`, string or locale-aware `label`) that addresses the panel body
  registered in `main` under the same key. `SidebarRootInjected` gains `selectPanel(id)`
  and `hooks.panels`; selecting a missing `main` entry throws without changing the current
  selection, and with no registrations neither the list nor its spacing renders.
- **Migration recipe**: move conversation-slot registrations to `'main.conversation'`;
  register a global panel as an icon in `'sidebar.panellist'` plus a body in `'main'` with
  the same key. Read the selected state through `usePanelInfo`, and keep the `main` key
  registered whenever the panel can be selected (selecting a missing key throws).
- **Verification**: a panel icon appears and selecting it renders the `main[key]` body; the
  conversation renders at the reserved `conversation` key; selecting an unregistered key
  throws and leaves the previous panel selected; zero registrations render no list.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts` (`main` keyed slot)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts) · [alpha.1 `client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts` (old `conversation` slot)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `client/ui-sidebar/src/client/contract/slots.ts` (`sidebar.panellist`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [alpha.2 `client/ui-sidebar/README.md` (panel contract)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar/README.md) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (Web plugin panel API)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: minimal profiles become persistent-shell-only (`str_replace_editor` is opt-in; the bare filesystem group is gone)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-04 · minimal profiles become persistent-shell-only (`str_replace_editor` is opt-in; the bare filesystem group is gone)

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: profile compositions and plugins that assumed the `minimal` preset or
  `sdk-minimal` bundle mounts an editor tool by default.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: the `minimal` agent preset is now described as a "single-tool
  coding-agent composition": the model receives only the platform persistent shell (`bash`
  on POSIX, `pwsh` on win32) — the `str_replace_editor` row and the bare local filesystem
  group are removed (`packages/preset/agent-presets/presets/minimal/agent.cordis.yml`).
  The `sdk-minimal` bundle patch likewise drops the `fs-local` and
  `str-replace-editor` rows (`packages/bundle/sdk-minimal/cordis.patch.yml`), and its
  package dependencies lose `dsh-fs-local` / `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor`. The bash tool
  description now says network access depends on the task environment (prefer configured
  mirrors/proxies) instead of claiming a package mirror. `str_replace_editor` remains
  available by explicit opt-in patch, and the CLI reference documents the new stance; the
  persistent-shell completion/timeout reporting is also unified.
- **Migration recipe**: if a workflow needs file editing in a minimal profile, add an
  explicit patch mounting the editor tool (see the CLI reference and the SDK smoke test's
  opt-in case) instead of assuming it ships. Re-check any prompt or tool-guidance text that
  promised an editor or a package mirror in these profiles.
- **Verification**: `dsh --profile <minimal-profile> --dump-config` lists only the
  persistent shell tool rows; the opt-in patch adds `str_replace_editor`; a filtered
  subagent no longer receives guidance for the removed tools (see
  [DSH-0.1.5-A2-07](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)).
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `presets/minimal/agent.cordis.yml` (single-tool composition)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/preset/agent-presets/presets/minimal/agent.cordis.yml) · [alpha.2 `bundle/sdk-minimal/cordis.patch.yml` (rows removed)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/bundle/sdk-minimal/cordis.patch.yml) · [alpha.2 `apps/cli/reference/README.md` (minimal-profile stance)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/apps/cli/reference/README.md) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (minimal-profile default tools)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: two new non-ignorable session events make alpha.2 sessions unreadable by older harnesses; `feedback/record` payload and subagent catalog semantics change
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-05 · two new non-ignorable session events make alpha.2 sessions unreadable by older harnesses; `feedback/record` payload and subagent catalog semantics change

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: anything that reads stored Session logs across harness versions, writes
  feedback events, or consumes the subagent catalog.
- **Touchpoints**: #2
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `deliverables/presented` and `subagent/catalog` join
  `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES` **without** an `ignorable` marker, and
  `packages/session/session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts` refuses unknown
  non-ignorable events ("unknown to this harness and not marked ignorable; refusing to
  interpret the log — it was likely written by a newer harness"). Because
  `Session.append()` has no `ignorable` channel, a producer cannot mark these events, so an
  **older harness (including `0.1.5-alpha.1`) cannot read a session that contains them** —
  one-way readability within the same V3 format. In addition, `feedback/record` changes
  from `{ text: string }` to `{ text?, category? }` and `recordFeedback(session, text)`
  becomes `recordFeedback(session, entry)`; subagents now persist a catalog entry
  (`subagent/catalog`, projection `subagentCatalog` at `stateVersion: 2`), and a catalog
  append failure disposes the run and surfaces the error to the caller.
- **Migration recipe**: keep read and write harness versions aligned across a session store
  — do not expect an older build to read sessions written by alpha.2, and do not hand-write
  the new event types. Update feedback callers to the entry object (optionally with
  `category`). When consuming subagent state, read the `subagentCatalog` projection and
  handle a disposed run when catalog persistence fails.
- **Verification**: an `0.1.5-alpha.1` build refuses a session containing the new events
  with the documented error; `recordFeedback(session, { text })` compiles and writes a
  `feedback/record` entry; the `subagentCatalog` projection populates after a subagent is
  created.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `core/session/src/known-event-types.ts` (two new events)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/core/session/src/known-event-types.ts) · [alpha.2 `session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts` (refusal path)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/session/session-persistence/src/storage-contract.ts) · [alpha.2 `feedback/command-feedback/src/index.ts` (`FeedbackRecord`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/feedback/command-feedback/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `subagent/subagent/src/catalog.ts` (`subagent/catalog`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/subagent/subagent/src/catalog.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: `dsh-llm-pi-ai` config/type changes (optional `piProvider`, required `modelErrors`, `deferred` resolution) and provider-level `error`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-06 · `dsh-llm-pi-ai` config/type changes (optional `piProvider`, required `modelErrors`, `deferred` resolution) and provider-level `error`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that construct or read `ResolvedPiAiProviderProfile`, call
  `resolveRouteModels`/`assertServiceable`, or surface provider diagnostics.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #1
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `ResolvedPiAiProviderProfile.piProvider` becomes optional, `modelErrors`
  becomes a required `ReadonlyMap<string,string>`, and `catalogError?` is added
  (`packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/config.ts`); `resolveRouteModels(request, validation)` takes
  a `'strict' | 'deferred'` validation mode, `assertServiceable(config, previous?)` takes
  the previous config, and `PiAiCatalogError` is a new export (`src/catalog.ts`). Stored
  configurations that drift after a catalog change no longer hide the whole model-settings
  entry: profiles resolve with `'deferred'` so per-model errors are preserved, writes
  validate only changed providers, and requesting a broken model fails with
  `INVALID_CONFIG` while other models keep working. `LlmConfigurableProvider.error?: string`
  surfaces a provider-level diagnostic (`packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts`).
- **Migration recipe**: null-check `piProvider` before use and handle `modelErrors` /
  `catalogError` instead of assuming a serviceable profile; update
  `resolveRouteModels`/`assertServiceable` call sites to the new signatures; surface
  `LlmConfigurableProvider.error` in provider lists rather than hiding the provider.
- **Verification**: a drifted stored config still shows the settings entry with per-model
  errors; a request for a broken model fails with `INVALID_CONFIG` while a healthy model
  succeeds; a provider-level `error` renders in the settings surface.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `llm-pi-ai/src/config.ts` (`piProvider?`, `modelErrors`, `assertServiceable`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/config.ts) · [alpha.2 `llm-pi-ai/src/catalog.ts` (`resolveRouteModels`, `PiAiCatalogError`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/catalog.ts) · [alpha.2 `llm-pi-ai/src/adapter.ts` (`INVALID_CONFIG` path)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/adapter.ts) · [alpha.2 `llm/src/types.ts` (`LlmConfigurableProvider.error`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (pi-ai config diagnostics)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: tool guidance sections follow the visible tool set per scope
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-07 · tool guidance sections follow the visible tool set per scope

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that contribute system-prompt guidance for tools, and any
  workflow relying on filtered subagents.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: the `read`/`write`/`edit`/`glob`/`grep` guidance sections in
  `tool-fs` and `tool-fs-search` now render conditionally:
  `text: ({ scope }) => ctx.tools.get(name, scope) === undefined ? '' : …`, so a subagent
  whose tools were filtered no longer receives instructions for tools it cannot use
  (`write` only recommends `edit` when `edit` is visible; `grep` only mentions reading
  context when `read` is visible). The functional `text` signature itself already existed
  at alpha.1; this edge is where the first-party tools adopt it. Scope-dependent **schema**
  wording is explicitly not implemented — tool schemas stay static.
- **Migration recipe**: apply the same pattern to your own guidance sections (render only
  when `ctx.tools.get(name, scope)` resolves), and do not rely on guidance text as evidence
  that a tool is mounted. Keep schema descriptions accurate for all scopes since they
  cannot vary per scope.
- **Verification**: a filtered subagent's prompt contains no guidance for the filtered
  tools; an unfiltered agent still gets the full guidance; tool schemas are unchanged
  across scopes.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `fs/tool-fs/src/read.ts` (scope-aware guidance)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/fs/tool-fs/src/read.ts) · [alpha.2 `fs/tool-fs-search/src/grep.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/grep.ts) · [alpha.2 `core/system-prompt/README.md` (`text({ scope })` pattern)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/core/system-prompt/README.md) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (guidance aligned with visible tools)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: file delivery and reveal (`present` tool, `deliverables/presented`, `workspaceDesktop()`/`revealPath`, native reveal helpers)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-08 · file delivery and reveal (`present` tool, `deliverables/presented`, `workspaceDesktop()`/`revealPath`, native reveal helpers)

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: Host and Web Client plugins that surface produced files to users.
- **Touchpoints**: #5, #3, #7
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: a new package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present` adds the model tool
  `present` (`name='tool-present'`, `inject=['tools','fs','sessionProjections']`, config
  `maxFiles` default 8). It declares final files accessible through the Session
  filesystem — including files created by shell commands — records paths and optional
  descriptions without copying contents, and appends a `deliverables/presented` event.
  Users open the current source file in their default application. The `present` tool joins
  the default Web tool set. For reveal, `SessionController.workspaceDesktop()` and the
  optional `SessionControllerInternals.revealPath` plus
  `SessionOpenWorkspacePathRequest.action?: 'reveal'` are added, and
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command` exports `nativeFileManager()`, `revealNativePath()` and
  the `NativeFileManager = 'finder' | 'explorer' | 'directory'` type (Windows uses
  `explorer.exe /select,` and treats Explorer exit 1 as handed off).
- **Migration recipe**: use `present` to declare deliverables instead of inventing your own
  "output file" event; read `deliverables/presented` to list them (see
  [DSH-0.1.5-A2-05](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md) for the readability caveat). For "show in file
  manager", call the reveal action or the native helpers rather than spawning a file
  manager yourself.
- **Verification**: a `present` call appends `deliverables/presented` and the file opens in
  the default application; the reveal action opens the containing folder with the file
  selected on macOS/Windows/Linux.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `fs/tool-present/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/fs/tool-present/README.md) · [alpha.2 `fs/tool-present/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/fs/tool-present/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `api/session-controller/src/index.ts` (`workspaceDesktop`, `revealPath`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/api/session-controller/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `util/native-command/src/index.ts` (reveal helpers)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/util/native-command/src/index.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (file delivery)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: document previews in the right sidebar; the `ui-sidebar-textpreview` package is renamed to `ui-sidebar-documentpreview`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-09 · document previews in the right sidebar; the `ui-sidebar-textpreview` package is renamed to `ui-sidebar-documentpreview`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins or compositions that depend on
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-textpreview`, and plugins that want richer file
  previews.
- **Touchpoints**: #6
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-textpreview` is renamed to
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview` (package name and
  `tsconfig.base.json` path mapping), and the right sidebar gains previews for common
  document types: Markdown, syntax-highlighted code, HTML, PDF and images. A dependency on
  the old package name no longer resolves.
- **Migration recipe**: update dependencies/imports to
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview` and re-check the tab definition's
  `patterns`/`kind` if you copied it as a reference implementation. Keep the `file`
  resource reading path from [DSH-0.1.5-A2-01](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md) in mind when rendering
  previews.
- **Verification**: the renamed package resolves and the right sidebar renders Markdown,
  code, HTML, PDF and image previews; the old package name resolves nowhere.

cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-10 · new `chunked-list` and `tool-present` packages, Agent Teams packages on npm, and the `fs-ext` install note

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugin packaging and deployments that install from npm.
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging surface); #2/#4 where the new packages are used.
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: two new packages ship in this window —
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-chunked-list` (`ChunkedList<T>`, `appendChunkedList`,
  `iterateChunkedList`, `chunkedListSchema`, chunk capacity 64, `peerDependencies` on
  cordis) and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present` (see
  [DSH-0.1.5-A2-08](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)). The experimental Agent Teams packages are now
  installable from npm but require an explicit profile addition (not enabled by default).
  `session-persistence-jsonl`'s worker build now inlines workspace dependencies (except the
  native addon) and skips the client face. The release notes also mention an npm-install fix
  for `fs-ext`; **note that the alpha.1→alpha.2 tag diff contains no `fs-ext` change**
  (the source switch to `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-system` landed earlier), so treat that
  note as a publication/pipeline fix. The published package corroborates it from the npm
  side: `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-alpha.2` lists 72 direct dependencies and none of them is
  `fs-ext`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local` depends only on `koffi` +
  `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` (registry checked 2026-09-09).
- **Migration recipe**: use `chunked-list` for large persisted lists instead of hand-rolled
  chunking; add Agent Teams explicitly if you want them. For the `fs-ext` note: assert that
  your installed dependency tree contains no `fs-ext` (and no local build requirement)
  rather than looking for a code change.
- **Verification**: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-chunked-list` resolves and round-trips a list through
  `appendChunkedList`/`iterateChunkedList`; `npm ls fs-ext` is empty in a fresh install;
  the Agent Teams profile only appears after an explicit add.

cards.title: repeated MCP tool-list pagination cursors are rejected instead of hanging
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-11 · repeated MCP tool-list pagination cursors are rejected instead of hanging

- **Type**: fix
- **Applies to**: deployments that connect MCP servers, and plugins that inspect the
  discovered MCP tool set.
- **Touchpoints**: #7
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: a repeated pagination cursor during MCP tool-list discovery is rejected
  instead of making startup or synchronization wait indefinitely, and the last valid tool
  set stays available (release notes). A headless expected-output case was added
  (`apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/mcp-pagination.expected.e2e.ts` with
  `expected/mcp-pagination/stderr-cause.txt`), which is the observable contract for this
  fix; the implementation lives in the MCP client package (outside this analysis face).
- **Migration recipe**: no action for most plugins; MCP-facing integrations should tolerate
  a rejected pagination cycle (keep using the last valid tool set) rather than retrying
  forever.
- **Verification**: a server that repeats a cursor produces the documented rejection
  message and the session continues with the previous tool set.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 headless MCP pagination expectation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/mcp-pagination.expected.e2e.ts) · [alpha.2 expected stderr cause](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/apps/cli/tests/profiles/headless/tests/expected/mcp-pagination/stderr-cause.txt) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (MCP pagination)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: `rightbar` becomes root-scoped with a new `rightbar.session` child; the layout service and store are rewritten
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-13 · `rightbar` becomes root-scoped with a new `rightbar.session` child; the layout service and store are rewritten

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that occupy the `rightbar` slot, read layout state, or
  call `ctx.layout`.
- **Touchpoints**: #5, #6
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: at alpha.1 `ui-layout` declares `'conversation'`
  (`{kind:'single'; scope:'session-maybe'}`) and `'rightbar'`
  (`{kind:'single'; scope:'session'}`). At alpha.2 the central column is the keyed root slot
  `'main'` (see [DSH-0.1.5-A2-03](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)) and `'rightbar'` is **root** scope,
  with Session-bound content moved to the new single session slot `'rightbar.session'`.
  `ui-sidebar-right` registers both layers: the root `rightbar` (`RightbarRoot`, which reads
  `usePanelInfo` to decide whether to mount the Session subtree) and the session
  `rightbar.session` (`RightbarSeat`). `AppFrame` no longer wraps the right column in
  `SessionProvider`, so `PropsRuntime<'rightbar'>` loses the Session standard props — an
  occupant that expects them stops typechecking and loses its Session binding. The layout
  service gains `selectPanel(panelId: MainPanelId | null)` (throws for an unregistered key
  and keeps the previous selection) and `beginNavigation(): AbortSignal`, drops
  `attachPanels` (the constructor now takes `(panels, hasMainPanel)`), and exports
  `MainPanelId`/`PanelInfo`; `usePanelInfo` becomes a global standard prop. The store state
  splits into `{ panelInfo, layoutInfo }`, so `useStore(s => s.sidebar)` must become
  `s.layoutInfo.sidebar`, and `ConvOwnerProps` is removed.
- **Migration recipe**: re-register right-bar content in `rightbar.session` and keep only
  root-level chrome in `rightbar`; read the current panel through `usePanelInfo`; update
  store selectors to the nested shape; replace `attachPanels` with constructor wiring; treat
  a `selectPanel` throw as a programming error (it means the `main` key is not registered).
- **Verification**: the right column renders a Session tab and collapses when the panel
  renders nothing; `selectPanel('missing')` throws and leaves the previous selection;
  typecheck fails on the old `PropsRuntime<'rightbar'>` usage and on `s.sidebar`; a root-level
  panel renders with no Session.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-layout/src/client/index.ts` (`main`/`rightbar` root, `usePanelInfo`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-layout/src/client/service.ts` (`selectPanel`, `beginNavigation`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/service.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-layout/src/client/stores.ts` (`panelInfo`/`layoutInfo`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/stores.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-layout/src/client/AppFrame.tsx` (no `SessionProvider`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/AppFrame.tsx) · [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-right/src/client/shell/RightbarRoot.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/shell/RightbarRoot.tsx) · [alpha.1 `ui-layout/src/client/index.ts` (session-scoped `rightbar`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-layout/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (Web plugin panel API)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: `client-resources` drops `reload` from `ResourceSnapshot`/`ResourceProvider`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-14 · `client-resources` drops `reload` from `ResourceSnapshot`/`ResourceProvider`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that consume `useResource` results or implement a
  resource provider.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: at alpha.1 `ResourceSnapshot` carries `readonly reload: () => void` and
  `ResourceProvider` an optional `reload?(address)`; both are gone at alpha.2, and the
  internal `idle(status)` no longer attaches one. `useResource(...).reload()` stops
  compiling, and a provider that still implements `reload` has dead code that the framework
  never calls. The file resource's own `reload(address)`/`ChangeFeed.requestRestat` removal
  is a separate symptom of the same cleanup (see
  [DSH-0.1.5-A2-01](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)).
- **Migration recipe**: delete `reload` from provider implementations and call sites;
  refresh through the provider's own protocol (bump a request key, re-call the Remote
  method, or invalidate your own cache) and derive staleness from the value's `version` where
  the resource carries one.
- **Verification**: typecheck passes without `reload`; the old reference fails; a refresh
  through the replacement path updates the rendered value.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `client/resources/src/client/contract.ts` (no `reload`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/resources/src/client/contract.ts) · [alpha.1 `client/resources/src/client/contract.ts` (`reload` present)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/resources/src/client/contract.ts) · [alpha.2 `client/resources/src/client/resources.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/resources/src/client/resources.ts)

cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-15 · `ui-primitives` replaces `DocumentFileIcon` with `FileTypeIcon`/`classifyFileType`/`fileExtension`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that import icon or file-type helpers from
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, or deep-import `relativizeToCwd` from `ui-tool`.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `DocumentFileIcon.tsx` is deleted and the export removed. New exports:
  `FileTypeIcon` (28 px, colour overridable with `--dsh-file-type-icon-color`),
  `classifyFileType(path, context?)`, `fileExtension(path)`, plus the
  `FileType`/`FileTypeKind`/`CodeFileType`/`FileTypeProjectContext` types;
  `LinkIcon.classifyLinkPath` now delegates to `classifyFileType` before folding to its six
  classes. `relativizeToCwd` moved out of `ui-tool`'s internal module into
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-util-workspace-path` (the public `./client` entry never exported it, so
  only deep imports break). Also in `ui-primitives`: `Menu` closes after a click inside a
  cross-origin iframe and gains `autoFocus` (arrow/Home/End keys, Esc returns to the anchor),
  and `CodeBlock` gains `lineNumbers` (copy text stays unnumbered) plus the
  `--dsl-code-block-background` variable.
- **Migration recipe**: import `FileTypeIcon`/`classifyFileType`/`fileExtension` instead of
  `DocumentFileIcon`; if you deep-imported `relativizeToCwd` from `ui-tool`, import it from
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-util-workspace-path`.
- **Verification**: no export named `DocumentFileIcon` resolves; the icon renders for a known
  extension and honours the colour variable; the deep import compiles from the new package.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-primitives/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-primitives/src/FileTypeIcon.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/FileTypeIcon.tsx) · [alpha.2 `ui-primitives/src/code-file-types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/code-file-types.ts) · [alpha.2 `util/workspace-path/src/index.ts` (`relativizeToCwd`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/util/workspace-path/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-primitives/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/README.md) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: `ui-dockkit` contract drifts again (required `dropZone`/`canCloseTab`, `hideSplitWhenBlocked`, TabMenu roles)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-16 · `ui-dockkit` contract drifts again (required `dropZone`/`canCloseTab`, `hideSplitWhenBlocked`, TabMenu roles)

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that embed the dock kit or feed it an adapter (the
  package is documented as a **non-stable internal dependency**, so this is a heads-up rather
  than a compatibility promise).
- **Touchpoints**: #5, #6
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `DockLabels` now requires `dropZone: Readonly<Record<DockZone, string>>`
  (five zone labels used by the new dashed-card drop hint); `PaneCallbacks` requires
  `canCloseTab(tabId)` and renames `hideSplitAtCapacity` to `hideSplitWhenBlocked`;
  `TabMenuProps.onClose` becomes `(() => void) | undefined` (undefined hides the close item);
  every `TabMenuExtras` item must carry `role="menuitem"` or the menu is treated as empty and
  not rendered; the chip's close affordance is now revealed on active/hover/focus and overlays
  the title end, titles clip with a 16 px fade (`data-dockkit-tab-clipped`) instead of an
  ellipsis, the chip strip scrolls with edge fades (`data-dockkit-strip-scroll`) and keeps the
  active chip in view.
- **Migration recipe**: supply `labels.dropZone` and `canCloseTab`, rename the split flag, add
  the menu item roles, and re-check any test selectors that keyed on the old chip markup
  (`.dockkit` data attributes replaced class-based assumptions).
- **Verification**: typecheck passes with the new required members; a tab menu renders with
  roles present; dropping a tab shows the dashed card with `labels.dropZone[zone]`; the sole
  guide chip has no close affordance.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-dockkit/src/contract/adapter.ts` (`dropZone`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/contract/adapter.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-dockkit/src/components/render.ts` (`canCloseTab`, `hideSplitWhenBlocked`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/render.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-dockkit/src/components/TabMenu.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-dockkit/src/components/TabMenu.tsx) · [alpha.2 `ui-dockkit/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-dockkit/README.md)

cards.title: `ui-message-feedback` injected surface is rewritten and grows a feedback dialog with categories
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-17 · `ui-message-feedback` injected surface is rewritten and grows a feedback dialog with categories

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that call the message-feedback service or register
  feedback UI.
- **Touchpoints**: #5, #3
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `MessageFeedbackInjected` loses `rate`, `clearNote` and `clear`; it gains
  `current(messageId)`, `openDialog(messageId)` and `acknowledge()`; `toggle` returns
  `MessageFeedbackToggleResult` instead of `MessageFeedbackActionResult`; the plugin's
  `inject` adds `remote.sessionFeedback`. A new `conversation.input.overlay` entry
  `feedback-dialog` (order 2) plus a `FeedbackDialogController` render the dialog, `/feedback`
  opens it through the new action-command kind (see
  [DSH-0.1.5-A2-22](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)), and the dialog offers the seven
  `FeedbackCategory` chips. `MessageFeedbackItem`/`MessageFeedbackPutRequest` gain an
  optional `category`, and changing it counts as a material edit.
- **Migration recipe**: replace removed calls with `current` + `openDialog` (or `toggle`),
  update the `toggle` result type, add `remote.sessionFeedback` to your inject list, and pass
  `category` where you write feedback. The Host-side `recordFeedback(session, entry)` change
  is separate — see [DSH-0.1.5-A2-05](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md). Forward note for targets at or
  above `0.1.5-rc.2`: that edge removes `toggle`/`acknowledge` again and makes `rating`
  required on `openDialog`, superseding the injected half of this card — see
  [v0.1.5-rc.2.md](v0.1.5-rc.2.md).
- **Verification**: typecheck passes against the new injected surface; `/feedback` opens the
  dialog and records an entry with a category; `acknowledge()` shows the toast; a stale
  `rate(...)` reference fails to compile.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-message-feedback/src/client/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/slots.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-message-feedback/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-message-feedback/src/client/FeedbackDialog.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/FeedbackDialog.tsx) · [alpha.2 `feedback/message-feedback/src/types.ts` (`category`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/feedback/message-feedback/src/types.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (`/feedback`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: `ui-workspace` exposes `openSession`/`openWorkspace`/`forkSession` and now requires the `layout` service
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-18 · `ui-workspace` exposes `openSession`/`openWorkspace`/`forkSession` and now requires the `layout` service

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that inject the `uiWorkspace` service or drive session
  and workspace switching.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `UiWorkspace` gains `openSession(sessionId)`,
  `openWorkspace(workspaceId, beforeOpen?)` and `forkSession(sessionId)`; the plugin's inject
  list becomes
  `['slots','sessions','workspaces','locale','remote','remote.directoryPicker','layout']`,
  and `dsh.client.inject`/devDependencies must add
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout`. `openSession` calls `ctx.layout.selectPanel(null)`, so
  selecting a Session returns the main column to the Conversation — including re-selecting the
  current Session — and the panel selection is transient (a reload resets it).
  `ui-conversation` now routes its navigation through `uiWorkspace.openSession/openWorkspace`
  (draft migration happens in the synchronous prepare callback).
- **Migration recipe**: add the `layout` dependency and inject entry; drive programmatic
  Session/workspace switching through `uiWorkspace` instead of manipulating layout state
  yourself; expect the main panel to reset to the Conversation.
- **Verification**: the plugin activates with `layout` injected; switching Session shows the
  Conversation even when a custom panel was selected; `forkSession` opens the fork;
  re-selecting the same Session still resets the panel.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-workspace/src/client/navigation.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-workspace/src/client/navigation.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-workspace/src/client/index.ts` (inject list)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-workspace/src/client/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-workspace/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-workspace/package.json) · [alpha.2 `ui-conversation/src/client/apply.ts` (navigation calls)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/apply.ts)

cards.title: `ChatFileMentions.forClosing` requires `sessionId`; the turn tail switches from produced files to deliverables
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-19 · `ChatFileMentions.forClosing` requires `sessionId`; the turn tail switches from produced files to deliverables

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that implement or call `chatFileMentions`, or read the
  conversation turn tail.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `forClosing(owner)` becomes
  `forClosing(owner: TurnTailOwnerProps, sessionId: SessionId)` — links built when a fork
  inherits history must point at the fork itself. The
  `conversation.chat.turnTail` seat's select changes from `selectProducedFiles` to
  `selectDeliverables` and its render from `ProducedFiles` to `Deliverables` (wrapping
  `PresentedFileCard`/`PresentRow`); the "Files changed" row now lists only successful
  file-tool mutations while final deliverables come from the `present` tool
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-08](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)). `ui-deliverables` adds `presentedOpen`/
  `presentedHost` hooks, `openPresented(sessionId, seq, index, action)` and
  `PresentedPath`/`presentedForClosing` (the last declaration for a path wins).
- **Migration recipe**: pass the Session id to `forClosing`; read deliverables from the new
  hooks instead of scraping the turn tail; do not expect presented files to appear in
  "Files changed".
- **Verification**: the two-argument `forClosing` call compiles and fork links resolve to the
  fork Session; a presented file renders as a deliverable card and opens through
  `openPresented`; "Files changed" no longer lists presented-but-untouched files.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-chat/src/client/contract/slots.ts` (`forClosing(owner, sessionId)`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-deliverables/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-deliverables/src/client/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-deliverables/src/client/turn-deliverables.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-deliverables/src/client/turn-deliverables.ts) · [alpha.1 `ui-chat/src/client/contract/slots.ts` (one-argument `forClosing`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (file delivery)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

cards.title: browser-only third-party libraries move from `dependencies` to `devDependencies` across the client packages
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-20 · browser-only third-party libraries move from `dependencies` to `devDependencies` across the client packages

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: authors publishing Web Client plugins and anyone reasoning about the client
  install graph.
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging surface); #5 where the moved libraries are imported.
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: `packages/client/AGENTS.md` rewrites rule 5 to "only Host runtime libraries
  require installation dependencies" and extends rule 3 so that workspace **and third-party**
  client imports belong in `devDependencies`. Around twenty client packages consequently move
  their browser-only libraries: `ui-primitives` drops its entire `dependencies` block
  (shiki + `@shikijs/langs`, anser, the micromark/mdast family, react/react-dom), and
  zustand/immer, lexical, clsx, picomatch, `@tanstack/react-virtual`, `diff` and
  `use-sync-external-store` move in `client-store`, `ui-conversation`, `ui-dockkit`,
  `ui-trajectory`, `ui-renderer`, `ui-sidebar-right` and others. The installed graph gets
  smaller and the browser artifact self-contained (inlined into `lib/client.js` or merged by
  the host's Vite build); a consumer that relied on a plugin's `dependencies` to provide
  React or lexical must now declare it. `ui-primitives` also documents that it imports no
  Cordis runtime.
- **Migration recipe**: when publishing a client plugin, keep browser-only implementations in
  `devDependencies` (inlined or left as bare imports for the host build) and keep only Host
  runtime libraries in `dependencies`; declare peer/runtime libraries your consumers must
  provide, and re-check `knip`-style dependency policies.
- **Verification**: `npm view <pkg> dependencies` shows the shrink for the listed packages;
  the built `lib/client.js` still resolves its bundled imports; a standalone consumer that
  needs React declares it itself.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `packages/client/AGENTS.md` (rules 3 and 5)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/AGENTS.md) · [alpha.2 `ui-primitives/package.json` (empty `dependencies`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/package.json) · [alpha.2 `ui-dockkit/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-dockkit/package.json) · [alpha.2 `ui-primitives/README.md` (no Cordis runtime)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/README.md)

cards.title: `ctx.documentPreviews` registry + keyed slot `sidebar.right.tab.document`; preview reads are text-paged or byte-complete
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-21 · `ctx.documentPreviews` registry + keyed slot `sidebar.right.tab.document`; preview reads are text-paged or byte-complete

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that want to render their own document previews in the
  right sidebar.
- **Touchpoints**: #5, #3
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: the renamed preview package now provides a registry and a keyed session slot:
  `ctx.documentPreviews.register({ id, extensions, priority?, title, loading: 'text-pages' |
  'bytes-complete', wrap? })` plus a body registered in `sidebar.right.tab.document` under the
  same `id`. Matching prefers extension over the builtin, then the longer suffix, then
  registration order; the body receives `{ resourceAddress, content: {kind:'text'|'bytes'},
  wrap }` with `useTabInfo`/`useResource`. Text/code/Markdown stream through the paged `read`
  path; PDF/HTML/images use `readAll` full bytes, so the Host's `maxFileBytes` applies and an
  over-limit file is refused (never truncated). HTML runs in a `sandbox="allow-scripts"` Blob
  iframe that packs referenced local `.js`/`.css` (4 MiB per file / 32 MiB total / 64 files).
  `loadPage`/`reloadPages` gain an optional `observedVersion` fifth parameter, and `loadAll`/
  `reloadAll` appear.
- **Migration recipe**: register previews through the registry instead of forking the
  package; pick `loading` from the content type; pass `observedVersion` so a stale page can be
  detected and reloaded.
- **Verification**: a registered extension renders its component in the right sidebar; a file
  above the cap fails with the Host's `too-large` error; HTML preview scripts execute inside
  the sandboxed iframe.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/document/registry.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/document/registry.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/document/contract.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/document/contract.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/index.ts` (`ctx.documentPreviews`, `tab.document`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/face.ts` (`observedVersion`, `loadAll`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/face.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md)

cards.title: `CommandUiSpec` gains `ActionSpec` for commands that run a client callback without submitting
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-22 · `CommandUiSpec` gains `ActionSpec` for commands that run a client callback without submitting

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that register command UI decorations.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: `CommandUiSpec` becomes `PopupSelectSpec | ActionSpec`; an `action` command
  (`kind: 'action'`) runs a client callback on a bare invocation — it consumes the token and
  neither submits a message nor triggers the attachment rejection path. The `/feedback`
  dialog is the first-party consumer. `PopupSelectSpec` and `ActionSpec` are exported by name,
  and the service exposes `invoke` (replacing `openPopup`).
- **Migration recipe**: use `kind: 'action'` for UI-only flows that must not submit (dialogs,
  navigation, local toggles); update call sites from `openPopup` to `invoke`.
- **Verification**: invoking the decorated command opens the UI without appending a user
  message; attaching a file to that invocation does not produce the submit-path rejection.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-commands/src/client/contract.ts` (`ActionSpec`, `CommandUiSpec`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/contract.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-commands/src/client/service.ts` (`invoke`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/service.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-commands/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (`/feedback`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)
