cards.title: `dsh-command-feedback` adds `./types`/`./remote`/`./typert` subpaths and a `sessionFeedback` Host Remote
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-23 · `dsh-command-feedback` adds `./types`/`./remote`/`./typert` subpaths and a `sessionFeedback` Host Remote

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Host plugins and compositions that record feedback or import feedback
  types.
- **Touchpoints**: #3, #2
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-feedback`'s `exports` map gains `./types`,
  `./remote` and `./typert` (previously only `.`), adds `zod@^4.4.3` as a dependency and
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol` as a peer/dev pair, and widens `files`. A
  `SessionFeedbackService extends TypertRemoteService` registers `ctx.sessionFeedback` with
  `@Remote('record')`, taking `{ sessionId, text?, category? }` and returning
  `{ok:true, value:{recorded:true}}` or
  `{ok:false, error:{code:'session-not-found', sessionId}}`. The Host-side
  `recordFeedback(session, entry)` and the `feedback/record` payload change are carded in
  [DSH-0.1.5-A2-05](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md).
- **Migration recipe**: import the feedback types from `./types` instead of reaching into
  internals; provide the `typert-protocol` peer when composing the Host; call the Remote from
  client code rather than the removed client-side `rate`/`clear` calls
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-17](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)).
- **Verification**: `ctx.sessionFeedback.record` resolves on the Host; an unknown Session
  returns the documented `session-not-found` error; the subpath imports compile; the package
  installs with its new `zod` dependency.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `feedback/command-feedback/package.json` (subpath exports, `zod`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/feedback/command-feedback/package.json) · [alpha.2 `feedback/command-feedback/src/index.ts` (`SessionFeedbackService`, `@Remote('record')`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/feedback/command-feedback/src/index.ts) · [alpha.2 `feedback/command-feedback/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/feedback/command-feedback/src/types.ts)

cards.title: guide tabs lose `description`; sidebar-right default pages seed lazily and the last tab's close collapses the column
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-A2-24 · guide tabs lose `description`; sidebar-right default pages seed lazily and the last tab's close collapses the column

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that register right-sidebar tab types or rely on the
  sidebar's default-page and close behavior.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: guide entries in the tab registry drop the required
  `description: () => string` — the capsule renders icon + title only, and
  `ui-sidebar-files` deletes its `guide.description` locale key. `makeGuideTab(id, title)` is
  replaced by `defaultSeed(tabs)` (the default page follows the registered guide count and
  throws for an unregistered kind). `createSurface()` becomes zero-argument and starts
  empty/collapsed with no tab, seeding the default page on the first expand; `canCloseTab` and
  `soleDockedTab` are exported, a sole docked guide cannot be closed (the kit hides its close
  routes), and closing another last tab collapses the whole column and clears the layout; an
  empty pane's `split()` is a no-op; page tabs always dedupe inside their target pane while
  `revealIfOpened: false` only lets resource tabs open repeatedly. The
  `conversation.session.header.corner` seat no longer reserves width when its occupant renders
  nothing (the tool area moves to the edge; CSS margin 12 px → 8 px), and the
  `sidebar.right.pane.tab.title` seat is now used by guide/files/document-preview tabs for
  live titles.
- **Migration recipe**: remove `description` from your guide tab definitions; do not assume a
  pre-seeded guide page (it appears on first expand); use `canCloseTab` when you render your
  own close affordance; stop depending on the corner's reserved width.
- **Verification**: typecheck passes without `description`; a collapsed sidebar opens on the
  seeded page; the sole guide has no close route; a corner whose occupant renders nothing
  collapses so the tool area reaches the edge.
- **Source**: [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts` (no `description`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/seed.ts` (`defaultSeed`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/seed.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-right/src/client/stores.ts` (`canCloseTab`, `soleDockedTab`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/stores.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts` (corner no longer reserves)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [alpha.2 `ui-sidebar-right/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md) · [0.1.5-alpha.2 release notes (Web plugin panel API)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2)

---

## Corridor status

- Second card set for the 0.1.5 line, covering `dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.1 → dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2`
  (1471 changed files, +30992/−11202; the previous edge is the much wider
  `0.1.3-alpha.2 → 0.1.5-alpha.1`). Status `draft`: no real-host cold start or browser
  entry was run (Windows-only analysis environment). The 12 client/packaging cards
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-13](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md) … [DSH-0.1.5-A2-24](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)) were
  gathered by a dedicated client-face pass and each was re-checked against the tags.
- **Distribution note**: `0.1.5-alpha.2` **is on npm** — `alpha` dist-tag,
  published 2026-09-09T14:41Z (registry checked the same day); `latest`/`next` remain
  `0.1.2-rc.1`, so npm users on the alpha channel get this build. Sources stay pinned to the
  git tags; the npm side independently corroborates the rename
  (`…-sidebar-textpreview` stops at alpha.1) and the `fs-ext` note
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-10](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)).
- **Corrections to the previous edge's file surface**: the `workspaceFiles`/`file`
  resource contract changed again ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-01](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md),
  [DSH-0.1.5-A2-02](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)) — the first parameter is a scope lookup rather
  than an Agent, the client resource is `WorkspaceFileStat`, `reload`/`restat` are gone,
  `absolute` addresses no longer authorize Host calls, and **reads are no longer confined
  to the workspace root**. The previous edge's file-surface card
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A1-11](v0.1.5-alpha.1.md), landed via PR #197) should be read together with
  these two cards for any target at or above `0.1.5-alpha.2`.
- **Corrections to the previous edge's client surface**: the `rightbar` slot changed scope
  again and `ui-layout`'s service/store was rewritten
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-13](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)); the deliverables turn-tail seat still exists but
  its select/render changed ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-19](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)); the
  `conversation.session.header.corner` seat no longer reserves width
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-24](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)); and `client-resources` lost `reload`

- Verified unchanged in this window (do not misreport): `packages/core/agent` and
  `agent-loop`, `core/system-prompt` (API), `core/tools`, `goal/*`, `compaction/*`,
  `context/*`, `subprocess/*`, `apps/cli/src/**`, `vendor/**`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`,
  `engines` (`^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`), and the `ctx.agent` removal / `Inbox` / `SurfaceOp`
  / PTC / `token-meter` changes from the previous edge. Also stable in this window:

  source, the `ui-slots` `SlotCore` API, `native/*`, and `apps/desktop*` (version bumps
  only).
- Not carded (listed): settings localization/accessibility, the Composer placeholder fix,
  the Windows folder-picker foreground fix, custom provider Base-URL validation/normalization
  in the settings UI (client-side; the provider-level `error` field it surfaces is carded in
  [DSH-0.1.5-A2-06](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)), the plugin-inventory subtitle/id display fix, the
  experimental `webworker-runtime` `fs.chmod`/`stat(bigint)` additions, the `apps/web` Vite
  preview-emit change, and the experimental Agent Teams profile UX beyond the npm-install
  note. The `/feedback` detailed-submission UI **is** carded
  ([DSH-0.1.5-A2-17](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md), [DSH-0.1.5-A2-22](v0.1.5-alpha.2.md)).

  `fs-ext` build" has no counterpart in the tag diff (`fs-ext` appears nowhere in

*Changes to host UI, performance, or non-carded surfaces do not prove the absence of API
or behavior impact. When a real plugin is affected, add a primary source and a
reproducible verification record.*

cards.title: the base bundle's default agent model id moves to `deepseek-flash`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-RC1-01 · the base bundle's default agent model id moves to `deepseek-flash`

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: every base-backed profile composition (the `dsh-base` first patch layer),
  and any deployment, preset, wrapper, snapshot, or document that names `deepseek-v4-flash`
  as the default model.
- **Touchpoints**: none (composition/config surface).
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the base bundle's `agent-default-model` row declares `model: deepseek-flash`
  where `dsh-v0.1.5-alpha.2` declared `deepseek-v4-flash`. New Sessions therefore start on
  DeepSeek-V41-Flash; a profile that previously inherited the default changes model
  silently, while a configuration file that names a model explicitly keeps winning.
- **Migration recipe**: grep your own profile patch, `agent.cordis.yml` presets, fixtures,
  and docs for `deepseek-v4-flash`. Accept `deepseek-flash` where the default is fine, or
  pin the previous id with your own `agent-default-model` row (`model: deepseek-v4-flash`).
  Do not assume the target gateway serves the new id yet — see DSH-0.1.5-RC1-02.
- **Verification**: `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` shows the effective
  `agent-default-model` row; open a fresh Session and confirm the model id in its header,
  then run one real turn.
- **Source**: [rc.1 `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) · [rc.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.1)

cards.title: `deepseek-flash` joins the adapter catalog with image input, in-history system prompts, and no gateway probe
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-RC1-02 · `deepseek-flash` joins the adapter catalog with image input, in-history system prompts, and no gateway probe

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: deployments on the `deepseek-official` provider, model-discovery consumers
  (`ctx.llm.listModels`), model pickers and settings UIs that enumerate the catalog, and
  plugins whose assumptions about the default catalog are text-only.
- **Touchpoints**: none (catalog/config surface).
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: the adapter's default catalog gains `deepseek-flash` (display name
  `DeepSeek-V41-Flash`, `inputModalities: ['text', 'image']`, a 1,000,000-token context
  window, and `systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'`), while `deepseek-v4-flash`,
  `deepseek-v4-pro`, and `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` stay. Two consequences matter for
  plugin and deployment authors:
  - the default entry is registered **without probing gateway availability**, so requests
    fail with `INVALID_REQUEST` on a gateway that has not enabled the id;
  - only the default `deepseek-flash` entry declares `systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'`;
    any other model needs that declaration in an explicit `models` list, and a value other
    than `in-history` fails at load.
- **Migration recipe**: do not hardcode the previous catalog list; read it through
  `ctx.llm.listModels('deepseek-official')` where you display or select models. If your
  gateway cannot serve `deepseek-flash`, declare your own `models` list or pin the previous
  default model. If your deployment relies on dynamic system prompts without rewriting the
  leading message, declare `systemPromptUpdate: 'in-history'` on the models you route to.
- **Verification**: `ctx.llm.listModels('deepseek-official')` lists four entries; one real
  Chat Completions turn against `deepseek-flash` succeeds on a gateway that serves it; a
  turn on an `in-history` model appends a changed system prompt after the cached history
  instead of rewriting the leading system message.
- **Source**: [rc.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts) · [rc.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/README.md)

cards.title: document renderers receive a required `scrollportRef` prop
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-RC1-03 · document renderers receive a required `scrollportRef` prop

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that register a `sidebar.right.tab.document` renderer.
- **Touchpoints**: #1 for source patches touching the renderer signature; none otherwise
  (client slot props).
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the document renderer props gain
  `scrollportRef: RefCallback<HTMLElement>`. A renderer that ignores it keeps the shared
  body as the scroll owner, and a TypeScript build fails until the new member is accepted.
- **Migration recipe**: attach the callback to the element that actually scrolls
  (`<div ref={scrollportRef}>`) and call it with `null` when your renderer stops owning the
  scrollport; pass `null` outright when the shared body should stay the owner.
- **Verification**: open a long document in the right sidebar, scroll it, switch tabs and
  return — the reading position survives; a renderer that never scrolls does not disturb
  the shared body's behavior.
- **Source**: [rc.1 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/document/contract.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/src/client/document/contract.ts)

cards.title: sidebar guide entries gain an optional `description`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-RC1-04 · sidebar guide entries gain an optional `description`

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: plugins that register a `sidebar.right.tab.*` type or its guide entries.
- **Touchpoints**: none (client slot props).
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: `SidebarRightGuideEntry` gains optional `description?: () => string`, read
  fresh on every use like `title`, so switching the interface language needs no
  re-registration. The guide renders it only while its entry list stays light and falls
  back to titles alone when crowded, so a type must still stand on its title. `icon` now
  falls back to the guide's cube placeholder when omitted. The builtin `files` tab adopts
  both (its definition moved from `definition.ts` to `definition.tsx` and added two locale
  keys).
- **Migration recipe**: add `description: () => t('guide.description')` (with the matching
  locale key pair) where one line explaining what opens helps the user; keep the title
  self-sufficient and keep thunked copy so language changes need no re-registration.
- **Verification**: open the right sidebar guide in a Session with several tab types and
  switch the UI language — title and description update without a reload; a crowded guide
  degrades to titles only.
- **Source**: [rc.1 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts) · [rc.1 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/src/client/definition.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/src/client/definition.tsx)

cards.title: the feedback surface's injected contract loses `toggle`/`acknowledge` and reshapes `openDialog`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-RC2-01 · the feedback surface's injected contract loses `toggle`/`acknowledge` and reshapes `openDialog`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that take over the `feedback` entry (order 10) of
  `conversation.chat.assistant-actions` or the `feedback-dialog` entry (order 2) of
  `conversation.input.overlay`, or that import `MessageFeedbackInjected`,
  `FeedbackDialogInjected` or `MessageFeedbackToggleResult` from
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-message-feedback/client`.
- **Touchpoints**: #1 for source or type patches against the injected surface; #5 for
  plugin code that drives the feedback controller programmatically.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the injected faces introduced one edge earlier do not survive this one:
  - `MessageFeedbackInjected.toggle(messageId, rating)` → `retract(messageId, rating)`,
    and its meaning narrows: it no longer writes the opposite judgment, it deletes only
    while the committed rating still matches and otherwise resolves to a no-op
    (`{ ok: true }`). The return type is `MessageFeedbackActionResult`, not
    `MessageFeedbackToggleResult`.
  - `MessageFeedbackInjected.openDialog(messageId)` → `openDialog(messageId, rating)`;
    the dialog must now know which judgment it is confirming.
  - `MessageFeedbackInjected.acknowledge()` is gone. `FeedbackDialogController` raises
    the acknowledgement itself after a successful submission and `acknowledge()` is now
    private.
  - `MessageFeedbackToggleResult` is no longer exported from the package's `client`
    entry, so an existing import fails to resolve.
  - `FeedbackDialogInjected` gains `dismissFailure()`, and `FeedbackDialogTarget`'s
    message branch gains a required `rating`.
  Seat names, orders and props-interface names are unchanged, so a plugin that only
  renders the seats still builds — the break lands on the injected members.
- **Migration recipe**: for a control that offers both judgments, branch on the committed
  item first and call `retract(messageId, rating)` only while
  `current(messageId)?.rating === rating`; otherwise call `openDialog(messageId, rating)`
  and let the dialog's Submit write the record. Drop every `acknowledge()` call, replace
  the removed result type with `MessageFeedbackActionResult`, stop reading a returned
  rating, and wire `dismissFailure` where the failure toast should be retired. This card
  supersedes the `openDialog(messageId)` / `acknowledge()` / `toggle`-result half of the
  `ui-message-feedback` card on the `0.1.5-alpha.1 → 0.1.5-alpha.2` edge, which is still in
  an open pull request: read the two together, and take this file's shape once both land.
- **Verification**: typecheck passes against `retract` and
  `openDialog(messageId, rating)`; clicking a recorded rating retracts it without opening
  the dialog; clicking an unrecorded rating opens the dialog and writes nothing until
  Submit; no stale import of `MessageFeedbackToggleResult` remains.
- **Source**: [rc.2 `packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/slots.ts) · [rc.2 `.../src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/index.ts) · [rc.2 `.../src/client/controller.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/controller.ts) · [rc.2 `.../src/client/dialog.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/dialog.ts)

cards.title: both ratings confirm in the dialog, and a failed submission becomes a warning toast
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-RC2-02 · both ratings confirm in the dialog, and a failed submission becomes a warning toast

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that mount, replace or drive the feedback surface
  (`ui-message-feedback`), and every test or automation that assumed a Like records on
  click.
- **Touchpoints**: #5; #3 for end-to-end suites that assert the feedback flow.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: on rc.1 a Like recorded immediately (one `messageFeedback` mutation plus
  the acknowledgement toast) and only a Dislike opened the dialog. On rc.2 one
  `choose(rating)` path serves both buttons: a matching committed rating retracts, any
  other state opens the dialog with that rating, and the record is written on Submit —
  an empty draft is still a valid submission. Submission failure also moves out of the
  dialog body: the draft stays open and its code is published as a 6-second warning
  toast in the same `conversation.input.overlay` entry, retired through
  `dismissFailure()`; a failure resets the acknowledgement toast sequence, and the two
  toasts never render together.
- **Migration recipe**: if you drive the surface programmatically, stop treating Like as
  fire-and-forget — expect a dialog target with `rating` instead. If you assert the flow
  in tests, replace "Like records immediately" with "Like opens the dialog, Submit
  records" and assert the failure copy on the toast rather than inside the modal. Keep
  the dialog's category/note contract unchanged; it is the same seven chips.
- **Verification**: a Like opens the dialog and records nothing until Submit; a recorded
  Like and a recorded Dislike both retract on click; a forced submission failure keeps
  the draft, shows the warning toast for its hold window, and closes it through
  `dismissFailure` without closing the modal.
- **Source**: [rc.2 `packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/MessageFeedbackActions.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/MessageFeedbackActions.tsx) · [rc.2 `.../src/client/FeedbackDialog.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/FeedbackDialog.tsx) · [rc.2 `.../src/client/dialog.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/src/client/dialog.ts) · [rc.2 `.../README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-message-feedback/README.md)

cards.title: `FileTypeIcon`'s code-category artwork is replaced by the design export and renders through injected markup
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-RC2-03 · `FileTypeIcon`'s code-category artwork is replaced by the design export and renders through injected markup

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that render `FileTypeIcon` (deliverables cards, file
  chips, custom file lists) or that assert on its rendered markup, and any plugin that
  bundles a copy of the code-file glyphs.
- **Touchpoints**: #5; #3 for DOM or string snapshots of the icon.
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: the 477-line hand-written artwork `switch` inside `CodeFileIcon` is gone
  (the file now adds 14 lines). Each of the 48
  `CodeFileType` categories now comes from the new `code-file-icon-artwork.ts` table,
  which is injected with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` after replacing a
  `__DSH_CODE_ICON_INSTANCE__` token with a per-instance `dsh-code-icon-*` id, so
  gradients and clip paths stay independent between two icons of the same type. The
  artwork itself is a new internal design export, recorded with `sha256` digests in
  `code-file-icon-artwork.manifest.json` (which also lists the deliberately excluded
  `markdown`), so every code and configuration icon changes appearance — a light plate,
  thinner brand artwork and a baked palette. `FileTypeIcon` keeps its props and its
  selection rule (`isCodeFileType(type) ? CodeFileIcon : glyph(type)`), so only the
  traditional set — the generic and `code` glyphs, Excel, folder, HTML, image, Markdown,
  PDF, PPT, video and Word — still honours `--dsh-file-type-icon-color`; the 48 artwork
  categories, letterform ones such as `css`/`env`/`ini`/`toml`/`yaml` included, keep their
  embedded palette.
- **Migration recipe**: no source change is needed to keep rendering. If you assert on
  the output, normalize or drop the instance id (`dsh-code-icon-*` differs per render)
  and refresh the expected markup. If you re-implement the code glyphs, keep using the
  public `FileTypeIcon` instead of copying SVG paths — the artwork is a closed set that
  the package test pins to `CODE_FILE_TYPES`, and its table is reachable but internal
  through the package's `./src/*` subpath.
- **Verification**: a code file yields the same artwork through `kind` and through `path`
  classification once instance ids are normalized; no snapshot contains a hardcoded
  `dsh-code-icon-` id; `--dsh-file-type-icon-color` still tints a traditional glyph such
  as the generic file.
- **Source**: [rc.2 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/CodeFileIcon.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/CodeFileIcon.tsx) · [rc.2 `src/code-file-icon-artwork.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/code-file-icon-artwork.ts) · [rc.2 `src/code-file-icon-artwork.manifest.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/code-file-icon-artwork.manifest.json) · [rc.2 `tests/code-file-icon.client.spec.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/tests/code-file-icon.client.spec.tsx)

cards.title: the completed-turn footer and file-section spacing become a documented contract
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.5-RC2-04 · the completed-turn footer and file-section spacing become a documented contract

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that contribute to the `conversation.chat.turnTail`
  hole — the seat `ui-deliverables` occupies and declares against `ui-conversation` — or
  that render their own file list into a finished turn's tail.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: the two built-in tail renderers stop carrying their own 16px top margins
  and lean on the chat flow instead. `ui-chat` gives the action footer a `margin-top:
  4px` and documents "the completed-turn action footer starts 20px below the preceding
  prose or extension content"; `ui-deliverables` drops both of its own top margins to 4px
  (the produced-files row and the delivery grid), zeroes the grid's again when a
  produced-files row already precedes it
  (`data-after-produced-files`), and documents the chain "first file section 20px below
  the closing prose, a following explicit-delivery section 16px below the row, action
  footer 20px below the last file section". The delivery grid also tightens: 10px gaps,
  60px cards, a 40px icon frame holding a 20px `FileTypeIcon`, 13px filename and 10px
  secondary text.
- **Migration recipe**: do not add your own 16px spacer at the top of a turn-tail
  contribution — the flow supplies the separation, and a second consecutive file section
  keeps the 16px offset instead. Re-check hardcoded row heights, icon sizes and grid gaps
  against the 20px/40px frame when your contribution sits in the same tail.
- **Verification**: with `ui-deliverables` and one custom contribution mounted, the
  closing prose → first section → second section → action footer gaps read 20/16/20px at
  default zoom, and a long delivery list stays inside its own section instead of pushing
  the footer away.
- **Source**: [rc.2 `packages/client/ui-chat/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-chat/README.md) · [rc.2 `ui-chat/src/client/chat/TurnTailNodeView.module.css`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/chat/TurnTailNodeView.module.css) · [rc.2 `packages/client/ui-deliverables/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-deliverables/README.md) · [rc.2 `ui-deliverables/src/client/Deliverables.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-deliverables/src/client/Deliverables.tsx)

cards.title: `agent/session-start` is deleted and `agent/created` becomes a serial, awaited initialization event carrying `source` and `signal`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-01 · `agent/session-start` is deleted and `agent/created` becomes a serial, awaited initialization event carrying `source` and `signal`



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Host plugins that listen for agent/session lifecycle — hook bridges, session-start context injectors, goal drivers, agent-team recovery, custom agent registries — and any plugin that calls `ctx.agents.register()` / `ctx.agents.announce()` or implements an agent factory with `publish()`.
- **Touchpoints**: #2 for the internal event name that disappeared and the lifecycle event whose payload changed; #3 for the `agents` service methods whose signatures and return types changed.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: on rc.2 a plugin could subscribe to the session lifecycle with `ctx.on('agent/session-start', ({ agent, source }) => …)`, declared as `'agent/session-start'(this: Scoped<Agent>, payload: { agent: Agent; source: SessionStartSource }): void` at `packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts:316` (`@mode emit` at `:314`). On 0.1.6-alpha.1 that event **does not exist**: a whole-snapshot text search finds 90 `agent/session-start` occurrences in rc.2 and only 6 in 0.1.6-alpha.1, all of them prose inside `.agents/notes/archived/…`. A listener left on the old name therefore never runs and produces no error and no warning, so a hook that injected context at session start silently stops injecting. The replacement is the same event, widened: `'agent/created'(this: Scoped<Agent>, payload: { agent: Agent })` with `@mode emit` at `packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts:258` becomes `'agent/created'(this: Scoped<Agent>, payload: { agent: Agent; source: SessionStartSource; signal?: AbortSignal }): undefined | Promise<undefined>` at `:261` with `@mode serial` at `:259`, documented as "Listeners run in order and are awaited before creation resolves. AgentLoop holds queued input until all listeners finish. A throw or rejection fails creation and skips later listeners." The service side moved in step: `register(agent: Agent): () => void` at `packages/core/agent/src/index.ts:434` (which fired and forgot, only warning on a returned rejection at `:553`) becomes `register(agent: Agent): ReturnType<Context['effect']>` at `:434` with `await this.announce(agent, 'startup')` at `:437`; `announce(agent: Agent): void` at `:533` becomes `async announce(agent: Agent, source: SessionStartSource, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>` at `:534`, dispatching `await this.ctx.serial(entry.carrier, 'agent/created', { agent, source, …signal })` at `:547`. In the loop, `publish(source: SessionStartSource): AgentHandle` at `packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts:218` is now `publish(source: SessionStartSource): Promise<AgentHandle>` at `:217`, and the pair `loopCtx.agents.announce(agent)` at `:670` plus `emitAgentEvent(loopCtx, agent, 'agent/session-start', { source })` at `:675` collapses to `await loopCtx.agents.announce(agent, source, abort.signal)` at `:674`. The generated routing table lost its entry too: `'agent/session-start': args => (args[0] as Record<string, unknown>)['agent'],` at `packages/core/scope/src/scoped-events.generated.ts:21` has no counterpart in the new `:11-:37` block.
- **Migration recipe**: replace every `ctx.on('agent/session-start', ({ agent, source }) => …)` with `ctx.on('agent/created', ({ agent, source, signal }) => …)`; the in-repo reference migration is `packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:205` → `:202`, which now reads `ctx.on('agent/created', async ({ agent, source, signal }) => {`, with the same change in `packages/hooks/hooks-codex/src/index.ts:187` and `packages/goal/goal/src/index.ts:255`. If the handler did asynchronous work (reading hook config, running a hook subprocess, injecting context), make it `async` and `await` that work: the dispatch is serial and awaited now, and a rejection fails agent creation instead of being logged and dropped, so a handler that must not break creation has to catch its own errors. Do not `await agent.whenIdle()` or the owner's disposal inside the listener — that is the documented deadlock. If the plugin registers agents by hand, `await` the value `ctx.agents.register(agent)` returns before using the agent. If the plugin implements its own agent factory, `publish()` must now return a promise the caller awaits.
- **Verification**: register one `agent/created` listener that records `payload.source` and confirm it observes `'startup'` for `ctx.agentLoop.create(...)` and `'resume'` for `resume(...)`, while a control listener still registered on `agent/session-start` observes nothing. Then make the `agent/created` listener throw and confirm agent creation *rejects*; on rc.2 creation succeeded and the failure was only logged.

cards.title: startup strictness moves to `auditStartupEntries`, the two `assertEntries*` helpers are gone, and a resolved `Loader.create()` no longer proves activation
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-02 · startup strictness moves to `auditStartupEntries`, the two `assertEntries*` helpers are gone, and a resolved `Loader.create()` no longer proves activation



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Host plugins, launchers and profile wrappers that boot or audit a config tree through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot`, and any plugin or preset code that assumed a failed sibling row would roll the tree back.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for the app-boot exports a launcher calls and the new `pluginPackages` service; #5 for the plugin-registration contract that a partially applied tree now leaves in place.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: on rc.2 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` exported two audit helpers — `export function assertEntriesLoaded(ctx: Context, binName: string): void` at `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:685` and `export async function assertEntriesActivated(ctx: Context, binName: string): Promise<void>` at `:722`, the latter documented as "Reject a settled Loader tree when an enabled entry failed or remains inactive". On 0.1.6-alpha.1 both symbols are deleted and the only audit is `export async function auditStartupEntries(ctx: Context, binName: string, warn: (line: string) => void = line => void process.stderr.write(line)): Promise<void>` at `:818`, whose policy is much narrower: `const requiredStartupEntryIds = new Set<string>(['agent-loop', 'webserver', 'modules', 'connection', 'headless-runner', 'acp', 'sdk-jsonrpc-server'])` at `:711`; a listed id that is absent or `disabled` is ignored, a listed id that is present, enabled and inactive rejects startup (`:832-:834`), every other inactive entry produces one `warning` line and leaves successful siblings running (`:831`), and a throwing `disabled` expression counts as an entry failure rather than as disabled (`:758-:761`). The Loader itself is non-transactional again, so an activation failure leaves the new options and a failed fiber in place — the decision note says plainly that "awaiting `Loader.create()` alone does not establish activation". The preset mount path changed shape for the same reason: `export function inactiveRows(tree: EntryTree): string[]` at `packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts:302` is now `export async function inactiveRows(tree: EntryTree): Promise<string[]>` at `:301`. The same module also gained a new public service: `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:56-:60` now exports `PluginPackages`, `type PluginPackage`, `type PluginPackagesConfig`, declared on the context as `pluginPackages: PluginPackages` (`packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/service.ts:16-:21`, `super(ctx, 'pluginPackages')` at `:68`) with `packageOf(specifier, parentURL)` at `:98`.
- **Migration recipe**: replace `assertEntriesLoaded(ctx, bin)` + `assertEntriesActivated(ctx, bin)` with one `await auditStartupEntries(ctx, bin)`, optionally passing a `warn` sink to capture optional-failure warnings instead of letting them go to stderr. Stop treating a resolved `Loader.create()` / `boot()` as "everything activated": if the plugin needs a specific sibling capability, audit the entries it cares about *after* settlement, the way the preset mount path does with `await inactiveRows(tree)`. Do not depend on rollback after a rejected plugin candidate — re-check the tree after a config edit and report the failure visibly instead of assuming the previous generation came back. Where the plugin needs package metadata, use `ctx.pluginPackages.packageOf(specifier, parentURL)` rather than requiring a `./package.json` export or walking `node_modules` by hand.
- **Verification**: boot a profile whose root config holds one enabled row that fails to activate and confirm boot rejects with a `required startup failure:` diagnostic when the row id is in the list, and only writes a `warning:` line when it is not — with the other rows still active in the second case. Add a row that injects the renamed service and confirm the diagnostic names it as `pending (waiting for services: …)` rather than silently succeeding.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts#L700-L835`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts#L700-L835) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/service.ts#L16-L108`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/service.ts#L16-L108) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts#L295-L330`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts#L295-L330) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-09-consumer-owned-startup-strictness.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-09-consumer-owned-startup-strictness.md) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-09-09-nontransactional-loader.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-09-09-nontransactional-loader.md) · [dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts#L685-L785`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts#L685-L785) · [dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts#L296-L305`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/preset/agent-presets/src/mount.ts#L296-L305)

cards.title: `Session.eventAt()`, `Session.snapshotEvents()` and `Session.ownEvents()` are deprecated and new production calls are prohibited
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-03 · `Session.eventAt()`, `Session.snapshotEvents()` and `Session.ownEvents()` are deprecated and new production calls are prohibited



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Host plugins that read Session history — projection, export and query plugins, title generators, telemetry, custom compaction or fork logic — and any plugin whose build runs the repository lint rules.
- **Touchpoints**: #2 for the session-history read contract and the persistent events it exposes; #3 for the `ctx.sessions` service methods.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the three readers still exist and still work, but on 0.1.6-alpha.1 they carry an explicit prohibition and the repository enforces it with `typescript/no-deprecated`. `packages/core/session/src/index.ts:627` now reads `@deprecated Existing logic may remain unmigrated for now, but new calls are prohibited.` above `eventAt(seq: SessionSeq): SessionEvent | undefined {` at `:632`; the same tag sits at `:640` above `snapshotEvents(fromSeq: SessionLogOffset = SessionLogOffset(0), toSeqExclusive: SessionLogOffset = this.seq): readonly SessionEvent[] {` at `:646` and at `:659` above `ownEvents(): readonly SessionEvent[] {` at `:663`. On rc.2 those same three methods are at `:621`, `:633` and `:648` with no `@deprecated` tag anywhere in the file. Nothing changes at runtime yet — the decision states the current implementation "still retains the complete event sequence in memory" — but the prohibition is a forward-looking contract: the storage direction will stop keeping the whole sequence resident, and the deprecation is how that dependency is bounded. A plugin that re-exports or wraps these three names under an alias is explicitly prohibited too, and a plugin that reads history in a hot path will be the one that breaks when the residency guarantee ends.
- **Migration recipe**: for "what state does this session have now", read the registered projection instead of scanning history, and for user-requested history use the explicit asynchronous paged read path rather than `snapshotEvents()` over the whole log. Where a complete historical sequence is genuinely required (forking, migration, invariant checks), keep the call and add a line-scoped waiver comment naming the reason — the repository's own callers do exactly that, e.g. `// oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-deprecated -- Existing Session history read; migration deferred.` in `packages/api/session-controller/src/index.ts`, `packages/api/session-controller/src/history.ts`, `packages/session/session-projection/src/index.ts` and `packages/core/session/src/invariant.ts`. Do not add an alias or thin wrapper that re-exposes synchronous historical access, and if the plugin publishes its own reader with one of these names, rename it — the lint allowance covers only the three exact names.
- **Verification**: run the plugin's lint/typecheck and confirm no unwaived `eventAt`, `snapshotEvents` or `ownEvents` call remains in production source (test files are exempt; other deprecated names are not). Then exercise the projection path that replaced a call and confirm the resumed session renders the same state the history scan produced before.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/core/session/src/index.ts#L622-L666`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/index.ts#L622-L666) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-09-deprecate-synchronous-session-event-reads.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-09-deprecate-synchronous-session-event-reads.md) · [dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/core/session/src/index.ts#L613-L651`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/core/session/src/index.ts#L613-L651)

cards.title: `ctx.sessions.registerMessageProjection()` is new, and an event that rewrites message content is refused without a registered pure interpreter
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-04 · `ctx.sessions.registerMessageProjection()` is new, and an event that rewrites message content is refused without a registered pure interpreter



- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: Host plugins that declare a `SessionEventMap` event changing the content of an existing message, and detached or offline readers (exporters, replay harnesses, query plugins, browser-safe validators) that fold a session log themselves.
- **Touchpoints**: #2 for the event-declaration contract and the required-on-read inventory; #3 for the `ctx.sessions` registration method and the detached `foldSurface`/`deriveEventMessage` entry points; #5 for the registration-as-effect pattern.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: rc.2 has no message-projection concept at all: `packages/core/session/src/surface.ts:182` declares `export interface SurfaceFoldResult`, `:487` declares `export function foldSurface(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): SurfaceFoldResult`, and `:92` declares `export function deriveEventMessage(event: SessionEvent): Message | null`. On 0.1.6-alpha.1 Session owns a registry: `packages/core/session/src/index.ts:925` adds `registerMessageProjection(projection: SessionMessageProjection): () => Promise<void>` on the `ctx.sessions` store, throwing `session message projection "<type>" is already registered` for a second owner (`:926-:928`), with `get messageProjections(): readonly SessionMessageProjection[]` at `:914` for detached callers. The definition is `export interface SessionMessageProjection<T extends SessionEventType = SessionEventType>` at `packages/core/session/src/surface.ts:35`, requiring `type: T` (`:37`) and a pure `project(event: SessionEvent<T>, context: SessionMessageProjectionContext): ReadonlyMap<SessionSeq, Message>` (`:46`); the context (`:23`) carries `nodes`, `events`, `baseSeq` and `messages`. The fold signature widened to `foldSurface(events: readonly SessionEvent[], projections: readonly SessionMessageProjection[] = [])` at `:544`, and `SurfaceFoldResult` (`:214`) gained `projectedMessages: ReadonlyMap<SessionSeq, Message>` (`:220`) and `readonly contentGeneration: number` (`:230`); `deriveEventMessage` (`:119`) gained a second parameter `projectedMessages?: ReadonlyMap<SessionSeq, Message>` (`:121`). The sharp edge is the refusal: `planSurfaceEvent` throws `session event "<type>" requires a message projection; load its owning plugin or supply its projection definition` when the event type is in the generated inventory `MESSAGE_PROJECTION_EVENT_TYPES` (`packages/core/session/src/known-event-types.ts:82-:85`, currently `{'image/offload'}`), and a definition removed after use invalidates cached reads with `session message projection "<type>" was removed or replaced; restore the session with its owning plugin`. `packages/core/session/src/index.ts:28` newly re-exports `SessionMessageProjection` and `SessionMessageProjectionContext` from `./surface.ts`.
- **Migration recipe**: if the plugin owns an event that rewrites an existing message's content, tag its `SessionEventMap` member with `@messageProjection`, implement a pure `SessionMessageProjection` (`type` plus `project()`), and register it from the plugin's own fiber with `ctx.sessions.registerMessageProjection(def)`, keeping the returned disposer so unloading the fiber removes it. Never mutate the input messages: validate the complete durable payload first and return immutable copies keyed by the original `SessionSeq`, because a throw from `project()` rejects the append. If the plugin folds a log offline, pass the definitions explicitly to `foldSurface(events, projections)` and read `result.projectedMessages`; do not rely on any process-global registry or import-time registration. If it reconstructs a single message, pass the fold's `projectedMessages` map as the second argument to `deriveEventMessage(event, projectedMessages)`.
- **Verification**: append the plugin's event to a live session and confirm derivation reflects the change with the projection registered, then throws the `requires a message projection` error with the registration removed; dispose the registering fiber and confirm further derivation refuses with the `was removed or replaced` error instead of silently reverting to the original content. Repeat the offline path by folding the same log through `foldSurface(events, [def])` and comparing `projectedMessages` against the live result.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/core/session/src/index.ts#L911-L933`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/index.ts#L911-L933) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L22-L47`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L22-L47) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L467-L481`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L467-L481) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L544-L558`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L544-L558) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-11-plugin-owned-message-projections.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-11-plugin-owned-message-projections.md) · [dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L92`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L92) · [dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L487`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/core/session/src/surface.ts#L487)

cards.title: the vendored Loader and HMR config-reload contract reverts to non-transactional: `ctx.hmr.registerConfig()` and `hmr/config-update-failed` are deleted, the update helpers stop reporting failures, and update listeners must be synchronous
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-05 · the vendored Loader and HMR config-reload contract reverts to non-transactional: `ctx.hmr.registerConfig()` and `hmr/config-update-failed` are deleted, the update helpers stop reporting failures, and update listeners must be synchronous


- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile overlays and tooling that watch or hot-reload `cordis.yml` / `cordis.patch.yml`; host plugins that call `ctx.hmr.registerConfig(...)`, that mutate entries through `ctx.loader` (`EntryTree` / `EntryGroup` / `Entry`), that `await fiber.update(config)`, or that subscribe to `internal/update`, `loader/patch-context` or `hmr/config-update-failed`.
- **Touchpoints**: #2 for the two internal waterfall event signatures and the deleted failure event; #3 for the `hmr` service method that no longer exists and for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot`'s replacement; #4 for the watched patch file and its failure reporting; #5 for the entry/HMR registration lifecycle.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the vendored config-reload path reverts to the pinned non-transactional Loader, and the surface an author compiles against moved without a version bump — `@deepseek-ai/cordis` stays `4.0.2`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader` `1.0.3`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-hmr` `1.0.17` and `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include` `1.0.7` at *both* tags, so nothing in a dependency range signals the change. `ctx.hmr.registerConfig(filename, refresh)` — `async registerConfig(filename: string, refresh: () => Promise<void> | void): Promise<() => Promise<void>>` at `vendor/hmr/src/index.ts:134` on rc.2 — is deleted; the new `Hmr` class has no such method, and the `'hmr/config-update-failed'(filename: string, error: Error)` event declared at `:29` (`@mode parallel`) and dispatched by `await this.ctx.parallel('hmr/config-update-failed', filename, error)` at `:312` is gone too, because the new watcher only logs. Exact-path watching moved to app-boot: `export async function watchConfig(ctx, filename, options: ChokidarOptions, refresh) : Promise<() => Promise<void>>` at `packages/boot/app-boot/src/watch-config.ts:36`, consumed by `watchUserPatches` (`packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:269`, which reads `ctx.get('hmr')` at `:265` only for `hmr.config`). The failure semantics changed more broadly: `Fiber.update()` at `vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts:748` dropped its `return`, so the JSDoc goes from "@returns the update waterfall result; the default restart returns a promise. @throws when validation, an update listener, or the restarted plugin fails" to "@returns nothing; the restart runs behind the `internal/update` waterfall" — `await fiber.update(config)` now resolves immediately even when the restart later fails. `EntryTree.await()` at `vendor/loader/src/config/tree.ts:42` lost its `@throws a settled fiber failure, or an aggregate when several fibers failed` and its per-entry `entry._await()` loop, so `await ctx.loader.await()` resolves on a tree containing a failed entry. `EntryGroup.update()` at `vendor/loader/src/config/group.ts:48` now assigns `this.data = config` before anything applies and swallows each sibling's failure with `.catch((error) => { this.ctx.logger.error(error) })` at `:58`, replacing the old single-throw / `AggregateError(failures, 'loader entries failed to apply')` plus full rollback (`'loader entry rollback failed'`, `'duplicate loader entry id: …'`); `EntryTree.remove()`, `EntryGroup.remove()` and `EntryGroup.stop()` all changed from `async`/`Promise<void>` to plain `void` methods. Entry update itself is eager: `vendor/loader/src/config/entry.ts:115` mutates `this.options` in place (`// step 1: update options` at `:118`, then `// step 2: execute`, then `// step 3: check if options are changed`) instead of building a candidate and committing it, and `updateError`, `replaceKeys`, `_disposing` and `_dispose()` are deleted, so the `failed to <import|dispose|apply|rollback> loader entry <id> (<name>): <detail>` wrapper no longer exists and an import failure is logged and swallowed (`this.ctx.logger.error(error)` at `:180`). Finally, `'loader/patch-context'(entry: Entry, next: () => void): void` and `'internal/update'(this: Fiber, config: any, noSave: boolean, next: () => void): void` both replaced a `void | Promise<void>` signature, and Include's `ConfigFileError` (`failed to <read|parse|validate> config file <path>`) became `TypeError('config file must be a top-level array of entries: <path>')`. The practical consequence is that nothing in the Loader call chain rejects on a failed plugin candidate any more — `fiber.update()`, `tree.await()`, `group.update()` and `entry.init()` all resolve — so a consumer that awaits an update and reports success keeps a broken tree silently unless it audits afterwards, which is what `watchUserPatches` learned to do (`packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:281-285`: await every `entry.fiber?.await()`, then `inactiveEntries(ctx)`, then throw an `activationDiagnostic(binName, 'warning', …)`).
- **Migration recipe**: stop calling `ctx.hmr.registerConfig(...)` and stop listening for `hmr/config-update-failed` (it can never fire) — use `watchConfig` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` with `ctx.get('hmr')!.config`, or own a watcher, and keep the returned disposer. After any programmatic entry mutation, config reload or live patch-layer edit, do not read rejection as failure or resolution as success: settle with `await ctx.loader.await()`, then `await Promise.allSettled([...ctx.loader.entries()].map(entry => entry.fiber?.await()))`, then inspect `entry.fiber` / `entry.fiber.state`. Make `internal/update` and `loader/patch-context` listeners synchronous and call `next()` synchronously — an `async` listener now contributes an unawaited promise instead of gating the update, while returning without `next()` still vetoes the restart. Drop reliance on rollback (after a rejected candidate the entry keeps the new options and the failed fiber stays in the tree; a later valid edit is the only recovery path) and stop `await`ing `EntryTree.remove()`, `EntryGroup.remove()` or `EntryGroup.stop()` for disposal. Update any code that matched the removed diagnostics: `failed to <stage> loader entry <id> (<name>): …`, `failed to <read|parse|validate> config file <path>`, `loader entries failed to apply`, `loader entry rollback failed` and `failed to roll back loader entry move <id>` are gone, and the raw module-resolution or parse error reaches the caller instead.
- **Verification**: boot a config tree containing one row whose module fails to import and confirm the audit reports it for that id, that `await ctx.loader.await()` *resolves* rather than rejecting, and that `entry.fiber` is `undefined` for that row while its siblings stay active. Then write a non-array into the watched `cordis.patch.yml` and confirm the process logs `config reload at … failed; keeping the running tree`, keeps serving the previous tree, and fires no reload-failure listener — where rc.2 rejected the update and rolled the tree back.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `vendor/hmr/src/index.ts#L20-L23`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/vendor/hmr/src/index.ts#L20-L23) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/boot/app-boot/src/watch-config.ts#L36-L80`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/watch-config.ts#L36-L80) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts#L260-L295`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts#L260-L295) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts#L728-L750`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/vendor/cordis/src/fiber.ts#L728-L750) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `vendor/loader/src/config/entry.ts#L115-L189`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/vendor/loader/src/config/entry.ts#L115-L189) · [0.1.6-alpha.1
