cards.title: `session-log-deepseek` now uploads the canonical session log by default
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-06 · `session-log-deepseek` now uploads the canonical session log by default



- **Type**: privacy
- **Applies to**: every deployment that mounts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-log-deepseek` (the shipped base bundle does), every plugin or overlay that composes or overrides that row, and plugin test compositions that build real provider requests.
- **Touchpoints**: #4 for the profile/composition state that decides the policy; #6 for the outbound request channel the contribution rides on; #2 for the durable acceptance event it now writes.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: on rc.2 the row was opt-in: `packages/session/session-log-deepseek/src/index.ts:45` read `enabled: z.boolean().default(false)` and the JSDoc at `:155` said `@param config - validated opt-in configuration.` On 0.1.6-alpha.1 the same line reads `enabled: z.boolean().default(true)` and the JSDoc at `:156` is `@param config - validated configuration.`; `apply` still early-returns on `config.enabled !== true` at `:159`, so only the default changed. A row that merely omits `enabled` therefore flips from "upload nothing" to "upload", and the decision note spells out what leaves the machine: the complete unaccepted canonical log suffix, "including message text, tool arguments and results, workspace paths, and feedback, to the resolved DeepSeek endpoint or configured gateway", with request bodies growing substantially. The plugin deliberately does not inspect test-runner or snapshot environment variables, so a plugin's own suite that assembles a real request can start shipping a `dsh_session_log` field without any test-visible signal. The shipped headless and ACP corpus patches and the Web scaffold explicitly disable upload, so only those profiles stay off; OTel remains independent and disabling OTel does not disable this contribution.
- **Migration recipe**: decide the policy per deployment and write it down explicitly — add `enabled: false` to the `session-log-deepseek` row in every profile, overlay or test composition that must not contribute the log, which is exactly what the headless, ACP and Web corpora do. Set `enabled: false` in the plugin's own test compositions too instead of inheriting the new default. If the plugin reads or forwards request bodies, expect a new `dsh_session_log` extension field and a new durable `session-log-deepseek/delivery-accepted` event in the session log; if it renders or diffs session events, account for that record. Do not treat `DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` or an OTel opt-out as covering this contribution.
- **Verification**: run one ordinary DeepSeek turn in the profile and confirm the outgoing request carries `dsh_session_log` and the session log gains a `session-log-deepseek/delivery-accepted` record with a `throughSeq`; then set `enabled: false`, repeat the identical turn, and confirm both the field and the record are absent.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/session/session-log-deepseek/src/index.ts#L37-L46`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/session/session-log-deepseek/src/index.ts#L37-L46) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/session/session-log-deepseek/src/index.ts#L154-L160`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/session/session-log-deepseek/src/index.ts#L154-L160) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-14-session-log-upload-default.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-14-session-log-upload-default.md) · [dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/session/session-log-deepseek/src/index.ts#L45`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/session/session-log-deepseek/src/index.ts#L45)

cards.title: The code-runtime seam is renamed to ptc-runtime and split into `resolve`/`run`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-07 · The code-runtime seam is renamed to ptc-runtime and split into `resolve`/`run`



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that register a program-execution provider (`ctx.codeRuntime` implementors), plugins that call `ctx.ptcRuntime`, and any plugin or profile that names the runtime packages/rows (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-code-runtime-python`, row ids `code-runtime`).
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (the seam is a Cordis service looked up by name), #5 (`run_code` schema/controls are registered from the provider's capabilities), #7 (the provider launches and governs a child process).
- **Action level**: required
- **Symptoms**: the service registration moved `codeRuntime` → `ptcRuntime` and the abstract execution method was split in two. OLD: `interface Context { codeRuntime: CodeRuntime }` and `export abstract class CodeRuntime extends Service` with `super(ctx, 'codeRuntime')` and `abstract run(request: CodeRunRequest): Promise<CodeRunResult>` (`packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/index.ts:88-92,101,122,134`). NEW: `interface Context { ptcRuntime: PtcRuntime }`, `export abstract class PtcRuntime extends Service` with `super(ctx, 'ptcRuntime')`, `abstract resolve(request: PtcRunRequest): PtcRunSpec` and `abstract run(spec: PtcRunSpec): Promise<PtcRunResult>` (`packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime/src/index.ts:91-95,104,134,143,150`). Types renamed wholesale: `CodeRunRequest{program,bindings,signal?}` → `PtcRunRequest{program,bindings,cwd?,timeoutMs?: number|null,sandboxPolicy?,signal?}` plus the new `PtcRunSpec{cwd: string; timeoutMs: number|null}` (`packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime/src/types.ts:73-106` vs `packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/types.ts:73-89`); `CodeRunResult{value?,logs,error?}` → `PtcRunResult{sandbox?: PtcRunSandbox,value?,logs,error?}` (`:144-162` vs `:115-131`); `PtcRunFailure.kind` gains `'protocol'` and `'sandbox-unavailable'` (`:134` vs `:105`). The service also grows capability getters `executionInstructions`, `sandboxMode`, `timeout` (`packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime/src/index.ts:125,128,131`) that the `run_code` tool reads: `timeoutMs` appears only when `runtime.timeout !== undefined`, and `sandbox_permissions` + `justification` only when `runtime.sandboxMode !== undefined` (`packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts:100-118`), with the failure text now appending `File sandbox: <mode>[; enforcement: …][; operation denied]` (`:712`). Provider packages renamed: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread` (exports `./worker` → `lib/worker.cjs`) → `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node` (exports `./process` → `lib/process.js`), class `WorkerThreadCodeRuntime`/`isolation='worker-thread'`/Config `{computeMs:60000,maxWallMs:600000,…}` → `NodePtcRuntime`/`isolation='process'`/`static inject=['fs','subprocess','sandbox','sandboxPolicy']`/Config `{timeoutMs:120000,maxTimeoutMs:600000,maxOutputBytes:67108864,maxOldGenerationSizeMb:512,maxMessageBytes:134217728,maxPendingCalls:128,graceMs:3000,nodeExecutable,bootstrapPath}` (`packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:238-247` vs `packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node/src/index.ts:52-64`). `dsh-tools` now demands a sandbox policy for a confined runtime and names the new package in its load error: `mode "…" requires a PTC runtime — load a ctx.ptcRuntime implementation (e.g. @deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node)` (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1025-1028`) instead of `… a code runtime … (e.g. @deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread)` (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:1009-1012`). Deliberately unchanged: `CodeRunFailedError` (`packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts:166,169`), `RUN_CODE_NAME`, the `run_code` tool name and `code` argument.
- **Migration recipe**: (1) swap every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime*` dependency/import for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node`, including `peerDependencies` and profile rows; (2) rename identifiers `CodeRuntime→PtcRuntime`, `CodeRunRequest→PtcRunRequest`, `CodeRunResult→PtcRunResult`, `CodeRunFailure→PtcRunFailure`, `CodeBinding*→PtcBinding*`, `CodeJsonValue→PtcJsonValue`, `CodeSdkLanguage→PtcSdkLanguage`, `ctx.codeRuntime→ctx.ptcRuntime`; (3) implementors: move defaulting/validation into `resolve(request): PtcRunSpec` (absolute `cwd`, capped `timeoutMs` or explicit `null`, resolved `sandboxPolicy`) and keep `run(spec)` default-free, rejecting unsupported explicit choices; (4) re-key old provider config (`computeMs`/`maxWallMs` have no successor — use `timeoutMs`/`maxTimeoutMs`); (5) update any profile patch that targets row id `code-runtime` to `ptc-runtime`, because a patch whose id is not found only warns (`patch: entry %C not found`, `vendor/include/src/index.ts:111`) and silently does nothing.
- **Verification**: mount the provider and assert `ctx.get('ptcRuntime')` is defined; run a program and assert `logs`/`value`; run a file-writing program outside the workspace and assert `result.sandbox.denied === true` and the failure message carries the `File sandbox: …` suffix; assert an over-budget program yields `kind: 'timeout'` and a host without a usable backend yields `kind: 'sandbox-unavailable'` (never an unconfined run).
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime/src/index.ts#L91-L150), [`packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime/src/types.ts#L73-L162), [`packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node/src/index.ts#L52-L64), [`packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts#L100-L118), [`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1025-L1028), [`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml#L368-L369) — old state: [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/index.ts#L88-L134), [`packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/types.ts#L73-L131), [`packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts#L238-L247), [`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1009-L1012), [`packages/bundle/headless/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/bundle/headless/cordis.patch.yml#L20-L21)

cards.title: `SandboxProvider.confine` is now asynchronous and cancellation-aware
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-08 · `SandboxProvider.confine` is now asynchronous and cancellation-aware



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: every plugin that implements a sandbox provider (`ctx.sandbox`) and every plugin that calls `ctx.sandbox.confine(...)` directly.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (Cordis service contract), #7 (the confined argv is what the consumer spawns).
- **Action level**: required
- **Symptoms**: OLD `abstract confine(argv: readonly string[], policy: SandboxPolicy): ConfinedArgv` (`packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts:175`) with no cancellation parameter; NEW `abstract confine(argv: readonly string[], policy: SandboxPolicy, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ConfinedArgv>` plus `@param signal - cancellation while the provider resolves the policy and runner.` (`packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts:172,176`). The shipped local provider follows: `confine(argv, policy): ConfinedArgv` (`packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts:315`) → `async confine(argv, policy, signal?): Promise<ConfinedArgv>` (`:316`), which now also canonicalizes `policy.workspaceRoot`. Every consumer awaits the call and threads its signal, e.g. `packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts:188-189`, `packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/index.ts:108`, `packages/api/terminal-controller/src/index.ts:328`, `packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node/src/index.ts:224`. The same edge adds a public diagnostics module re-exported from the seam: `export { classifyRunnerFailure, isRunnerSpawnFailure, matchesSignature } from './diagnostics.ts'` (`packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts:181`; definitions `packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/diagnostics.ts:33,65,96`), and the self-inspection catalog publishes the new signature string (`packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts:1436`). `SandboxMode`, `SandboxPolicy`, `ConfinedArgv`, `SandboxEnforcement`, `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` and `SandboxUnavailableError` are unchanged, and fail-closed behavior is still required.
- **Migration recipe**: (1) change each `extends SandboxProvider` method to `async confine(argv, policy, signal?): Promise<ConfinedArgv>` and call `signal?.throwIfAborted()` before resolving a runner; (2) convert every call site to `await ctx.sandbox.confine(argv, policy, signal)`, passing the caller's signal when one exists; (3) keep throwing `SandboxUnavailableError` (code `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`) instead of returning unconfined argv when the mode cannot be enforced; (4) if you previously classified runner spawn failures by string matching, prefer the newly exported `classifyRunnerFailure` / `isRunnerSpawnFailure` / `matchesSignature`.
- **Verification**: `await ctx.sandbox.confine(['true'], { mode: 'read-only', workspaceRoot })` resolves with `argv` + `enforcement`; passing `AbortSignal.abort(reason)` rejects with `reason` before any spawn; on a host with no backend it rejects with `SandboxUnavailableError` and no command runs; assert the spawned argv is the confined argv, not the original.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts#L164-L181), [`packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/diagnostics.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/diagnostics.ts#L33-L96), [`packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts#L316), [`packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts#L188-L189) — old state: [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts#L164-L176), [`packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/index.ts#L315)

cards.title: `ShellExecutor.start` returns a Promise
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-09 · `ShellExecutor.start` returns a Promise



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that implement `ctx.shell` (shell executors) and plugins that start background commands through `ctx.shell.start(...)`.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (Cordis service contract), #7 (subprocess launch, stdout ownership, cancellation during preparation).
- **Action level**: required
- **Symptoms**: OLD `abstract start(spec: ShellExecSpec): ShellProcess`, documented as "Start a background process and return its handle immediately." (`packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:94-99`); NEW `abstract start(spec: ShellExecSpec): Promise<ShellProcess>`, documented as "Prepare a background process asynchronously and publish its live handle… cancellation or setup failure rejects." (`packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:96-101`). `run` gains the same preparation semantics: foreground work now runs "under the resolved timeout" and `@throws` "on preparation failure or caller cancellation before process publication" (`:87-94` vs `:86-92`), and `ShellRunResult.exitCode` is documented `null` also when "preparation expired", not only on signal death. In-tree consumers wrap the call in an async path: `signal => ctx.shell.start(ctx.shell.resolve({ ...request, signal }))` (`packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:369`, `packages/shell/tool-pwsh/src/index.ts:385`), and `terminal-bash` awaits confinement before publishing (`packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/index.ts:108`).
- **Migration recipe**: (1) implementors: declare `start(spec): Promise<ShellProcess>`, `await` preparation (sandbox confinement, helper launch) before publishing, reject (never resolve) on cancellation or setup failure, and keep observing `spec.signal` throughout preparation; (2) consumers: `const proc = await ctx.shell.start(ctx.shell.resolve({ ...request, signal }))` and move post-start work into the continuation; treat rejection as "no process was published" so there is nothing to kill; (3) handle `exitCode === null` for preparation-timeout outcomes as well as signal deaths.
- **Verification**: with a provider whose confinement is delayed, assert no `ShellProcess` is observable before preparation completes, that aborting during preparation rejects and leaves no orphan process, and that a normal start still yields a handle whose `readOutput`/`kill` behave as before.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts#L87-L101), [`packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts#L369), [`packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/index.ts#L108) — old state: [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts#L86-L99)

cards.title: Subprocess providers must implement `terminalEnvironment()`, and may now serve a control channel
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-10 · Subprocess providers must implement `terminalEnvironment()`, and may now serve a control channel



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that implement a subprocess backend (`ctx.subprocess`); additionally, plugins whose child processes need the new control channel (PTC/Node runtime, workflow).
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (Cordis service contract), #7 (spawn/stdio layout — fd 7 is a new inherited descriptor).
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
  (required for a `SubprocessRuntime` implementation, since the new abstract method has no
  default; honoring `stdio.control` is conditional on wanting the PTC Node runtime to run on
  your provider.)
- **Symptoms**: NEW abstract method `abstract terminalEnvironment(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SubprocessTerminalEnvironment>` (`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:138-143`) has no OLD counterpart — OLD declared only `resolveExecutable`, `spawn`, `spawnTerminal` (`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts:131,144,153`). The new result type is `interface SubprocessTerminalEnvironment { platform: 'posix' | 'windows'; defaultShell?: string }` (`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts:205-211`), consumed by `const environment = await subprocess.terminalEnvironment(signal)` (`packages/api/terminal-controller/src/shells.ts:17`) and implemented by `packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/index.ts:247` and `packages/ssh/subprocess-ssh/src/index.ts:266`. The same edge adds an optional control channel: `interface SubprocessStdio { stdin; stdout; stderr; control?: 'pipe' }` (`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts:62-69`, OLD had no `control` at `:62-65`) and `readonly control: Duplex | undefined` on the handle (`:174-175`, OLD handle at `:165-190` had no such member). A new package subpath `"./control"` exports `SUBPROCESS_CONTROL_FD = 7`, `SUBPROCESS_CONTROL_ENV = 'DSH_SUBPROCESS_CONTROL'` and `openInheritedControlChannel(): Duplex` (`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/control.ts:7,10,19`); `subprocess-local` also gains `"./output"` exposing `OutputCollector` and `prepareManagedProcessBinding` (`packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/output.ts:40,57`). First in-tree user: `stdio: { stdin:'ignore', stdout:'pipe', stderr:'pipe', control: 'pipe' }` and a hard failure when `handle.control === undefined` (`packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node/src/index.ts:236-240`).
- **Migration recipe**: (1) add `async terminalEnvironment(signal?)` to your `SubprocessRuntime` subclass returning `{ platform: 'posix' | 'windows' }` (plus `defaultShell` when resolvable) and honor the signal; (2) plain `spawn` consumers need no change — `control` is absent unless requested; (3) to support the PTC Node runtime, honor `stdio.control === 'pipe'`: create a separate duplex byte channel, expose it as `handle.control`, place it at descriptor 7 in the child (POSIX preserves fd 7 across exec; Windows resolves it through the CRT startup descriptor table, keeping 3–6 closed), and set `DSH_SUBPROCESS_CONTROL=pipe` in the child environment — never share stdout/stderr with the protocol; (4) bound and validate every control frame (bytes are model-authored and untrusted) and keep the endpoint open until the host closes it, so a late binding reply cannot race an `EPIPE` against an already-completed program; (5) a child consumes the channel with a single `openInheritedControlChannel()` call from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess/control` before executing untrusted code.
- **Verification**: spawn with `stdio.control: 'pipe'` and assert `handle.control` is a connected duplex, that a child-first write reaches the host without a prior host write, and that `terminate()`/`waitForExit()` still prove range quiescence while one endpoint is paused; for `terminalEnvironment`, assert the platform value and that an aborted signal rejects.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts#L138-L143), [`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts#L62-L69), [`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/control.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/control.ts#L7-L23), [`packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/output.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/output.ts#L40-L57), [`packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node/src/index.ts#L236-L240) — old state: [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/index.ts#L120-L153), [`packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/subprocess/subprocess/src/types.ts#L62-L65)

cards.title: The workflow engine provider is `workflow-ptc`, requires a PTC runtime and sandbox policy, and drops `disposeGraceMs`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-11 · The workflow engine provider is `workflow-ptc`, requires a PTC runtime and sandbox policy, and drops `disposeGraceMs`



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins/profiles that mount or configure a `ctx.workflowEngine` provider.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (service composition: the engine now injects two more services), #7 (the engine executes scripts in a sandboxed Node process instead of a worker thread).
- **Action level**: required
- **Symptoms**: the provider package was replaced: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread` (class `WorkerThreadWorkflowEngine`, `static inject = ['subagents']`, `packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/src/index.ts:112-113`) → `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc` (class `PtcWorkflowEngine`, `static inject = ['subagents','ptcRuntime','sandboxPolicy']`, `packages/workflow/workflow-ptc/src/index.ts:102-103`), and the new provider fails loud at load when the wrong runtime is mounted: `if (ctx.ptcRuntime.language !== 'typescript') throw new Error('workflow-ptc requires the Node TypeScript PTC runtime')` (`:117`). Its config drops `disposeGraceMs`: OLD `Config { provider, maxConcurrentAgents, maxTotalAgents, maxItemsPerCall, syncTimeoutMs, disposeGraceMs }` with `disposeGraceMs: z.natural().default(5000)` (`packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/src/index.ts:32-49,115-122`) → NEW the same set without `disposeGraceMs` (`packages/workflow/workflow-ptc/src/index.ts:32-43,105-111`). Each run now receives resolved file authority — `runCtx.sandboxPolicy.resolve({ session: request.parent.session })` (`:166`) — and passes `timeoutMs: null` to PTC, disabling PTC's elapsed timer for the run. The shipped composition row changed id and name: `- id: workflow-worker-thread` / `name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread'` (`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:368-371`) → `- id: workflow-ptc` / `name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc'` (`:371-374`). The seam itself is unchanged: `ctx.workflowEngine` and `abstract start(request: WorkflowStartRequest): WorkflowRun` (`packages/workflow/workflow/src/index.ts:156-167` in both trees), as are the `workflow/*` events.
- **Migration recipe**: (1) swap the package name in dependencies and profile rows, and update any patch layer that targets row id `workflow-worker-thread` (a stale id only warns — `patch: entry %C not found`, `vendor/include/src/index.ts:111`); (2) mount a TypeScript `PtcRuntime` provider and a `sandboxPolicy` provider in the same composition, otherwise the engine fiber fails at load; (3) remove `disposeGraceMs` from the engine config — there is no successor; (4) if you relied on worker-thread metering, note the run is now bounded by the VM's `syncTimeoutMs` slice plus the host's sandbox/subprocess rules, with no engine-level elapsed deadline.
- **Verification**: boot a profile with `ptc-runtime-node` + `sandbox-policy` + `workflow-ptc` + `tool-workflow`, run one workflow that starts a child agent, and assert the run settles with a `stopReason`, `workflow/*` events fire in order, a script writing outside the workspace is denied by the OS sandbox (not by the VM), and cancelling the enclosing tool deadline cancels the run and disposes children.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/workflow/workflow-ptc/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/workflow/workflow-ptc/src/index.ts#L102-L174), [`packages/workflow/workflow-ptc/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/workflow/workflow-ptc/package.json#L2), [`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml#L371-L374) — old state: [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/src/index.ts#L32-L122), [`packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/package.json#L2), [`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml#L368-L371)

cards.title: MCP client moves to the 2.0 SDK, bounds server instructions, and exports the tool adapter
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-12 · MCP client moves to the 2.0 SDK, bounds server instructions, and exports the tool adapter



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins/profiles configuring `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`, plugins that imported `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/*` transitively, and authors adapting a foreign MCP transport onto `ctx.tools`.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (service composition — two new optional peers), #5 (tool registration), #6 (MCP stdio/HTTP transport is a custom channel owned by this plugin).
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: (a) SDK swap — OLD `dependencies: { "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.12.0", "zod": "^4.4.3" }` (`packages/mcp/mcp-client/package.json`), NEW `"@modelcontextprotocol/client": "2.0.0"` (line 42) with `zod` demoted to devDependencies; imports move from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js` / `…/sdk/types.js` to `@modelcontextprotocol/client` (`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/connection.ts:1`, `src/tools.ts:1`). Discovery/execution becomes SDK-owned: the hand-rolled uncached `client.request({method:'tools/list'})` cursor loop and `RawCallToolResultSchema` are replaced by `client.listTools(undefined, { cacheMode: 'refresh' })` and `client.callTool(…, { toolDefinition: tool })`. (b) New bounded instructions — NEW config `maxInstructionBytes?: number` on both transport shapes, schema default `DEFAULT_MAX_INSTRUCTION_BYTES = 32_768` (`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/index.ts:73-74,129,139`; `src/connection.ts:48-49`), and a new fail-loud path `if (Buffer.byteLength(instructions) > maxInstructionBytes) throw new Error('${label}: server instructions exceed maxInstructionBytes (${maxInstructionBytes})')` (`src/connection.ts:319-321`). (c) Prompt contribution — the client now calls `registerServerContext(ctx, config.serverName, connection)` (`src/index.ts:182`), which registers into `ctx.mcpResources` and adds a `systemPrompt.section({ name: 'mcp:<server>', interpolate: false, text: () => connection.instructions() })` (`src/server-context.ts:28-39`). (d) New public exports — `export { createMcpToolDefinition } from './tools.ts'` and `export type { McpResult, McpToolDefinitionOptions }` (`src/index.ts:26-27`; `createMcpToolDefinition` at `src/tools.ts:225`, options at `:196`), where OLD only exported `McpResult` (`src/index.ts:20`). (e) New optional peers with `peerDependenciesMeta … optional: true`: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-resources`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` (`package.json:37-38,63-70`).
- **Migration recipe**: (1) a server whose instructions exceed ~32 KiB (or a row with `failOnStartupError: true`) now fails to publish — shorten the instructions or raise `maxInstructionBytes` explicitly; (2) if you imported `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/...`, add `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.0.0` to your own dependencies and move to `listTools`/`callTool`; (3) if you bridge a foreign MCP transport, construct definitions with `createMcpToolDefinition(ctx, { name, rawName, description, inputSchema, outputSchema?, taskRequired?, call })` and register them on `ctx.tools`, leaving validation to the adapter (it throws on `isError` results before image storage); (4) do not assume server instructions reach the model unless `ctx.systemPrompt` is mounted.
- **Verification**: connect a server with 40 KiB instructions under the default config and confirm `server instructions exceed maxInstructionBytes (32768)` (activation rejects with `failOnStartupError: true`), then raise the field and confirm the section text appears in the assembled system prompt; connect a tools-only server and confirm it publishes no tools while still contributing its name.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/index.ts#L20-L27), [`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/connection.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/connection.ts#L319-L321), [`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/server-context.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/server-context.ts#L28-L39), [`packages/mcp/mcp-client/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/mcp/mcp-client/package.json#L29-L70) — old state: [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/index.ts#L20-L72), [`packages/mcp/mcp-client/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/mcp/mcp-client/package.json#L40-L44)

cards.title: New `ctx.mcpResources` service publishes three shared resource tools
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-13 · New `ctx.mcpResources` service publishes three shared resource tools



- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: plugins/profiles that want MCP resource access, plugins that enumerate the tool registry, and plugins implementing their own MCP bridge.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (new Cordis service `mcpResources`), #5 (three conditionally registered model-facing tools + a prompt section).
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: NEW package `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-resources` (absent in OLD) declares `interface Context { mcpResources: McpResourceRuntime }` (`packages/mcp/mcp-resources/src/index.ts:14-18`) and `export class McpResourceRuntime extends Service` with `static inject = ['tools']`, `super(ctx, 'mcpResources')`, `register(server: string, provider: McpResourceProvider): () => void` and `request(server, request, exec)` resolving the provider in the calling agent's scope (`src/index.ts:47-56,80-105,122-126`); the provider contract is `request(request: McpResourceRequest, exec: ToolExecution): Promise<JsonValue>` over `{method:'resources/list'|'resources/templates/list'; cursor?}` and `{method:'resources/read'; uri}` (`:20-34`). `registerResourceTools()` registers exactly three tools — `list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates` (`server` required, optional `cursor`) and `read_mcp_resource` (`server` + `uri` required) — each with `output: { schema: { type: 'json' }, render: renderResourceResult }` (`src/tools.ts:15-61`; renderer `src/render.ts:16`). Visibility is provider-driven: the first provider in a scope registers the tools and the last removal disposes them (`src/index.ts:83-105,108-119`), and caller-visible server names are injected as the literal system-prompt section `mcp-resource-servers` (`:59-71`). `dsh-mcp-client` joins through an optional injection — `ctx.inject(['mcpResources'], (inner) => inner.mcpResources.register(server, connection.resources))` (`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/server-context.ts:29-31`). Shipped profiles mount it once: `- id: mcp-resources` / `name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-resources'` in `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:470-471` and `packages/bundle/sdk-minimal/cordis.patch.yml:94-95`.
- **Migration recipe**: (1) existing plugins need nothing — with no configured MCP server there is no prompt section, no tool schema, no PTC declaration and no PTC binding; (2) to offer resources, mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-resources` in the composition and let each `mcp-client` instance self-register; (3) to supply your own provider, call `ctx.mcpResources.register(serverName, provider)` inside a scope, return the disposer, validate the closed request union, and return lossless JSON; (4) never hardcode the three resource tool names in registry-inspection code — their presence depends on at least one configured provider in scope.
- **Verification**: with no configured server assert the three tools are absent from `ctx.tools` and the prompt has no `mcp-resource-servers` section; configure one server and assert the tools appear and `read_mcp_resource` for an unknown server rejects with `MCP resource server "<name>" is unavailable in this agent's scope` (`src/index.ts:124`); dispose the client and assert the tools disappear while inherited providers survive.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/mcp/mcp-resources/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/mcp/mcp-resources/src/index.ts#L14-L126), [`packages/mcp/mcp-resources/src/tools.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/mcp/mcp-resources/src/tools.ts#L31-L61), [`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/server-context.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/server-context.ts#L28-L39), [`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml#L470-L471)

cards.title: New SSH execution world: `ctx.ssh` plus remote filesystem, subprocess and sandbox providers
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-14 · New SSH execution world: `ctx.ssh` plus remote filesystem, subprocess and sandbox providers



- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: plugins/profiles that must run file, shell, terminal or Node work on a remote POSIX host; plugins that wrap `ctx.fs` / `ctx.subprocess` / `ctx.sandbox` and must keep working when those services are the remote providers.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (one new service plus three providers that replace local services), #4 (path spelling is execution-world absolute; host-path projection is unavailable), #7 (per-stream SSH channels, fd 7 control traffic, disconnection without replay).
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: NEW packages `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ssh`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-ssh`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-ssh`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-ssh` (no `packages/ssh/**` exists in OLD). The connection service is `interface Context { ssh: SshConnection }` with `export class SshConnection extends Service` / `super(ctx, 'ssh')` (`packages/ssh/ssh/src/index.ts:42-47,74`) and a config requiring verified coordinates — `host`, `node`, `helper`, `helperHash`, `workspace`, optional paired `bootstrapPath`/`bootstrapHash`, and defaults `requestTimeoutMs: 30_000`, `maxFrameBytes: 64 MiB`, `maxPending: 128`, `leaseMs: 30_000` (`:17-40,48-54`) — with `readonly ready: Promise<Hello>` awaited through `[Service.init]` (`:57,92`) and a POSIX-client guard (`:75`). Providers: `class SshFileSystem extends FileSystem` with `static inject = ['ssh','sandboxPolicy']` (`packages/ssh/fs-ssh/src/index.ts:20-21`); `class SshSandboxProvider extends SandboxProvider` with `static inject = ['ssh']`, `override async confine(argv, policy, signal?): Promise<ConfinedArgv>` (`packages/ssh/sandbox-ssh/src/index.ts:10-13`) translating every failure into `SandboxUnavailableError` (`:28`); `packages/ssh/subprocess-ssh/src/index.ts` implements the full `SubprocessHandle` including `readonly control: Duplex | undefined` (`:25`) and `override terminalEnvironment(signal?)` (`:266`). `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ssh` additionally exports `./helper`, `./protocol` and `./schemas`, which the provider packages consume (`packages/ssh/subprocess-ssh/src/index.ts:9-11`).
- **Migration recipe**: (1) mount `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ssh` with verified helper coordinates, then mount `dsh-fs-ssh`, `dsh-subprocess-ssh` and `dsh-sandbox-ssh` in place of — not beside — their local counterparts so all consumers share one execution world; (2) compute `helperHash`/`bootstrapHash` from the exact installed artifacts (a mismatch refuses the connection instead of degrading); (3) for remote PTC/workflow, configure a `ptc-runtime-node` row with `nodeExecutable` = `ctx.ssh.nodeExecutable` and `bootstrapPath` = `ctx.ssh.bootstrapPath` (both getters are verified against the remote helper, and the runtime refuses to run without them); (4) keep terminal allocation asynchronous in consumers; (5) treat a lost connection as terminal for pending operations — the providers do not reconnect or replay.
- **Verification**: against a disposable remote host, assert a modified helper fails the digest check; a remote confined Bash command is denied outside the workspace; `handle.control` traffic progresses while the remote stdout channel is paused; and killing the SSH connection fails pending operations instead of replaying them.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/ssh/ssh/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/ssh/ssh/src/index.ts#L17-L104), [`packages/ssh/fs-ssh/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/ssh/fs-ssh/src/index.ts#L20-L27), [`packages/ssh/sandbox-ssh/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/ssh/sandbox-ssh/src/index.ts#L10-L30), [`packages/ssh/subprocess-ssh/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/ssh/subprocess-ssh/src/index.ts#L25-L266)

cards.title: LLM adapter image preparation reports required offloads instead of projecting request images itself
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-15 · LLM adapter image preparation reports required offloads instead of projecting request images itself



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that implement the provider-adapter seam — an `LlmAdapter` subclass registered through `ctx.llm.registerAdapter()` that sends images — and plugins that prepare request images through `ctx.attachments.readImageRequest()`; also `llm/stream` middleware that rewrites `options.messages`.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for the `ctx.llm` adapter registration and the `ctx.attachments` service call; #2 for the `image/offload` decision the new failure triggers.
- **Action level**: required
- **Symptoms**: the adapter-side image vocabulary was replaced, so an adapter that used to shrink a request by dropping images must now fail and let the surface record the omission.
  - On rc.2 `packages/llm/llm/src/content.ts:354` exported `offloadRequestImagesWithPolicy(messages, policy: RequestImageOffloadPolicy)` (policy interface at `:213`, exported pure helper `offloadedImagePrefixCount()` at `:319`) so an adapter could remove the oldest images, substitute placeholders and send a reduced request without telling the log.
  - On 0.1.6-alpha.1 those three symbols are gone. `packages/llm/llm/src/content.ts:311` exports `requiredImageOffload(messages, budget, versionBytes)`, which returns how many *more* oldest retained occurrences must be offloaded, and `:258` exports `projectOffloadedImages(messages, placeholder)`, which renders only occurrences the surface already marked; `offloadedImagePrefixCount()` is private (`:277`) and the budget vocabulary is `LlmImageRequestBudget` at `packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts:341`.
  - The failure vocabulary is new: `IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED_CODE = 'IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED'` at `packages/llm/llm/src/error.ts:172`, the `offloadImages?: number` field on `LlmFailure` at `packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts:57`, carried through `LlmErrorOptions`/`LlmError.failure` at `packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:85-86,125` and accepted by `normalizeLlmFailure()` at `packages/llm/llm/src/adapter-failure.ts:72,79,86` (rejected unless a positive safe integer).
  - The durable mark is `ImageBlock.offloaded?: true` at `packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts:87`: a marked occurrence must reach every route as placeholder text, and `contentHasImage()` (`content.ts:126-137`) still reports it as an image, so a preflight built on it will not skip it.
  - Image pricing changed shape with it: `priceImages(images: readonly ImageAttachmentRef[])` at `packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts:192` on rc.2 became `priceImages(images: readonly ImageBlock[])` at `:206`, and an `offloaded` block prices as its placeholder text with `visualTokens: 0` (reference implementation `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/request-pricing.ts:100-108`).
  - The attachment call an adapter makes to prepare bytes also changed: `ImageRequestPolicy { maxPixels, maxBytes }` at `packages/attachment/attachment/src/types.ts:136` and `readImageRequest(ref, policy: ImageRequestPolicy, signal?)` at `packages/attachment/attachment/src/index.ts:248-250` became `ImageRequestTarget { width, height, maxBytes }` at `types.ts:136` and `readImageRequest(ref, target: ImageRequestTarget, signal?)` at `index.ts:249-251`, with `longEdgeDimensions` newly exported beside `requestImageDimensions` (`index.ts:25`).
  - First-party adapters show the target shape: `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/context.ts:300-315` throws the failure and then projects, and `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/chat-completions/serialize.ts:393-414,433-436` plus `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/images.ts:44,83-91` do the same per protocol.
- **Migration recipe**: delete every use of `offloadRequestImagesWithPolicy`, `RequestImageOffloadPolicy` and `offloadedImagePrefixCount` (grep those three names). Compute each retained occurrence's exact request-version byte length, call `requiredImageOffload(messages, budget, block => bytes)`, and when it returns `n > 0` throw `new LlmError(message, IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED_CODE, { offloadImages: n })` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` instead of removing anything; `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-image-offload` records the selection and the caller retries. Send `projectOffloadedImages(messages, ref => offloadedImageText(ref, access))` so marked occurrences become placeholders and all other occurrences stay untouched. Widen `priceImages` to `readonly ImageBlock[]` and price `offloaded === true` entries as placeholder text. Replace `readImageRequest(ref, { maxPixels, maxBytes })` with `readImageRequest(ref, { width, height, maxBytes })`, deriving the dimensions from `requestImageDimensions(w, h, maxPixels)` or `longEdgeDimensions(w, h, maxEdge)`. If you keep `llm/stream` middleware, preserve `offloaded` marks and never reintroduce offloaded bytes — the runtime only auto-projects files and text-only-model images (`packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:1046-1060`).
- **Verification**: with a route budget of `maxImages: 2` and three retained occurrences, the request must end as a terminal `finish` chunk whose failure has `code === 'IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED'` and `offloadImages === 1`, rather than a silently shortened request. After the owning plugin records one `image/offload` event for the oldest occurrence, the retried body must carry that occurrence's placeholder text and zero image bytes while message ids, attachment ids and every other occurrence are unchanged. `ctx.llm.imageRequestPricing(provider, model).priceImages([retained, offloaded])` must return the same handle/placeholder `text` the serializer produces for both entries.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm/src/content.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm/src/content.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm/src/error.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm/src/error.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/context.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/context.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/attachment/attachment/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/attachment/attachment/src/index.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/llm/llm/src/content.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/llm/llm/src/content.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/attachment/attachment/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/attachment/attachment/src/types.ts)

cards.title: the deepseek-official route defaults to the Anthropic Messages protocol
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-16 · the deepseek-official route defaults to the Anthropic Messages protocol



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: profiles, overlays, bundle wrappers and provisioning scripts that configure the `llm-deepseek` entry or override its endpoint (`baseURL`, `$DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`); plugins that assert, mock, proxy or record the DeepSeek wire format.
- **Touchpoints**: #6 for the wire protocol, request path and headers; #3 for the `llm-deepseek` composition/settings namespace that selects the implementation.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the same provider route and the same default model id now speak a different protocol to a different default endpoint.
  - On rc.2 `Config` (`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:134`) had no protocol field, the endpoint default was `PUBLIC_BASE_URL = 'https://api.deepseek.com'` (`:210`), and the adapter appended a fixed path: `fetch(\`${connection.baseURL}/chat/completions\`, …)` at `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:651` (documented at `:82`).
  - On 0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/config.ts:26-27` adds `protocol?: DeepSeekProtocol` with schema default `'messages'` at `:81`; the type is `DeepSeekProtocol = 'chat-completions' | 'messages'` at `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/types.ts:10`; `MESSAGES_BASE_URL = 'https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic'` is new at `config.ts:106-107` and is exported from the package root alongside `DeepSeekProtocol` (`src/index.ts:13,29`).
  - Resolution changed at `config.ts:292-293`: with no `baseURL` and no `$DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, `protocol: 'messages'` resolves to the Messages root instead of the public API root. `config.ts:207-210` re-validates a widened `protocol` value, and `config.ts:294-299` rejects a Messages `baseURL` that is not a bare HTTP(S) root (`llm-deepseek: Messages baseURL must be an HTTP(S) root without credentials, query, or fragment`).
  - The Messages transport posts to `${baseURL}/v1/messages` and adds an `anthropic-beta` Files header (`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/adapter.ts:122,128`); protocol dispatch lives at `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts:21-39`.
  - `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml` still sets `provider: deepseek-official` / `model: deepseek-flash` unchanged, so an overlay that only overrode `baseURL` at a Chat-Completions-only gateway now posts Anthropic-shaped requests there, and a proxy allowlist or request recorder keyed on `/chat/completions` stops matching.
- **Migration recipe**: grep your profile, overlay, plugin and provisioning scripts for `llm-deepseek`, `deepseek-official`, `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` and `chat/completions`. If you override the endpoint with a Chat-Completions-only URL, add `protocol: chat-completions` to the same config block; if the endpoint is a Messages gateway, keep the default and make sure the URL is a bare root with no query, fragment or embedded credentials. Update mock servers, proxies, allowlists and recorders to expect `POST <base>/v1/messages` with an Anthropic body (plus the `anthropic-beta` header when DeepSeek Files are used). Keep the protocol out of user settings: the design keeps one route id and one settings namespace, so the choice belongs in composition YAML.
- **Verification**: call the plugin's exported `resolveAdapterOptions({}, undefined)` and confirm `baseURL === 'https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic'`; call it with `{ protocol: 'chat-completions' }` and confirm `https://api.deepseek.com`. Point a profile at a local mock and confirm a default run issues `POST /v1/messages` while the explicit `protocol: chat-completions` run issues `POST /chat/completions`. Confirm a `baseURL` carrying a query string now fails resolution with the message above instead of issuing requests.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/config.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/config.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/adapter.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/adapter.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/adapter.ts)

cards.title: DeepSeek request images move onto the v41 token grid and the image exports are renamed
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-17 · DeepSeek request images move onto the v41 token grid and the image exports are renamed



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that import the image helpers or constants from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek`, supply a custom model catalog with `imagePixelBudget`, or consume DeepSeek image token accounting (token-meter readings, compaction pressure); deployments whose gateway has its own image limits.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for the published package exports and the resolved connection data; #2 for the `IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED` retry that replaces silent projection.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: both the projection budget and the token calculator changed, and several root exports were removed or renamed.
  - `DEFAULT_REQUEST_IMAGE_PIXEL_BUDGET = 640_000` (`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/request-pricing.ts:24` on rc.2) is gone. `DEFAULT_REQUEST_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES` went from `1024 * 1024` (`:28`) to `2 * 1024 * 1024` (`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/request-pricing.ts:26`), and `REQUEST_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION = 4096` is new at `:31`.
  - `resolveRequestImagePolicy(model): ImageRequestPolicy` (`request-pricing.ts:36`) became `resolveRequestImageMaxBytes(model)` at `common/request-pricing.ts:39` and `resolveRequestImageTarget(model, source): ImageRequestTarget` at `:53`; an omitted `imagePixelBudget` now means "use `deepSeekRequestImageDimensions`" (`:57-64`) rather than a 640,000-pixel budget.
  - The calculator moved from `MAX_IMAGE_TOKENS = 384` / `MIN_PIXELS = 384 * 384` with an aspect-ratio clamp (`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/image-tokens.ts:17,23` on rc.2) to `MAX_IMAGE_TOKENS = 1024` / `MIN_PIXELS = 544 * 544` with no clamp (`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/image-tokens.ts:21,23`), plus the new `deepSeekRequestImageDimensions(width, height)` at `:132`. Pinned vectors moved from `deepSeekImageTokens(9000, 1) === 113` and `deepSeekImageTokens(16, 8192) === 381` (`tests/image-tokens.spec.ts:35,41` on rc.2) to `deepSeekImageTokens(9000, 1) === 1024`, `deepSeekImageTokens(1, 9000) === 1024` and `deepSeekImageTokens(100, 100) === deepSeekImageTokens(544, 544)` (`tests/image-tokens.spec.ts:34,38,42` on 0.1.6-alpha.1).
  - The default catalog no longer pins a pixel budget: rc.2 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:92-121` gave `deepseek-flash` (`:94-98`) and `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` (`:119`) `imagePixelBudget: DEFAULT_REQUEST_IMAGE_PIXEL_BUDGET` and materialized it during resolution (`:290`); 0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/models.ts:7-13,27-31` omits the field and `src/config.ts:183-188` copies it only when present, so `imagePixelBudget` is now `undefined` for those resolved catalog entries.
  - Root exports of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek` renamed or disappeared: `DEFAULT_REQUEST_IMAGE_PIXEL_BUDGET`, `resolveRequestImagePolicy` and `MAX_CHAT_IMAGE_BYTES` (rc.2 `src/index.ts:68-73`, `src/file-store.ts:11`) are replaced by `REQUEST_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION`, `resolveRequestImageMaxBytes`, `resolveRequestImageTarget`, `deepSeekRequestImageDimensions` and `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` (same 32 MiB value) at `src/index.ts:31-42`, `src/common/file-store.ts:12`. The `Wire*` request types kept their names across the file split (`src/types.ts` on rc.2 → `src/protocols/chat-completions/types.ts`, re-exported at `src/index.ts:51` on 0.1.6-alpha.1).
  - Behavior, documented in `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/README.md:92`: a square request image is kept up to 1302×1302 pixels, a 16:9 source is sent as 1708×961 for the provider's 1708×966 grid, every request image is capped at 4096 pixels per side, and the encoded-byte target defaults to 2 MiB — where rc.2 projected every image under a 640,000-pixel budget.
- **Migration recipe**: grep `DEFAULT_REQUEST_IMAGE_PIXEL_BUDGET`, `resolveRequestImagePolicy` and `MAX_CHAT_IMAGE_BYTES`. Replace `resolveRequestImagePolicy(model)` with `resolveRequestImageTarget(model, ref)` (returns `{ width, height, maxBytes }`) or with `resolveRequestImageMaxBytes(model)` when only the byte target is needed. If you ship a catalog with `inputModalities: ['text', 'image']`, decide explicitly whether the entry inherits the provider grid (omit `imagePixelBudget`) or keeps a total-pixel budget (a positive integer, or `'low'` for 512×512), and add an `undefined` branch before reading `imagePixelBudget` off a resolved entry. Re-pin any image-token expectations: cap 1024 instead of 384, scale-up floor 544×544 instead of 384×384, no aspect-ratio clamp. Rename `MAX_CHAT_IMAGE_BYTES` to `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` and drop the removed constants. Expect larger image prices and earlier compaction pressure wherever you measure context.
- **Verification**: assert `deepSeekImageTokens(100, 100) === deepSeekImageTokens(544, 544)`, `deepSeekImageTokens(9000, 1) === 1024` and `deepSeekImageTokens(1224, 1429) === 959` (0.1.6-alpha.1 `tests/image-tokens.spec.ts:34,38,55`). Against a mock server, confirm a 2000×2000 attachment is requested at 1302×1302 with a ≤2 MiB encoded target and that an 8192-pixel-tall thin image is capped to 4096 on its long edge. Assert `resolveAdapterOptions({}).models.find(model => model.id === 'deepseek-flash')?.imagePixelBudget === undefined`.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/request-pricing.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/request-pricing.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/models.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/common/models.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/README.md) · [rc.2 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/request-pricing.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/request-pricing.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts)

cards.title: token-meter folds image/offload and bumps both context projection state versions to 5
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-18 · token-meter folds image/offload and bumps both context projection state versions to 5



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that read token measurement or persisted session-projection state (`contextBreakdown`, `contextPressure`), fixtures pinned to a projection state version, and compositions that install `@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter` on its own.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for `ctx.tokenMeter` and the session-projection service; #2 for the `image/offload` event the meter now folds.
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: the meter learned one new event and both context projections invalidated their cached state.
  - `packages/llm/token-meter/src/index.ts:253-264` adds `case 'image/offload':`, which maps the event's `{ seq, imageIndexes }` targets onto the current surface nodes and marks those images `{ ...image, offloaded: true }`; rc.2 had no such arm.
  - `stateVersion: 4` became `stateVersion: 5` in `packages/llm/token-meter/src/breakdown-projection.ts:50` and `packages/llm/token-meter/src/usage-projection.ts:175`; `tokenUsage` stays at `2` (`:119`). The wire view is unchanged (`{ systemTokens, toolsTokens, messageTokens }` at `breakdown-projection.ts:24-28,77-80`), so the invalidation hits cached checkpoints only, not the payload shape.
  - `estimateStructuralBlock()` now excludes the mark by destructuring it away for images (`packages/llm/token-meter/src/estimate.ts:30-32`), so an offloaded occurrence keeps the reference-only structural price and the route pricing owns its placeholder.
  - This edge also replaces the durable `ImageBlock` vocabulary the meter reads: `packages/llm/token-meter/src/surface-fold.ts:35` now types `readonly images: readonly ImageBlock[]` where rc.2 had `readonly ImageAttachmentRef[]` (`:36`); the node type is not re-exported from the package root, whose exports are only `types.ts`, `usage-projection.ts` and `breakdown-projection.ts` (`src/index.ts:40-45`), so this bites `src`-path consumers only.
  - The package gained a hard peer for the event's owner: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-image-offload` is now in both `peerDependencies` and `devDependencies` of `packages/llm/token-meter/package.json`, with a type-only import at `src/index.ts:8`.
  - The public measurement shapes are untouched: `src/types.ts` (`TokenMeasurement`, `TokenMeasurementBaseline`, `TokenMeterConfig`) did not change on this edge, and `contextPressure`'s only change is its version.
- **Migration recipe**: re-derive any persisted projection state — a version-4 `contextBreakdown` or `contextPressure` checkpoint is a cache miss on 0.1.6-alpha.1 and must not be asserted as current — and update pinned fixtures to `stateVersion: 5`. If you fold session events yourself for accounting, mirror the new arm: mark the targeted nodes' images offloaded, price them as placeholder text (route pricing returns `visualTokens: 0` for an `offloaded` block, see DSH-0.1.6-A1-15), and keep node identity, message ids and prior usage anchors unchanged. When installing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter` standalone, add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-image-offload` to the composition so the peer resolves. Do not fold the `offloaded` mark into the fixed structural heuristic.
- **Verification**: fold a session containing one `image/offload` event and read the `contextBreakdown` view — the `seq` set and message ids must be identical to the pre-event read while `messageTokens` changes only by the placeholder text price. Request a stale version-4 checkpoint and confirm it is re-derived rather than served. Run `ctx.tokenMeter.measure()` on an image-heavy session after the event and confirm the image price drops without losing the prior usage anchor or re-anchoring the baseline.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/token-meter/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/token-meter/src/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/token-meter/src/breakdown-projection.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/token-meter/src/breakdown-projection.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/token-meter/src/usage-projection.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/token-meter/src/usage-projection.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/token-meter/src/estimate.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/token-meter/src/estimate.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/llm/token-meter/src/surface-fold.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/llm/token-meter/src/surface-fold.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/llm/token-meter/src/breakdown-projection.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/llm/token-meter/src/breakdown-projection.ts)

cards.title: AssistantProvenance is renamed to AssistantProviderMetadata
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-19 · AssistantProvenance is renamed to AssistantProviderMetadata



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that import the assistant provenance/replay type from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, and client-face plugins that re-declare or read the provenance view of an assistant message.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for the published type import from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`; #5 for the client view contract on a message record.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the identifier was renamed across both the host type and the client view, with no alias left behind.
  - Host: `packages/llm/llm/src/message.ts:10` declared `export interface AssistantProvenance { provider; model; replayState? }` on rc.2 and declares `export interface AssistantProviderMetadata` with identical members on 0.1.6-alpha.1; `ModelMessageSource` extends the renamed interface at `:24` in both trees.
  - Package root: `packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts:29` re-exported `AssistantProvenance` on rc.2 and re-exports `AssistantProviderMetadata` on 0.1.6-alpha.1. No deprecated alias exists in either tree.
  - Client: `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts:27` declared `AssistantProvenanceView` with the field `provenance?: AssistantProvenanceView` at `:76`; on 0.1.6-alpha.1 those are `AssistantProviderMetadataView` and `providerMetadata?: AssistantProviderMetadataView` at the same lines and `:136` of `request-inspection.ts`, and the renamed view is re-exported from `packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/contract/snapshot.ts:8`.
  - The rename is a coordinated repository-wide sweep (five client files per side, plus `scripts/type-equiv.manifest.json:11` on rc.2 and `:16` on 0.1.6-alpha.1), so nothing keeps the old spelling compiling.
- **Migration recipe**: grep `AssistantProvenance` and replace the host import with `AssistantProviderMetadata` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`. On the client face, replace `AssistantProvenanceView` with `AssistantProviderMetadataView` and the `provenance` property with `providerMetadata` in any snapshot, record or request-inspection type you re-declare or read. The member set is identical, so no data or session migration is involved — only the identifier and the property name.
- **Verification**: `import type { AssistantProviderMetadata } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'` typechecks and `AssistantProvenance` no longer resolves. An assistant message you construct still satisfies `ModelMessageSource` as `{ kind: 'model', provider, model, replayState? }`, and a client record you render reads its metadata from `providerMetadata` rather than `provenance`.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm/src/message.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm/src/message.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/llm/llm/src/message.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/llm/llm/src/message.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts)

cards.title: Context "provenance" becomes "producer", and assistant "provenance" becomes "provider metadata"
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-20 · Context "provenance" becomes "producer", and assistant "provenance" becomes "provider metadata"



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that import node types from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation/client` or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-chat/client` — in particular any keyed `conversation.chat.node` renderer that shows a context row's producer label or an assistant node's provider/model identity.
- **Touchpoints**: #5; #2 for plugins that fold the durable `user/message` `source` payload into their own node.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the vocabulary is renamed on both public entrypoints, with no alias left behind:
  - `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/context-provenance.ts` is renamed to `context-producer.ts`. rc.2 line 14 `export interface ContextProvenanceView {` → alpha.1 line 14 `export interface ContextProducerView {`. Members (`role: ContextRole`, `label: string | null`) are unchanged, so this is a pure symbol rename.
  - `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts` rc.2 line 27 `export interface AssistantProvenanceView {` → alpha.1 line 27 `export interface AssistantProviderMetadataView {`; members stay `provider: string`, `model: string`.
  - `records.ts` rc.2 line 76 `provenance?: AssistantProvenanceView` → alpha.1 line 76 `providerMetadata?: AssistantProviderMetadataView`.
  - `records.ts` rc.2 line 107 `provenance: ContextProvenanceView` (on `ContextMessageNode`) → alpha.1 line 107 `producer: ContextProducerView`.
  - Public entry `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/index.ts`: rc.2 line 24 exports `AssistantProvenanceView` and lines 31–32 export `ContextProvenanceView` from `'./contract/context-provenance.ts'`; alpha.1 line 24 exports `AssistantProviderMetadataView` and lines 31–32 export `ContextProducerView` from `'./contract/context-producer.ts'`.
  - Public entry `packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/index.ts`: rc.2 line 17 `AssistantProvenanceView`, line 45 `ContextProvenanceView, ContextRole, KnownContextForm` → alpha.1 line 17 `AssistantProviderMetadataView`, line 45 `ContextProducerView, ContextRole, KnownContextForm`. `ui-chat/src/client/contract/snapshot.ts` repeats the first rename at rc.2 line 8 → alpha.1 line 8.
  Because no slot name moves, a plugin that only registers seats still loads; the failure is a compile error on the exported symbols and on the two renamed node fields.
- **Migration recipe**: rename every import (`ContextProvenanceView` → `ContextProducerView`, `AssistantProvenanceView` → `AssistantProviderMetadataView`); update field reads (`AssistantMessageNode.providerMetadata`, `ContextMessageNode.producer`); repoint any deep `./src/client/contract/context-provenance.ts` import to `contract/context-producer.ts`; re-run typecheck before touching runtime code.
- **Verification**: typecheck against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation/client@0.1.6-alpha.1` — a lingering `.provenance` read must fail, not render an empty label; then render one context row and assert its header still shows the producer label.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/context-producer.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/context-producer.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/context-provenance.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/context-provenance.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/contract/snapshot.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-chat/src/client/contract/snapshot.ts)

cards.title: `CommandClaim` gains a required `name`, and `InputState.claim` carries it
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-21 · `CommandClaim` gains a required `name`, and `InputState.claim` carries it



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: every plugin that registers an `InputTriggerSource` through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-input-trigger/client` and returns a `{ claim }` from `onPick`, `matchSpace` or `matchEnter` — any third-party `/` command or `@` mention source that takes over the composer draft — plus any test double that builds an `InputState`.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**:
  - `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/input.ts` rc.2 line 45 `export interface CommandClaim {` lists `token`, `hint?`, `attachments?`, `submit(...)`. alpha.1 line 38 opens the same interface and lines 39–40 add `/** Catalog command name without the leading slash (the key of per-command composer copy such as `hint.*`). */ readonly name: string`. A claim that supplies only `token` no longer typechecks.
  - The published state carries it too: rc.2 line 338 `readonly claim?: { readonly token: string; readonly hint?: string; readonly attachments?: boolean }` → alpha.1 line 252 `readonly claim?: { readonly name: string; readonly token: string; readonly hint?: string; readonly attachments?: boolean }`.
  - `PickOutcome` (alpha.1 lines 56–61) still unions `{ readonly claim: CommandClaim }`, so the requirement reaches any source that returns a claim.
  - The reference implementation shows the intended separation: `ui-commands` rc.2 line 348 `private leadingClaim(desc: CommandDescriptor, session: ClientSessionContext): CommandClaim` → alpha.1 line 363 `private leadingClaim(desc: CommandDescriptor, session: ClientSessionContext, shown: string): CommandClaim` with alpha.1 line 367 `name: desc.name,`. `name` is the canonical catalog name; `token` may be a localized spelling that stays in the draft.
  - Imports still resolve — `CommandClaim` remains exported from `ui-input-trigger/src/types.ts` (line 18 re-export list) and from `ui-conversation/client` — so the break is a type error at the construction site, not a module-resolution error.
- **Migration recipe**: add `name` to every `CommandClaim` you build — the catalog command name without the leading slash, i.e. what `/name args` executes — and keep your existing `token` as the spelling the composer draft shows; if a test synthesizes an `InputState`, add a `name` to its `claim`.
- **Verification**: typecheck the trigger source; then drive one menu pick and one Space adjudication on a composed client and assert the claimed token stays in the draft while the executed line uses the catalog name.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/input.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/input.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/service.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/service.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-input-trigger/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-input-trigger/src/types.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/input.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/input.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/service.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-commands/src/client/service.ts)
