cards.title: The composer's permission control moves to the new `conversation.input.permission` slot, and the `permissions` projection keeps only the current value
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-22 · The composer's permission control moves to the new `conversation.input.permission` slot, and the `permissions` projection keeps only the current value



- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that render or replace a composer tool-row control; plugins that read `session.projections.faceOf('permissions')` to build their own preset picker; anything that reached into the built-in picker that used to live inside `ui-conversation`.
- **Touchpoints**: #5; #3 for the new `remote.permissionPresets` endpoint.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
  (required for readers of the `permissions` projection; optional for new occupants of the seat.)
- **Symptoms**: the composer's third control becomes a slot and the projection behind it loses its option list:
  - rc.2 had no permission slot: `ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts` ended the composer tool row at `'conversation.input.plan'` (line 184) and `'conversation.input.model'` (line 186), and `ComposerBarProps` rendered only those (`:341-342`). alpha.1 line 185 adds `'conversation.input.permission': { kind: 'single'; scope: 'session'; owner: InputControlOwnerProps }` and line 341 adds it to `ComposerBarProps`'s `PropsRenderSlots` union.
  - The control left the shell: rc.2 `ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/InputBar.tsx` line 38 `import { PermissionSelect } from './PermissionSelect.tsx'` and line 372 `<PermissionSelect key={sessionId} value={permissions} locked={locked} command={command} t={t} />`; `skeleton/PermissionSelect.tsx` and `skeleton/PermissionSelect.module.css` are deleted on this edge. alpha.1 `InputBar.tsx` line 423 `{sessionId === undefined ? null : renderSlot('conversation.input.permission', { locked })}`, declared as a child at alpha.1 `ui-conversation/src/client/apply.ts` line 325.
  - A different package now occupies it: alpha.1 `ui-permission-presets/src/client/index.ts` lines 167–174 `ctx.slots.inject('conversation.input.permission', () => ctx.slots.register({ name: 'conversation.input.permission', locale: PERMISSION_ACCESS_NS, inject: (sessionId) => ({ hooks: { permissionCatalog: catalog.store }, select: preset => submit(sessionId, preset) }) }, PermissionSelect))`, with new `PermissionSelect.tsx` and `catalog.ts` files in that package.
  - The projection narrowed: `packages/interaction/permission-presets/src/types.ts` rc.2 line 27 `export interface PermissionSelect {` (`options: PresetOption[]` + `currentValue: string`) with line 42 `permissions: PermissionSelect` → alpha.1 line 32 `export interface PermissionSelection {` (`currentValue: string` only) with line 57 `permissions: PermissionSelection`. The option list is now a process catalog (`PermissionCatalog`, alpha.1 line 26, `options: PresetOption[]`) read through a new Remote: alpha.1 `ui-permission-presets/src/client/catalog.ts` line 134 `const operation = this.ctx.remote.permissionPresets.catalog()`, wired at alpha.1 `packages/api/remotes/src/client/index.ts` line 162.
- **Migration recipe**: if you built your own picker from `faceOf('permissions').getSnapshot().options`, stop — read `currentValue` from the projection and fetch the options from `ctx.remote.permissionPresets.catalog()` (declare `remote.permissionPresets` in `inject`), or better, drop the duplicate and register one control into `conversation.input.permission` with `InputControlOwnerProps` (`locked: boolean`), which is now the single seat for it. Register through `ctx.slots.inject('conversation.input.permission', ...)` (the declarer is `ui-conversation`, a different plugin) and declare `slots` in `inject`.
- **Verification**: on a composed client, open a session and confirm one permission control still renders between Plan and Model; typecheck a projection reader and confirm `.options` no longer exists; dispose `ui-permission-presets` and confirm the seat empties cleanly instead of rendering a stale control.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/InputBar.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/InputBar.tsx) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-permission-presets/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-permission-presets/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/interaction/permission-presets/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/interaction/permission-presets/src/types.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/PermissionSelect.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/PermissionSelect.tsx) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/interaction/permission-presets/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/interaction/permission-presets/src/types.ts)

cards.title: Right-sidebar tab types: guide entries now need an `id`, a keyed `sidebar.right.tab.guide.entry` slot appears, and `multiple` / close handlers join the registry
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-23 · Right-sidebar tab types: guide entries now need an `id`, a keyed `sidebar.right.tab.guide.entry` slot appears, and `multiple` / close handlers join the registry



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: every plugin that calls `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register(...)` with a `guide` list, and every plugin that owns a resource-backed sidebar tab it must release before removal.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
  (required for guide entries; optional for the new seats.)
- **Symptoms**:
  - `packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts` rc.2 line 61 `export interface SidebarRightGuideEntry {` begins with `order`. alpha.1 line 61 opens the same interface and lines 62–63 add `/** Stable entry identity within its provider. */ readonly id: string` as a **required** member, while line 251 now throws at registration: `if (new Set(entries.map(entry => entry.id)).size !== entries.length) throw new Error(\`sidebarRight: duplicate guide entry id in "${id}"\`)`. An existing `guide: [{ order, title }]` fails to typecheck.
  - `SidebarRightGuideBox` (alpha.1 line 83) gains line 85 `/** Active implementation identity used to dispatch the entry renderer. */ readonly providerId: string`.
  - `SidebarRightTabDefinition` gains `readonly multiple?: boolean` at alpha.1 line 103 ("Each open by kind creates independent content; omission keeps one page per kind in each pane"), consumed at alpha.1 `service.ts` line 348 `const address = definition.multiple === true ? \`${pageAddress(kind)}/${randomUUID()}\` : pageAddress(kind)`.
  - New keyed slot at alpha.1 `ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/slots.ts` lines 82–88: `'sidebar.right.tab.guide.entry': { kind: 'keyed'; scope: 'session'; owner: SidebarRightGuideEntryOwnerProps; hookContext: UseSidebarRightTabInfo; inject: { hooks: { tabInfo: SlotHookFactory<'sidebar.right.tab.guide.entry', UseSidebarRightTabInfo> } } }`, with line 184 `export interface SidebarRightGuideEntryOwnerProps { readonly entryId: string; readonly kind: string; readonly title: string; readonly description?: string }`, declared as a child of `sidebar.right.pane.tab` at alpha.1 `ui-sidebar-right/src/client/index.ts` line 192.
  - New close seam: alpha.1 `service.ts` line 139 `export type SidebarRightCloseHandler = (sessionId: SessionId, tab: TabRecord) => void` and line 218 `registerCloseHandler(kind: string, handler: SidebarRightCloseHandler): () => void` (throws on a duplicate kind), run through `removeAfterCleanup` at lines 318 and 321. `close(tabId)` now routes through `closeIn` for an adopted session, so closing consults `canCloseTab` and the kind's handler.
  - Both `SidebarRightCloseHandler` and `SidebarRightGuideEntryOwnerProps` join the `client` entry's export list. First-party migrations: alpha.1 `ui-sidebar-files/src/client/definition.tsx` line 37 `id: 'workspace',`; alpha.1 `ui-sidebar-terminal/src/client/index.ts` line 48 `id, kind: 'terminal', multiple: true, priority: 'builtin', ...`, line 49 a guide entry `{ id: 'new', order: 20, ... }`, line 51 `ctx.sidebarRight.registerCloseHandler('terminal', (sessionId, tab) => { ctx.webTerminals.close(sessionId, tab.id, terminalId(sessionId, tab.id)) })`.
- **Migration recipe**: give every guide entry a stable, provider-unique `id`; set `multiple: true` for a kind whose tabs must not collapse into one page; register `ctx.sidebarRight.registerCloseHandler(kind, handler)` (one per kind, effect-scoped disposer) when the tab owns a process or resource; to render per-entry guide content, register a keyed component into `sidebar.right.tab.guide.entry` with `key` = your provider id and read `SidebarRightGuideEntryOwnerProps`, keeping the existing `sidebar.right.tab.guide` chain registration only if you replace the whole guide page.
- **Verification**: register a type with two guide entries and confirm two distinct cards, and that a duplicate `id` throws at registration; open a `multiple: true` type twice and confirm two independent pages; close one and assert your close handler ran exactly once before removal.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/service.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/service.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/tab-registry.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/src/client/contract/slots.ts)

cards.title: `ConnectionIndicator` loses its required `reconnectLabel` prop
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-24 · `ConnectionIndicator` loses its required `reconnectLabel` prop



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: any Web Client plugin that renders the shared connection pill from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` in its own chrome — `ui-primitives` is the baseline static library every dynamic bundle may reuse.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: rc.2 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/ConnectionIndicator.tsx` line 22 `export function ConnectionIndicator({` destructured `disconnectedLabel` (line 24) and `reconnectLabel` (line 25), with the props type declaring `disconnectedLabel: string` (line 33) and `reconnectLabel: string` (line 34); lines 44–45 fed both into the hidden widest-label spans and line 90 rendered `reconnectLabel` as the hover/focus swap. alpha.1 line 28 keeps the same function and line 38 still declares `disconnectedLabel: string`, but **no `reconnectLabel` member exists in the file**. The pill now shows its retry action statically through `IconRefreshOutline14` (alpha.1 line 6 import), sizes to its current label, and gains a 150 ms exit transition (`EXIT_MS = 150`, alpha.1 line 13) with a `window.setTimeout` unmount. `ConnectionIndicatorState` and the root barrel are unchanged (`ui-primitives/src/index.ts` line 27). The first-party consumer shows the mechanical edit: rc.2 `ui-settings-general/src/client/SettingsRoot.tsx` passed `reconnectLabel={t('connection.retry')}`; that prop is deleted on the alpha.1 side.
- **Migration recipe**: delete `reconnectLabel` from every `<ConnectionIndicator>` call site and make `disconnectedLabel` itself name the retry action (that is the new copy contract: the outage label names what clicking does). No other prop moves.
- **Verification**: typecheck the call site — a leftover `reconnectLabel` is an excess-property error; render `state='disconnected'` and confirm one visible label plus a refresh glyph, no hover-dependent text swap, and no width change between `disconnected` and `connecting`.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/ConnectionIndicator.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/ConnectionIndicator.tsx) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-settings-general/src/client/SettingsRoot.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-settings-general/src/client/SettingsRoot.tsx) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/ConnectionIndicator.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/ConnectionIndicator.tsx)

cards.title: `DiffBlock` and `diffTotals` compare contextual content instead of whole fragments
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-25 · `DiffBlock` and `diffTotals` compare contextual content instead of whole fragments



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that render a diff through the shared `DiffBlock` primitive or compute a `+/-` summary with `diffTotals` — both are root exports of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`.
- **Touchpoints**: #5
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: rc.2 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/DiffBlock.tsx` line 73 `export function diffTotals(...)` counted every old-side line as removed and every new-side line as added, and line 154 `export function DiffBlock(...)` flattened the same fragments into all-`del`-then-all-`add` rows. alpha.1 line 68 adds `const MAX_DIFF_EDIT_LENGTH = 256`; line 76 derives real patches — `structuredPatch('', '', normalize(oldLines), normalize(newLines), undefined, undefined, { context: 3, maxEditLength: MAX_DIFF_EDIT_LENGTH })?.hunks` — from the new `diff` dependency, and both line 87 `diffTotals` and line 173 `DiffBlock` consume those hunks. Observable consequences: up to three neutral context lines render on each side of a change (a new `'context'` row kind, alpha.1 line 49), shared context counts toward neither total, distant changes split into separate hunks separated by a `⋯` gap, and a fragment whose edit search exceeds 256 edits falls back to a coarse whole-fragment replacement that does include shared lines in display, copy and counts. `DiffHunk` keeps its member names and types (`oldText: string | null`, `newText: string`) but its documented meaning changes to "content including context" (alpha.1 lines 18–21), so callers must stop passing pre-diffed fragments. Root barrel unchanged: `ui-primitives/src/index.ts` line 55 `export { DiffBlock, DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_LINES, diffTotals } from './DiffBlock.tsx'`. The first-party chat card follows: `ui-tool/src/client/tool/models/diff-card-model.ts` moves `CHAT_DIFF_MAX_LINES` from 8 to 9 ("Room for a path, one removed/added pair, and three context lines on each side").
- **Migration recipe**: keep passing the raw before/after fragments including unchanged context — do not pre-split them. Refresh pinned `+/-` totals, rendered row strings, DOM snapshots and `diffTotals` expectations: they shrink to the changed lines and gain two-space-prefixed context rows in copied text. Re-derive any pinned `maxLines` for the context-inclusive geometry (the first-party chat row went 8 → 9).
- **Verification**: render a `DiffBlock` whose fragment contains unchanged context between two edits and assert the context renders once, `diffTotals` counts only the changed lines, and a copied body carries `  `-prefixed context rows; snapshot a >256-edit fragment and confirm the whole-fragment replacement renders instead of throwing.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/DiffBlock.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/DiffBlock.tsx) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/tool/models/diff-card-model.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/tool/models/diff-card-model.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/ui-primitives/src/DiffBlock.tsx`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/ui-primitives/src/DiffBlock.tsx)

cards.title: The standalone `?fixture` page mode is removed; the whole-client assembly test tier replaces it
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-26 · The standalone `?fixture` page mode is removed; the whole-client assembly test tier replaces it



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugin authors who develop or smoke a Web Client plugin against the local `?fixture` page instead of a real Host, and any CI lane that opened the served client with that query flag.
- **Touchpoints**: #6 (the page URL a client composition reads); #5 for the plugin-activation tests that replace it.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**:
  - `packages/client/connection/src/client/fixture.ts` is deleted, together with `packages/client/connection/tests/fixture.client.spec.ts` and `packages/client/connection/tests/fixture-commands.client.spec.ts`.
  - rc.2 `packages/client/connection/src/client/index.ts` line 11 `import { createFixtureConnectionRpc } from './fixture.ts'`, line 184 `const fixture = pageLocation !== undefined && new URLSearchParams(pageLocation.search).has('fixture')`, line 185 `const fixtureRpc = fixture ? createFixtureConnectionRpc() : undefined`, folded into `const rpc = fixtureRpc ?? createWebConnectionRpc(...)`. alpha.1 line 315 `apply` has no query-string branch at all.
  - The replacing seam is explicit and additive: alpha.1 line 79 `export interface ClientTransportHooks {` with line 85 `rpc?: ClientConnectionRpc` ("Already decoded logical RPC carrier ... an in-process Host such as a test mock plugs in here"), and line 203 `export function installConnection(ctx: Context, options: ConnectionInstallOptions = {}): void` with the new `ConnectionInstallOptions` (`transport?`, `recovery?`, `location?`). Both are exported from the `client` entry.
  - The upload runtime loses the flag too: rc.2 `packages/client/file-upload/src/client/runtime.ts` lines 170, 180 and 314–318, and rc.2 `packages/client/file-upload/README.md` line 12 documented "The standalone `?fixture` page uses the generated Remote for replayable Blob and exact-byte inputs" — that sentence is gone.
  - The replacement tier is new on this edge: `packages/test-support/client-runtime/src/assembly/index.ts` lines 7–14 export `ClientRoster`, `TestClient`, `remoteDefaultResponses`, `bundleRoster`, `webApp` and `createClientTest`. It boots the real roster through the production `bootClient` over an endpoint-named Remote mock, and is a deliberate deep import: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-test-runtime/src/assembly/index.ts`.
- **Migration recipe**: stop opening the client with `?fixture`, and drop any CI job that does. For slot/component work keep `SlotTestRuntime.create()` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-test-runtime` (unchanged). For plugin activation, reload, reconnect and cleanup, move to the assembly tier: `import { createClientTest, webApp } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-test-runtime/src/assembly/index.ts'`, then `const test = createClientTest({ roster: webApp }, { mount: true })`, and inside a case stub the endpoints your plugin calls (`remote.<ns>.<method>.mockResolvedValue(ok(...))`) before `await start()`. `webApp.closure(names)` / `webApp.pick(names)` cut the roster to your plugin plus everything it injects; an unstubbed endpoint fails the test at `dispose()`. If you own a non-browser carrier, call `installConnection(ctx, { transport: { rpc } })` directly instead of forking the Connection plugin.
- **Verification**: `rg -n "\?fixture|isFixturePage" <plugin>` returns nothing; a stale `ctx.fileUpload.available` read no longer typechecks; the new assembly test boots your plugin's roster row and `client.ctx.slots.entries('<your.slot>')` shows your registration.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/client/connection/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/connection/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/test-support/client-runtime/src/assembly/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/test-support/client-runtime/src/assembly/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/test-support/client-runtime/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/test-support/client-runtime/README.md) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/connection/src/client/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/connection/src/client/index.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/connection/src/client/fixture.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/connection/src/client/fixture.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/client/file-upload/src/client/runtime.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/client/file-upload/src/client/runtime.ts)

cards.title: the base composition swaps the `workflow-worker-thread` row for a `ptc-runtime` + `workflow-ptc` pair
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-27 · the base composition swaps the `workflow-worker-thread` row for a `ptc-runtime` + `workflow-ptc` pair



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile wrappers, overlays and provisioning scripts that name the `workflow-worker-thread` row id or depend on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread`; plugins that consumed the worker-thread PTC runtime.
- **Touchpoints**: #5 for composition rows that register tools/services; #3 when a plugin resolved the removed package as a service provider.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: on rc.2 the base bundle inserted one row, `- id: workflow-worker-thread` / `name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread'` with `config: { provider: spawn }`. On 0.1.6-alpha.1 that row is gone and two rows replace it: `ptc-runtime` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node`) with no config, and `workflow-ptc` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc`) which keeps `provider: spawn`. The old package is deleted from the workspace, so an overlay that still names it fails resolution instead of silently degrading, and `pnpm why`/`dsh plugin` on a profile pinned to the old name reports a missing package.
- **Migration recipe**: replace the old row with the two new rows in every overlay/patch you maintain, and move any `provider: spawn` config onto `workflow-ptc`; keep `ptc-runtime` config-free unless the deployment needs a different PTC runtime, in which case name the runtime row explicitly. Delete `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread` from manifests and lockfiles rather than aliasing it.
- **Verification**: boot the profile and confirm both rows resolve (the boot log names `ptc-runtime` and `workflow-ptc`), a PTC/workflow tool run still executes in spawn mode, and no lockfile entry for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread` remains.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) · [rc.2 `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml)

cards.title: the base composition mounts `image-offload`, whose `image/offload` event is required on read
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-28 · the base composition mounts `image-offload`, whose `image/offload` event is required on read



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: anything that reads, validates, replays or downgrades a session log written by a base-backed 0.1.6-alpha.1 profile (session readers, exporters, replay/projection consumers, Web Client plugins that render messages); and any deployment that adds the image-offload plugin to a composition.
- **Touchpoints**: #2 for the persistent event contract; #5 for the composition row.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the shipped base gains `- id: image-offload` / `name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-image-offload'`. The package is new on this edge and owns a new durable event, `image/offload`, declared by module augmentation on `SessionEventMap` and carrying `{ targets: [{ seq, imageIndexes }] }`. The event has no `ignorable: true`, so builds that do not know the type refuse the log; the persistence record states this explicitly and keeps the structural Session format version unchanged. The same package registers `imageOffloadProjection` with Session before accepting the event, so a missing projection rejects live restore and blocks message derivation, and it acts on `IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED` failures carrying `offloadImages` on the `agent/request-error` waterfall, appending the event instead of spending provider retry budget.
- **Migration recipe**: do not widen a plugin's own message handling to assume images always arrive as image blocks — read the projection instead, because a selected occurrence arrives as `offloadedImageText` naming the attachment and its read-only path (`ImageBlock.offloaded` carries the mark). If a plugin registers its own projections or validates session artifacts, either register the `image/offload` projection from the package's browser-safe `./projection` entry or accept that sessions containing the event cannot be replayed. Treat a downgrade of those logs as unsupported: keep the older build only for reading logs written before the first offload.
- **Verification**: open a session that contains an `image/offload` event in the newer build and confirm the selected occurrences render as placeholders while unselected images stay images; then open the same log in a pre-0.1.6 build and record the refusal instead of an unexpected success. Confirm an over-budget image request retries without an `llm/retry` event.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/compaction/compaction-image-offload/src/projection.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/compaction/compaction-image-offload/src/projection.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `docs/persistence-changes/2026-09-14-image-offload.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/docs/persistence-changes/2026-09-14-image-offload.md) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/compaction/compaction-image-offload/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/compaction/compaction-image-offload/README.md)

cards.title: the base bundle disables the `tool-ralph` row by default
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-29 · the base bundle disables the `tool-ralph` row by default



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: profiles and plugin sets that relied on the `ralph` tool being present in a base-backed profile, and automations that call it without an explicit user request.
- **Touchpoints**: #5 for tool registration; #2 if an automation consumed the tool's session events.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: on rc.2 the base inserted `- id: tool-ralph` / `name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph'` as an enabled row. On 0.1.6-alpha.1 the row survives but carries `disabled: true`, and the surrounding comment states the reason: the tool description restricts `ralph` to runs the human explicitly asked for, and completion is a worker self-report rather than an independent evaluation. A profile that merely inherits base therefore loses the tool, and any prompt or automation that assumes it exists fails at tool lookup rather than at dispatch.
- **Migration recipe**: restore the row from an overlay only where the deployment genuinely wants it, by adding `- id: tool-ralph` with `disabled: false` (and the previous `subagentProvider`/`maxRounds` config) to `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` or a `--patch <file>` layer in that profile. Do not re-enable it in a shared profile template to satisfy one automation; scope the overlay to the profile that needs it.
- **Verification**: boot the profile without the overlay and confirm the tool list has no `ralph` entry; boot with the overlay and confirm the row is present and one bounded run completes, while an unrelated profile stays without it.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) · [rc.2 `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml)

cards.title: `mcp-resources` becomes a base and sdk-minimal row
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-30 · `mcp-resources` becomes a base and sdk-minimal row



- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: MCP-consuming deployments and plugins that read MCP resources or instructions; profile wrappers that previously added the row themselves.
- **Touchpoints**: #5 for the composition row; #3 for the MCP resource service surface.
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-resources` does not exist on rc.2. On 0.1.6-alpha.1 it is a new package, mounted by the base bundle (`- id: mcp-resources`) and by the sdk-minimal bundle, and it is added to the launcher's dependency cohort. A profile overlay that already mounted its own copy under the same row id now collides with the shipped row; one that mounted it under a different id ends up with two rows.
- **Migration recipe**: drop a hand-added `mcp-resources` row from overlays that inherit base or sdk-minimal, and keep only deployment-specific config in an overlay that overrides the shipped row. Adopt the resource surface through the plugin's documented config rather than by importing the package directly.
- **Verification**: boot a base-backed profile and confirm exactly one `mcp-resources` row is present and that an MCP server exposing resources surfaces them without a duplicate registration error.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/sdk-minimal/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/sdk-minimal/cordis.patch.yml)

cards.title: the Web app bundle drops the `code-runtime` row and mounts three new rows
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-31 · the Web app bundle drops the `code-runtime` row and mounts three new rows



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web-app overlays that named `code-runtime`/`@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread`, and client plugins that need the new terminal/session-settings seats.
- **Touchpoints**: #5 for composition rows and client seats; #3 for the terminal controller service.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the Web app bundle loses `- id: code-runtime` / `name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread'`, because the `code-runtime` package family is deleted on this edge; PTC execution is composed from the base's `ptc-runtime` row instead. The same bundle gains `terminal-controller` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-terminal-controller`) ahead of `workspace-files`, `ui-sidebar-terminal` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-terminal`) beside `ui-sidebar-files`, and `ui-settings-unarchive-sessions` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-unarchive-sessions`) ahead of `ui-conversation`. Client plugins that assume the right sidebar pane list is exactly the shipped set now see an extra terminal pane, and settings plugins see an extra page.
- **Migration recipe**: remove `code-runtime` from Web overlays and manifests and let the base's PTC row serve execution; if an overlay pinned the row to keep PTC out of the Web bundle, re-express that intent against the new row ids. Audit client code that hardcodes sidebar or settings composition instead of reading the registry, and re-run it against the new default set.
- **Verification**: boot the Web profile and confirm the right sidebar lists the terminal pane next to the file tree, the settings surface shows the unarchive-sessions page, and a PTC execution still runs with no `code-runtime` row present.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml) · [rc.2 `packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml)

cards.title: the workspace ledger adds 22 packages and retires 7, including both `code-runtime` runtimes and the E2B providers
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-32 · the workspace ledger adds 22 packages and retires 7, including both `code-runtime` runtimes and the E2B providers



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugin authors and profile owners who depend on a removed package by name, and packagers who pin the published cohort rather than the launcher alias.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for plugins that resolved a removed package as a service provider; #7 when the removed provider executed subprocesses.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: comparing the two workspaces, 267 packages become 283. Removed: `packages/code-runtime/code-runtime`, `packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread`, `packages/e2b/e2b`, `packages/e2b/fs-e2b`, `packages/e2b/subprocess-e2b`, `packages/experimental/code-runtime-python`, `packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread`. Added: `packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime`, `packages/ptc-runtime/ptc-runtime-node`, `packages/workflow/workflow-ptc`, `packages/mcp/mcp-resources`, `packages/api/terminal-controller`, `packages/compaction/compaction-image-offload`, `packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal`, `packages/client/ui-settings-unarchive-sessions`, `packages/test-support/remote-mock`, the four-package SSH family (`ssh/ssh`, `ssh/fs-ssh`, `ssh/sandbox-ssh`, `ssh/subprocess-ssh`), the four browser-use packages, the four computer-use packages (`computer-use`, `experimental/browser-use-*`, `experimental/computer-use-*`) and `experimental/ptc-runtime-python`. The retirement is deliberate rather than a rename in place: the E2B providers were retired as a group, and the code-runtime family is replaced by the PTC runtime pair plus a sandboxed Node runtime.
- **Migration recipe**: treat a dependency on a removed package as a broken coordinate, not as a version problem. Move worker-thread code runtime consumers to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime-node` (composed by the base's `ptc-runtime` row) and Python code-runtime consumers to `experimental/ptc-runtime-python`; for remote execution that used E2B, migrate to the SSH provider family, which is the maintained remote seam on this edge. Re-run install and let the lockfile drop the retired names instead of pinning them for compatibility.
- **Verification**: `pnpm install` succeeds with no reference to the seven removed names, and one execution path per adopted replacement runs (a PTC call on the node runtime, one remote command over SSH).
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages) · [rc.2 `packages/`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/base/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/base/package.json)

cards.title: headless mode gains `--session-id` and `--json`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-33 · headless mode gains `--session-id` and `--json`



- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: automations that drive `dsh --profile headless "<task>"` and parse its output; headless profile wrappers.
- **Touchpoints**: #7 for stdout contract; #5 for the CLI option surface.
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: the headless bundle used to read only `task` from the `headlessStartup` provider and always created a fresh Agent. On 0.1.6-alpha.1 the bundle patch passes `sessionId: !!js ctx.headlessStartup.sessionId` and `json: !!js ctx.headlessStartup.json` into the runner, and `packages/bundle/headless/src/json-stream.ts` is new. The module doc states both: the runner "creates one Agent through the core registry (or adopts the exact Session a `--session-id` names)" and "with `--json` it projects the run as newline-delimited events instead of the final text". An automation that scrapes the human-readable output keeps working, but one that assumed a new session per invocation must now pass `--session-id` deliberately, and one that wants structured output should stop parsing prose.
- **Migration recipe**: for machine consumers, switch to `--json` and parse the documented fields instead of scraping text; when continuing existing work, pass `--session-id <id>` and assert the run appends to that session rather than creating a new one.
- **Verification**: run one task with `--json` and confirm the output parses; run a second task with `--session-id` naming the first run's session and confirm no new session file appears and both runs share one log.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/headless/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/headless/cordis.patch.yml) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/headless/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/headless/src/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/headless/src/json-stream.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/headless/src/json-stream.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/bundle/headless/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/bundle/headless/cordis.patch.yml)

cards.title: the public package manifest type is redefined and three exported types are gone
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-34 · the public package manifest type is redefined and three exported types are gone



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugin authors that import `@deepseek-ai/dsh-package-manifest`, and any
  package that declares a host requirement or a local profile project that types its own
  `package.json`.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for the package-level declaration a Host-side plugin compiles against;
  #5 for Client plugins whose build reads `dsh.client` from the same declaration.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the package keeps its name, `exports`, `files` and `publishConfig.access`, so
  only the exported type set moves — and a stale `node_modules` copy of the old declarations
  keeps compiling silently:
  - `packages/util/package-manifest/src/index.ts`: OLD exported
    `DshBundleManifest`, `DshClientManifest`, `DshConfigTreeDeclaration`, `DshManifest`,
    `DshModuleFallbackManifest`, `DshProfileManifest`,
    `DshSessionFormatMigrationManifest`, `ProfilePatchReload`; NEW exports
    `DshBundleManifest`, `DshClientManifest`, `DshEnginesManifest`, `DshManifest`,
    `DshPackageManifest`, `DshProfileManifest`, `ProfilePatchReload`.
    Removed: `DshConfigTreeDeclaration`, `DshModuleFallbackManifest`,
    `DshSessionFormatMigrationManifest`. Added: `DshPackageManifest`, `DshEnginesManifest`.
  - `packages/util/package-manifest/src/types.ts`: OLD `DshManifest` carried `bundle`,
    `profile`, `client`, `configTrees?`, `sessionFormatMigration?` and the `@internal`
    `moduleFallback?`; NEW `DshManifest` carries only `manifestVersion?: 1`, `bundle`,
    `profile`, `client`. The three internal members are no longer public API; their on-disk
    keys stay readable by the owning internal tools.
  - NEW `DshPackageManifest` requires `name` and `version` and adds optional `description`,
    `private`, `dependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `engines`, `dsh`. Local profile projects
    are read through app-boot's `Partial<DshPackageManifest>` adaptation, so they need no
    published identity.
  - NEW `DshEnginesManifest` gives runtime requirements one location at top-level `engines`:
    `dsh`, `node` and `npm` as optional version strings plus an open index signature for other
    engines. It is not `dsh.engines`. No manifest in either tree declares `engines` yet, and no
    installer or loader enforces the declaration on this edge.
  - NEW `dsh.manifestVersion?: 1` identifies the declaration format and is independent of the
    npm package version and the Session format version.
  - The root workspace stopped depending on the declaration package (`package.json` OLD
    `devDependencies` listed `@deepseek-ai/dsh-package-manifest`); the package still publishes.
- **Migration recipe**: split `rg -n "@deepseek-ai/dsh-package-manifest"` hits into type-only
  imports and value imports — the package has no runtime exports in either version, so a value
  import was already a type error. Replace reads of `configTrees`, `sessionFormatMigration` and
  `moduleFallback` with the owning implementation's own on-disk reader instead of re-declaring
  them locally. Move a host requirement to top-level `engines`, never `dsh.engines`
  (`"engines": { "dsh": ">=0.1.6-alpha.1", "node": ">=22.19" }`). Switch a whole-manifest type
  to `DshPackageManifest` and supply the now-required `name` and `version`. Add
  `"dsh": { "manifestVersion": 1 }` only to pin the format; nothing rejects a manifest without
  it.
- **Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` fails on a removed type rather than at runtime. Then
  `npm pack` and read `package.json` inside the tarball back for `engines` and
  `dsh.manifestVersion`; a lockfile pinned to the old declaration package passes typecheck
  against stale bytes, so reinstall before believing a green build.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/util/package-manifest/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/util/package-manifest/src/types.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/util/package-manifest/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/util/package-manifest/src/index.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/util/package-manifest/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/util/package-manifest/src/types.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/util/package-manifest/src/index.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/util/package-manifest/src/index.ts)

---

cards.title: experimental packages publish by default, and the allowlist is replaced by an empty denylist
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-35 · experimental packages publish by default, and the allowlist is replaced by an empty denylist



- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: plugin authors who want one of the newly published experimental packages, and
  packagers who mirror or re-vendor the cohort.
- **Touchpoints**: #4 for anything that installs these into `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>`; #3 for
  the install channel itself.
- **Action level**: required-if-mirroring
  (optional for an author who wants an experimental
  package.)
- **Symptoms**: the publication default inverted, so the set of package names that resolve from
  npm grew without an allowlist edit:
  - `scripts/experimental-package-policy.ts` OLD was a public **allowlist**
    (`PUBLIC_EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_DIRECTORIES` listing
    `packages/experimental/agent-team`, `agent-team-profile`, `agent-team-web-profile`,
    `client-ui-agent-team`, `tool-agent-team`) consumed by
    `isPublicExperimentalPackageDirectory(directory)` over a `Set`; NEW is an **empty
    denylist** (`PRIVATE_EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_DIRECTORIES: readonly string[] = []`) consumed by
    `isPublicExperimentalPackageDirectory(directory, privateDirectories =
    PRIVATE_EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_DIRECTORIES)` and matching
    `/^packages\/experimental\/[^/]+$/`.
  - The directory census went from 9 experimental packages (4 with `private: true`) to 16 with
    none private. Newly public on this edge:
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-runtime`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-playwright-mcp`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-chrome-devtools-mcp`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-browser-use-stagehand-native`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-computer-use-cua-driver-mcp`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-computer-use-cua-driver-native`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-ptc-runtime-python`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-inspector`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-webworker-packer`,
    `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-webworker-runtime`.
  - Four manifests had to change publication state, each dropping `private: true` and adding
    `publishConfig.access: public`: `packages/experimental/inspector/package.json`,
    `packages/experimental/webworker-packer/package.json`,
    `packages/experimental/webworker-runtime/package.json`, and
    `packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/package.json` (which also moved to
    `packages/experimental/ptc-runtime-python/`).
  - The policy text flipped with it: root `AGENTS.md` OLD read
    `experimental/ pre-stable prototypes; private by default with explicit public exceptions`;
    NEW reads `public by default with explicit private exceptions`.
  - The npm baseline stopped selecting by allowlist: new `scripts/npm-baseline-packages.ts`
    globs `vendor/*/package.json`, `packages/*/*/package.json` and `apps/*/package.json` and
    excludes only the denylist directories.
  - Publication grants neither stability nor support: nothing on this edge adds these packages
    to a shipped profile, and every one keeps the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-*` prefix.
- **Migration recipe**: re-derive a mirrored release set from
  `packages/*/*/package.json` + `apps/*/package.json` + `vendor/*/package.json` minus
  `PRIVATE_EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_DIRECTORIES`; a hardcoded 5-entry allowlist now under-publishes.
  For every manifest in your set, omit `private` and set `publishConfig.access: "public"` — the
  workspace constraint requires exactly that pairing, so `private: true` under a public policy
  and a public manifest without the access field are both rejected. Keep the
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-*` prefix when publishing your own prototype, because the
  isolation checks classify by prefix and repository directory rather than by a list. To add a
  private prototype later, add both its `private: true` manifest and its
  `PRIVATE_EXPERIMENTAL_PACKAGE_DIRECTORIES` entry. Adopt an experimental package only through
  explicit user composition — it is not in any default product layer.
- **Verification**: `pnpm run verify-default-product-isolation` and
  `pnpm run verify-packed-install` both fail when a default entry's graph reaches an
  experimental package. For a mirror, assert
  `grep -c '"private": true' packages/experimental/*/package.json` is 0 and that every
  experimental manifest carries `publishConfig.access == "public"`; then confirm the intended
  names resolve from npm at the new version.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `scripts/experimental-package-policy.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/scripts/experimental-package-policy.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `scripts/npm-baseline-packages.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/scripts/npm-baseline-packages.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/experimental/inspector/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/experimental/inspector/package.json) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/AGENTS.md) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `scripts/experimental-package-policy.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/scripts/experimental-package-policy.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `packages/experimental/inspector/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/experimental/inspector/package.json)

cards.title: the `node-addon-require-builtin` floor moved `^0.1.4` → `^0.1.6` on the install channel
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-36 · the `node-addon-require-builtin` floor moved `^0.1.4` → `^0.1.6` on the install channel



- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile owners whose lockfile resolved 0.1.4, and packagers who mirror the
  vendored framework or the CLI.
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for the loader seam that reads Node's internal ESM and CommonJS resolvers;
  #7 for the child processes that startup spawns around the same tree.
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the floor moved in exactly two manifests, and one of them is a published peer
  range, so a stale profile resolution now contradicts the installed host:
  - `vendor/loader/package.json` (`@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader`) peer floor
    `"node-addon-require-builtin": "^0.1.4"` → `"^0.1.6"`.
  - `apps/cli/package.json` dependency `"node-addon-require-builtin": "^0.1.4"` → `"^0.1.6"`.
  - Published launcher tarball: `packs/rc2/package/package.json` had `"^0.1.4"`,
    `packs/a1/package/package.json` has `"^0.1.6"`.
  - No other manifest in either tree declares the addon: the root `package.json` has no such
    entry, so a mirror cannot patch the floor from the workspace root.
  - The floor is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: profile resolution in `runtime` mode reads
    `internal/modules/esm/loader` and `internal/modules/cjs/loader` through this addon, and the
    internal-loader shape differs across the supported Node lines (Node 22 versus 24 tag the raw
    object rather than normalising it). A profile that keeps 0.1.4 against a 0.1.6 host is the
    unsupported variant.
- **Migration recipe**: delete the stale resolution for the addon from the profile and reinstall
  so the package manager picks `>=0.1.6` — remove `node_modules/node-addon-require-builtin` and
  its lockfile entry, then reinstall rather than hand-editing one range. If you mirror the
  vendored framework or the CLI, bump the loader peer range and the CLI dependency together; a
  mirror that ships the new CLI with the old loader peer fails resolution. If your profile pins
  the whole graph, regenerate the pin from the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.6-alpha.1`
  manifest. A plugin that declares the loader or the addon as a peer must widen to `^0.1.6`,
  because `^0.1.4` does not satisfy the new host.
- **Verification**: install the profile and read the resolved version back
  (`node -p "require('./node_modules/node-addon-require-builtin/package.json').version"` under
  the profile root), then start the host and mount a shipped profile — the addon load is on the
  startup path, so a mismatch surfaces there rather than at first use.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `vendor/loader/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/vendor/loader/package.json) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `apps/cli/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/apps/cli/package.json) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/resolver.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/resolver.ts) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `vendor/loader/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/vendor/loader/package.json) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `apps/cli/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/apps/cli/package.json)

cards.title: Desktop ships a bundled runtime and requires shared host packages as peers
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-37 · Desktop ships a bundled runtime and requires shared host packages as peers



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugin authors who want their plugin installable into the Desktop profile
  (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`).
- **Touchpoints**: #3 for shared host package instances and peer validation; #4 for the
  Desktop-owned profile directory; #7 for the bundled-Node Host and the reviewed native-build
  step.
- **Action level**: conditional
  (Desktop has not been released, so there is no shipped
  predecessor to migrate from, but these are the rules a plugin must meet to install at all.)
- **Symptoms**: Desktop's packaging was replaced wholesale before any release, so the rules a
  plugin must satisfy are new rather than changed:
  - `apps/desktop/package.json` description: "Electron desktop shell for an isolated
    pnpm-installed dsh runtime" → "Electron desktop shell for a bundled dsh runtime and external
    plugins". The build script `prepare:seed` (`tsx scripts/prepare-seed.ts`) became
    `prepare:dsh` (`tsx scripts/prepare-dsh.ts`), and
    `apps/desktop/scripts/prepare-seed.ts`, `apps/desktop/scripts/macos-seed-store.ts` and
    `apps/desktop/src/seed-store.ts` are deleted. The replacement adds
    `apps/desktop/src/runtime-tree.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/profile-packages.ts`,
    `apps/desktop/src/backend-controller.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/startup-document.ts`,
    `apps/desktop/src/startup-error.ts` and `apps/desktop/src/owned-directory.ts`.
  - The seed-based profile has no reader or migration: Desktop's own decision records that it
    "has not been released" and that "this is its first installation format; there are no
    readers or migrations for the unpublished seed-based profile".
  - Shared-package rule: Desktop links every bundled first-party package into the profile with
    directory symlinks (junctions on Windows) and states that "Reserved host packages must be
    peers; nested copies and aliases of shared packages fail validation. Ordinary plugin
    dependencies must resolve inside the profile." Validation rejects incompatible enabled
    peers, nested or aliased copies of shared packages, private package links, and dependency
    resolution through the CLI or other ancestor directories.
  - Upgrade behavior a plugin must survive: a compatible release change refreshes shared links
    and checks enabled plugins' peer requirements **without running pnpm** — plugin files,
    versions and lockfile stay in place — while a Node version, platform or architecture change
    reinstalls the locked plugin graph with scripts disabled, validates, runs approved lifecycle
    builds and validates again.
  - Concrete names a packager needs: `apps/desktop/src/core-package-set.ts` defines
    `DESKTOP_PACKAGE_SET_FILE = 'desktop-packages.json'`,
    `DESKTOP_PACKAGES_DIR = 'desktop-packages'`,
    `DESKTOP_HOST_PACKAGE = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-host'` and
    `DESKTOP_HOST_RUNTIME_FILES = ['lib/index.js', 'config/desktop.cordis.patch.yml']`; the same
    module verifies every local core tarball by sha512, rejects extra files in the package
    directory, and rejects a lockfile that resolved a packaged core name through a registry
    version. `apps/desktop/src/profile-packages.ts` records
    `DESKTOP_PROFILE_STATE = 'desktop-runtime-state.json'` with `schemaVersion: 1` and imports
    `satisfies` to validate peer ranges against the shared inventory.
- **Migration recipe**: declare every first-party package the plugin shares with the host as a
  `peerDependency` whose range the Desktop release version satisfies, and never bundle, nest or
  alias a copy of a shared host package. Keep ordinary dependencies local — they may differ from
  the host's versions, and Desktop deliberately does not link them. If the plugin needs
  host-wide module identity for a package that is not in the bundled runtime, that package has
  to join the runtime's shared inventory at Desktop build time; matching version numbers alone
  are not sufficient, so treat it as a release request rather than a profile-side edit. Do not
  write into `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`: Electron owns that profile and its package-manager
  state exclusively, and the CLI cannot boot or mutate it. A plugin that requires a native build
  must be installable under the profile's reviewed `allowBuilds` list, because an unapproved
  build-requiring dependency fails the transaction.
- **Verification**: install the plugin into a Desktop profile and start the application — profile
  preparation recreates shared links and validates enabled peers before the Host starts. In a
  checkout, `apps/desktop/tests/profile-packages.spec.ts` and
  `apps/desktop/tests/runtime-tree.spec.ts` are the focused specs for the link and inventory
  rules, and `apps/desktop/tests/profile-mcp.spec.ts` covers the Desktop composition including
  its Host overlay. Signed installed-artifact qualification remains a release-environment check.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `apps/desktop/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/apps/desktop/README.md) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `apps/desktop/src/core-package-set.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/apps/desktop/src/core-package-set.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `apps/desktop/src/profile-packages.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/apps/desktop/src/profile-packages.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `apps/desktop/src/runtime-tree.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/apps/desktop/src/runtime-tree.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-08-desktop-bundled-runtime-and-external-plugins.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-08-desktop-bundled-runtime-and-external-plugins.md) · [0.1.5-rc.2 `apps/desktop/package.json`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/apps/desktop/package.json)

cards.title: the session format version, the engine floor and the launcher CLI grammar did not move (negative evidence)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A1-38 · the session format version, the engine floor and the launcher CLI grammar did not move (negative evidence)



- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: every plugin and profile wrapper upgrading from `dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2`.
- **Touchpoints**: none for the unchanged items; #2 only through the new `image/offload` event documented above.
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: several surfaces that usually move on a corridor this size did not, so a plugin should not spend its migration budget there:
  - `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` is still `3` at `packages/core/session/src/types.ts:88` in both tags. The new `image/offload` event is a *type* addition that readers must know (see the image-offload card), not a structural format bump: the persistence records for `2026-09-12-auto-review-error-metadata` and `2026-09-14-image-offload` both decide `same-version`, and neighbours stay readable.
  - `engines` is unchanged (`node: ^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`) and the workspace still declares `packageManager: pnpm@11.7.0`; the launcher's Cordis dependency ranges (`@deepseek-ai/cordis ^4.0.2`, `cordis-plugin-loader ^1.0.3`, `-hmr ^1.0.17`, `-include ^1.0.7`, `-timer ^1.1.4`) are identical at both ends.
  - The launcher's own CLI grammar is unchanged: `lib/bin.js` differs only in the three content-hashed dynamic-import specifiers (`profile-boot-*`, `plugin-*`, `dump-config-*`), so `dsh web`, `dsh --profile <name>`, `dsh plugin` and `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` parse exactly as before. `lib/plugin-*.js` differs only in the same way, and `dump-config` only in its import.
  - Untouched configuration surfaces that a profile owner might otherwise re-check: root `tsconfig.json`, `packages/bundle/README.md`, and the `acp-app` and `sdk-app` bundle patches are byte-identical across the edge.
- **Migration recipe**: no source action. Spend the effort on the moved surfaces instead — the PTC runtime replacement, the package ledger, the required-on-read `image/offload` event, and the adapter image-budget seam.
- **Verification**: `git diff --name-only dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2 dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1` prints 4015 paths, 307 of them `package.json`; `git diff` restricted to `packages/core/session/src/types.ts` shows no change to the `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` line, and a diff of the two launcher tarballs shows no flag or subcommand change.
- **Source**: [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/core/session/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/core/session/src/types.ts) · [rc.2 `packages/core/session/src/types.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/packages/core/session/src/types.ts) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 root `package.json` (`engines`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/package.json) · [rc.2 root `package.json` (`engines`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.5-rc.2/package.json) · [0.1.6-alpha.1 `packages/bundle/acp-app/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/bundle/acp-app/cordis.patch.yml)

cards.title: Multi-instance Session references: `SessionListState.current` is removed; resolve the main Session through `uiSession.adapter.current`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A2-01 · Multi-instance Session references: `SessionListState.current` is removed; resolve the main Session through `uiSession.adapter.current`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Touchpoints**: none (client root services: the Session Controller list snapshot and the `uiSession` service from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session`)
- **Applies to**: Plugins resolving the current/main session id through `sessions.list.getSnapshot().current` or `useSessions(s => s.current)` (keyboard helpers, paste/drop handlers, any event-time session resolution outside a slot component)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: On alpha.1 `SessionListState` carried `current: SessionId | undefined` (`packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/service.ts:74`); on alpha.2 the interface (`:53-67`) has no `current` field, because Session ownership becomes per-source reference counts and "current" now means main-view occupancy — a row whose `retainedBy.mainView` count is positive (architecture note `2026-09-15-client-session-references.md:80`). Plugins keep passing their compat guards (the `sessions`/`uiConversation` services still exist) but silently no-op: every current-session read returns `undefined`. First-hand fleet evidence: a composer input-recall plugin lost Ctrl+Up/Down entirely and a paste/drop attachment plugin raised "请先打开一个会话" on every paste after the host upgrade.
- **Migration recipe**: `uiSession` is not new — it is registered by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session` on both tags (alpha.1 `ui-approval` already injects it) — but its field holding the current binding is private on both (`private currentBinding` on alpha.1, `private readonly current` at `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts:280` on alpha.2). The public path that works on both hosts is the slot-scope adapter: inject `uiSession` and read `ctx.uiSession.adapter.current.getSnapshot()`, a `StandardSourceBinding` whose `key` is the main Session id (or `undefined` with no Session); when `key` is defined the binding is a `ScopedStandardSourceBinding` that also carries the session-scoped `ctx`. Subscribe through `ctx.uiSession.adapter.current.subscribe(listener)` if the plugin caches the id. On alpha.2 the same fact can also be derived from the catalog as the row with `retainedBy.mainView > 0` in `sessions.list.getSnapshot().byId` (note `:80`, `:152`). Slot components (scope `session`) are unaffected — they receive session context through their Provider.
- **Verification**: With one session open, the plugin's event-time resolution returns the open session's id on both alpha.1 and alpha.2 hosts; switching the main-view session changes the id; with no session open the resolution returns `undefined` rather than throwing.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2) · [alpha.1 `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/service.ts#L69-L76`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/service.ts#L69-L76) · [alpha.2 `packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/service.ts#L53-L67`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/api/session-controller/src/client/sessions/service.ts#L53-L67) · [alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L212-L256`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L212-L256) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L273-L316`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L273-L316) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-slots/src/renderer.ts#L72-L91`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-slots/src/renderer.ts#L72-L91) · [alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-approval/src/client/index.ts#L24`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-approval/src/client/index.ts#L24) · [alpha.2 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-15-client-session-references.md#L80`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-15-client-session-references.md#L80) · first-hand (2026-09-17 upgrade, fixes shipped: [dsh-input-history v0.1.15](https://github.com/dsh-external/dsh-input-history/commits/v0.1.15), [dsh-paste-input v0.1.27](https://github.com/dsh-external/dsh-paste-input/commits/v0.1.27))

cards.title: Global standard props: `useSessionPendingInteraction` is replaced by `useSessionStatus` (plus the new `useSessionRetainInfo`); `useSessions` stays
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A2-02 · Global standard props: `useSessionPendingInteraction` is replaced by `useSessionStatus` (plus the new `useSessionRetainInfo`); `useSessions` stays

- **Type**: breaking
- **Touchpoints**: none (the `GlobalStandardProps` that `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-session` merges into every slot's standard props, including `conversation.input.dock`)
- **Applies to**: Slot components that destructure `useSessionPendingInteraction` from their standard props — first-hand evidence: a resident session-progress strip in `conversation.input.dock` that called it unconditionally
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: On alpha.1 `GlobalStandardProps` held `useSessions` and `useSessionPendingInteraction` (`packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts:104-110`). On alpha.2 it holds `useSessions`, `useSessionStatus` and `useSessionRetainInfo` (`:155-160`): `useSessionPendingInteraction` is gone, `useSessions` remains (its snapshot just lacks `current`, see DSH-0.1.6-A2-01). The dock slot itself is unchanged — `'conversation.input.dock': { kind: 'list'; scope: 'session'; owner: InputZone }` and the session kit `useConversation` / `useInput` / `inputActions` are declared the same way on both tags (`packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts`). A component that calls the missing prop throws at render and takes the whole dock subtree down — first-hand evidence: the progress strip vanished entirely after the host upgrade, and a co-tenant dock entry's chips stopped rendering with it.
- **Migration recipe**: Replace the pending-interaction read with the unified status hook: alpha.1 `useSessionPendingInteraction(snapshot => snapshot.get(sessionId))` (a `ReadonlyMap<SessionId, SessionPendingInteraction>`) becomes `useSessionStatus(snapshot => snapshot.get(sessionId)?.pendingInteraction)` on alpha.2, whose `SessionStatus` record also carries `running` and `completionUnread` (`:56-70`; architecture note `2026-09-15-client-session-references.md:92-102` says Workspace status indicators and composer selection moved to `useSessionStatus` for the same reason). To serve both hosts from one build, pick the hook by which prop the host supplies — the set of props is fixed per host, so the branch is stable across renders — and degrade to an empty state when neither is present. `useSessionRetainInfo(sessionId, selector)` / `useSessionRetainInfo(selector)` is the new public way to read reference counts such as `retainedBy.mainView`.
- **Verification**: The dock renders on both hosts with no console throw from the dock subtree; on alpha.2 a pending approval in the session shows up through `useSessionStatus`, and on alpha.1 through `useSessionPendingInteraction`.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2) · [alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L103-L118`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L103-L118) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L155-L160`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L155-L160) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L50-L80`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-session/src/client/index.ts#L50-L80) · [alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L165`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L165) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L188`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L188) · [alpha.2 `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L241-L248`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/slots.ts#L241-L248) · [alpha.2 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-15-client-session-references.md#L88-L102`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-15-client-session-references.md#L88-L102) · first-hand (2026-09-17 upgrade; [dsh-ui-progress v0.10.2](https://github.com/dsh-external/dsh-ui-progress/commits/v0.10.2) shipped with the optional-seat fix)

cards.title: New Plugin Manager service manages profile bundles and patch-row toggles; link-installed plugins stay outside its bundle management
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A2-03 · New Plugin Manager service manages profile bundles and patch-row toggles; link-installed plugins stay outside its bundle management

- **Type**: behavior
- **Touchpoints**: none (host plugin-manager surface; plugin install topology)
- **Applies to**: Plugins installed the legacy way — a repo junction/symlink into the profile's `node_modules` plus a manual `cordis.patch.yml` insert row — and plugin authors deciding how users should install them on alpha.2
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: alpha.2 adds `packages/boot/plugin-manager` (absent on alpha.1) behind the Web sidebar's **Plugins** page and the `plugin_manager` tool. Per its README, it manages the current profile's *bundles* and their uniquely addressable rows: a bundle toggle edits the ordered `dsh.profile.bundles` list in the profile directory's `package.json`; install and remove run pnpm in the profile directory (a failed or cancelled install restores `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`); a plugin-row toggle updates only `disabled` in the last matching override in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, or appends one; `listBundles` leaves out an unselected plain dependency; changes apply immediately only with HMR enabled, otherwise at restart. There is no separate plugin store directory — earlier drafts of this card named `~/.dsh/community-plugins`, which does not exist upstream. First-hand observation (2026-09-17, not upstream documentation): six link-installed plugins with hand-written patch insert rows all kept loading and serving their bundles, but the Plugins page did not manage them as bundles, so the real-time toggle appeared not to apply to them even though the plugins worked.
- **Migration recipe**: To be fully managed, ship the plugin as a package that declares a bundle and install it through the Plugins page, the `plugin_manager` tool, or `dsh plugin` — it then lands in the profile's `package.json` / `dsh.profile.bundles` and pnpm lockfile. Or keep the link install and manage it by editing the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (a `disabled` override on the row) plus an HMR reload or host restart. Runtime unload still requires the plugin's own dispose paths to be fiber-clean (listener/effect pairs), which the upgrade is a good moment to re-verify.
- **Verification**: After installing through the manager, the profile `package.json` lists the bundle under `dsh.profile.bundles` and toggling it in the Plugins page changes that list; toggling a row writes a `disabled` override into the profile `cordis.patch.yml`. A link-installed plugin shows up (or not) according to that model, matching the chosen install topology.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2) · [alpha.2 `packages/boot/plugin-manager/README.md#L12-L46`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/boot/plugin-manager/README.md#L12-L46) · [alpha.2 `packages/boot/plugin-manager/README.md#L98-L123`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2/packages/boot/plugin-manager/README.md#L98-L123) · [alpha.1 `packages/boot/` (no `plugin-manager`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.1/packages/boot) · first-hand (2026-09-17 upgrade: six legacy-installed plugins all loaded and served their bundles while being unmanaged by the new page)
