cards.title: npm publish lags the GitHub release; pinned upgrades hit an E404 window
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.6-A2-04 · npm publish lags the GitHub release; pinned upgrades hit an E404 window

- **Type**: behavior
- **Touchpoints**: none (release engineering; install channel)
- **Applies to**: Anyone upgrading `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>` within hours of a GitHub pre-release; update automation that pins exact versions
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2` was published on GitHub releases (tag `ddefc45`) but `npm view @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.6-alpha.2` returned E404 for at least the first minutes-to-hours; `dist-tags.alpha` still pointed at 0.1.6-alpha.1. An upgrade attempt in that window fails with "No match found for version".
- **Migration recipe**: Poll `npm view` until the version resolves before killing the running host — never start the stop-host phase against an unpublished version. Fallbacks (build from the git tag) are discouraged: the repository root is a private pnpm monorepo (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-root`), so a git/tree install does not produce the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh` package and hand-built trees violate the formal-install rule.
- **Verification**: `npm view @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version> version` resolves before starting the upgrade; after install, `dsh --version` prints exactly the pinned version.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2) · first-hand (2026-09-17: E404 observed through three polls ~7 minutes after the GitHub release; npm alpha tag still `0.1.6-alpha.1`)

cards.title: Client UI primitives icon set renamed: every `*16` export is gone
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-01 · Client UI primitives icon set renamed: every `*16` export is gone

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: client plugins rendering primitives icons (Web surface)
- **Touchpoints**: none (the host `dsh-client-ui-primitives` static module's export surface)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: a slot contribution that destructures any `Icon...16` named export gets `undefined` and crashes on render with React error #130 (element type invalid); the framework's slot-level error boundary unmounts the WHOLE slot entry, so the user-visible symptom is an entire surface (dock, header widget) silently vanishing with one minified console error and no request failures. First-hand fleet evidence (2026-09-22, `dsh-ui-progress` on Windows/Edge): the resident input-dock progress strip disappeared after the host upgrade; the crash surfaced in `conversation.input.dock` and the four destructured `*16` icons were the only breakage.
- **Migration recipe**: enumerate every named import from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` in the plugin source; for each `...16` icon, look up the replacement in the target tag's primitives export surface (the 0.1.7 set observed: `IconDatabaseOutline16` -> `IconDatabaseOutlineMedium`/`IconDatabaseOutlineRegular`, `IconLoadingOutline16` -> `IconLoadingOutlineMedium`/`...Regular`, `IconWarningOutline16` -> `IconWarningOutlineMedium`/`...Regular`, `IconSparkle16` -> `IconSparkleMedium`/`...Regular`; re-check the target tag - the variant split may widen). Plugins that must run on both pre- and post-rename hosts resolve the component at runtime through a fallback chain (`*16` -> `*Medium` -> `*Regular`) instead of static named imports, and extend their unit-test module mocks with every fallback name (strict module mocks throw on undefined-export access, which masks the real failure).
- **Verification**: in a driven browser against the upgraded host, assert all three: the surface's DOM marker is present, zero `slot entry crashed` console records, and the expected network requests fire. A single "CSS loaded, no errors" check has false negatives.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1); primitives export surface at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`); first-hand: dsh-external/dsh-ui-progress v0.10.3.
- **See also**: DSH-0.1.7-J1-26 in the version-jump companion [jump-0.1.5-rc.2-to-0.1.7-rc.1.md](jump-0.1.5-rc.2-to-0.1.7-rc.1.md) (the same rename seen from `0.1.5-rc.2`, with the full `Outline14`/`Fill14` and `ReferenceIcon`/`LinkIcon`/`PermissionIcon` mapping).

cards.title: `workspaceFiles` reads unify on `readBytes`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-02 · `workspaceFiles` reads unify on `readBytes`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: client/server plugins reading workspace file content through the `workspaceFiles` Remote namespace
- **Touchpoints**: #4 (Remote namespace calls) or direct service calls
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: reads through the retired read methods stop working (or fail type checks at build time against the new host types).
- **Migration recipe**: the release notes state the direction only (workspace file reads unify to readBytes; plugins must migrate the old interface) - do NOT invent call signatures: open `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-files` at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1` (Remote types + Host service) and migrate each old read call to the `readBytes` contract (parameter shape, return envelope, chunking) from the tag's declared types. Grep the plugin for `workspaceFiles.read`, `readAll`, `readText`, `readRelated` and re-derive each against the tag.
- **Verification**: exercise one real file read through the migrated path against a 0.1.7 host and assert the bytes match the on-disk file.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1); `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-files` types at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1`.

cards.title: Settings move into the current Profile's plugin configuration
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-03 · Settings move into the current Profile's plugin configuration

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that persist user settings, and any plugin reading the legacy global settings file
- **Touchpoints**: #6 (settings/config surfaces), profile files
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: settings written through the legacy global settings file stop being read after the one-time import; live edits to undeclared fields do not reach a running plugin.
- **Migration recipe**: per the release notes, settings are now saved through the current Profile's plugin configuration and the legacy settings.yaml is attempted exactly once - verify after upgrading that the values the plugin depends on actually landed in the new store (do not assume the import covered plugin-specific namespaces). If the plugin ships its own settings plugin/config surface, declare its fields so no-reload live updates apply; re-check the declaration mechanism against tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1` types before shipping.
- **Verification**: change one plugin setting in the UI, restart the host, assert the value survives; and confirm the one-time import carried the plugin's previously stored values.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1).

cards.title: Agent presets are declared and installed by plugin bundles
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-04 · Agent presets are declared and installed by plugin bundles

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins shipping agent presets, and presets authored in the legacy preset directory
- **Touchpoints**: composition (bundle-declared presets), profile files
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: presets in the old preset directory no longer appear; the settings page removes copy/delete/open-directory entries.
- **Migration recipe**: move preset declarations into the plugin bundle per the mechanism at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1` (re-check the exact bundle declaration fields in the target tag's types / shipped bundle examples - the release notes give the direction only). Authoring via creation mode remains; the settings page keeps viewing and selection.
- **Verification**: after migration, the preset appears in the settings page selector and a session started with it mounts the expected tools/prompt.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1).

cards.title: Session log format V4 with a batch migration tool
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-05 · Session log format V4 with a batch migration tool

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that parse session log files directly; everyone else via host compatibility
- **Touchpoints**: none (session persistence plane), or direct log parsing in the plugin
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**: none for plugins that read session data through host services; direct log parsers may meet V4 records (including turn-end records synthesized for compatibility with some V3 sessions).
- **Migration recipe**: if the plugin parses raw session logs, re-check the V4 record shapes at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1` and the batch migration tool the release ships; prefer routing reads through host services so format versions stay an implementation detail. Per the released session-format status, versions are additive generations - never write down-version.
- **Verification**: open a migrated V4 session and a not-yet-migrated V3 session; both render through the plugin's read path.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1); session-format status doc in the harness repository.

cards.title: Official DeepSeek adapter is Messages-API only
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-06 · Official DeepSeek adapter is Messages-API only

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile/composition files configuring the official DeepSeek provider
- **Touchpoints**: none (provider config)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: profiles carrying the removed `protocol` option fail or mis-route against the Messages-only adapter.
- **Migration recipe**: delete the `protocol` key from the official DeepSeek provider config and point the base URL at a Messages-compatible address. Third-party OpenAI-completions providers configured through `llm-pi-ai` are unaffected (their `api: openai-completions` selection is a different seam).
- **Verification**: one chat round-trip on the official provider after migration.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1).

cards.title: Plugin bundles support multiple ordered patch files and no-reload config fields
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-07 · Plugin bundles support multiple ordered patch files and no-reload config fields - **Type**: capability - **Applies to**: plugin packaging; plugins with configuration surfaces - **Touchpoints**: #7 (bundle patch composition) - **Action level**: optional - **Symptoms**: none (additive). Single-file cordis.patch.yml keeps working. - **Migration recipe**: to split a growing patch, declare the ordered patch-file list per the packaging contract at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1` (re-check the exact declaration key in the target tag). To keep a running instance alive across config edits, mark the fields the plugin can re-read live as no-reload fields in the same declaration. - **Verification**: boot with the split patches and confirm the composed tree equals the single-file composition (`dsh --profile

--dump-config`); edit a declared no-reload field and assert the instance is not restarted. - **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1).

cards.title: Tolerant Profile loading: unreadable optional bundles no longer abort the Profile
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-08 · Tolerant Profile loading: unreadable optional bundles no longer abort the Profile

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: profile composition; every installed plugin's failure visibility
- **Touchpoints**: none (loader behavior)
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: a plugin whose package cannot be read no longer crashes the whole boot; the Profile loads without it, the Plugin Manager keeps the error plus disable/remove controls.
- **Migration recipe**: none for the plugin. Two awareness items for fleet maintainers: (1) after a host upgrade, a plugin can be MISSING rather than crashing the boot - check the Plugin Manager page / boot roster instead of assuming no crash means all loaded; (2) this is load-level tolerance only - a plugin that loads but fails activation can still vanish a slot silently (see DSH-0.1.7-A1-01), so keep the fail-loud diagnosis habit.
- **Verification**: on a profile with one deliberately broken bundle, boot succeeds and the Plugin Manager shows the error entry.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1).

cards.title: Plugins can declare locale-aware title/description and a package.json icon
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-09 · Plugins can declare locale-aware title/description and a package.json icon

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: plugin packaging (Plugin Manager display)
- **Touchpoints**: #7 (packaging metadata)
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: none (additive).
- **Migration recipe**: add the locale title/description structure and the package.json icon field per the contract at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1` (re-check exact field names in the target tag); the Plugin Manager renders them.
- **Verification**: the Plugin Manager page shows the localized title/description and icon for the plugin.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1).

cards.title: Attachments stored only in custom events are no longer auto-read or exported
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-10 · Attachments stored only in custom events are no longer auto-read or exported

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins that store attachment payloads in custom session events
- **Touchpoints**: #5 (session events / projections)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: attachment payloads that exist only inside a plugin's custom events are no longer read back or included in exports - the plugin must own their storage and reading.
- **Migration recipe**: per the release notes this is a declared adaptation duty: give the plugin its own durable storage for such attachments (or reference host-delivered attachments instead of duplicating payloads into custom events); re-check the event/export boundary at tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1` before shipping. Audit existing sessions for payloads that would silently drop on export.
- **Verification**: create a session with such an attachment, export the session, and assert the plugin's data survives the export/import round trip (or is intentionally excluded with a surfaced reason).
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1).

cards.title: Two new settings-page seats: `settings.launcher` and `settings.models.sign-in`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A1-11 · Two new settings-page seats: `settings.launcher` and `settings.models.sign-in`

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: client plugins extending the settings panel's opening surface (sidebar account launcher) or the Models settings credential flow (sign-in step)
- **Touchpoints**: #5 (Web Client slots)
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: none (additive). Both seats are optional by contract and render nothing without a registrant.
- **Migration recipe**: `settings.launcher` is a root-scoped `single` seat typed in the `ui-settings` slot contract; the rendering site passes `{ wide, openSettings(), openOnboarding(id) }` and the contribution is the sidebar account launcher that opens the shell-owned settings panel (the settings shell declares the seat in its children). `settings.models.sign-in` is a root-scoped `single` seat in `ui-settings-models`; the site passes `{ complete(), useApiKey() }` and the contribution renders the optional account login choice before the credential editor. Both arrived with the DeepSeek account sign-in integration. Register through `ctx.slots.inject(name, () => ctx.slots.register(...))` so the contribution waits on the declaring plugin's slot declaration (cross-package apply order is unconstrained).
- **Verification**: `packages/client/ui-settings-general/tests/shell.client.spec.ts` covers the shell's launcher seat; in a driven browser, register a stub into each seat and assert it renders inside the settings shell / the Models credential editor.
- **Source**: [alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-settings/src/client/contract/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-settings/src/client/contract/slots.ts) · [alpha.1 `packages/client/ui-settings-models/src/client/slot-contract.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1/packages/client/ui-settings-models/src/client/slot-contract.ts) · [introducing commit 048297321a](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/048297321ad1364557308d360b8e535978ec8876)
- **See also**: DSH-0.1.7-J1-34 in the version-jump companion [jump-0.1.5-rc.2-to-0.1.7-rc.1.md](jump-0.1.5-rc.2-to-0.1.7-rc.1.md) (the same seats seen from `0.1.5-rc.2`).

cards.title: `spill-policy` config: `maxInlineBytes` becomes `maxInlineTokens`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A2-01 · `spill-policy` config: `maxInlineBytes` becomes `maxInlineTokens`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: profile/composition files and plugins carrying a custom `spill-policy` configuration
- **Touchpoints**: #6 (settings/config surfaces)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: a custom `spill-policy` keeps its old `maxInlineBytes` key after the upgrade: the key is no longer read, so the intended retention budget silently falls back to defaults (and MCP images can become unavailable after text truncation, per the release notes).
- **Migration recipe**: rename the key to `maxInlineTokens` and re-express the budget in tokens (there is no fixed bytes-to-tokens ratio — re-set the number for your content, do not just reuse the old byte value). The new retention keeps the head AND tail of tool-result text and images within one shared estimated-token budget, and omitted content gets a readable access path. A spill-policy without either key is unaffected.
- **Verification**: trigger a tool result long enough to spill; assert the retained head+tail lengths match the new token budget and that an MCP image referenced after truncation still renders.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2).
- **See also**: DSH-0.1.7-J1-13 in the version-jump companion [jump-0.1.5-rc.2-to-0.1.7-rc.1.md](jump-0.1.5-rc.2-to-0.1.7-rc.1.md) (same change seen from `0.1.5-rc.2`; records the shipped baseline moving `50000` → `12500`).

cards.title: Vendored dependency auto-updates pin to same-minor patch releases
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A2-02 · Vendored dependency auto-updates pin to same-minor patch releases

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugin installs whose dependency resolution pulls vendored packages (Cordis and the vendored set) or Node Addon System
- **Touchpoints**: #7 (packaging/dependency resolution)
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: installing or updating plugins no longer auto-introduces a NEW minor of Cordis/other vendored packages or Node Addon System: automatic updates are restricted to patch releases within the same minor. Installs that previously jumped minors silently now stay pinned.
- **Migration recipe**: no plugin action. Awareness for fleet maintainers: after upgrading hosts and re-installing plugins, expect vendored-dependency versions in lockfiles to stay within the same minor; a lockfile diff showing a minor jump indicates an explicit dependency somewhere, not the auto-update.
- **Verification**: run the plugin install once and diff the lockfile: vendored packages and node-addon-system must change only within patch range.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2).

cards.title: First plugin installation auto-selects the most responsive npm registry
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A2-03 · First plugin installation auto-selects the most responsive npm registry

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: plugin installation UX (Plugin Manager installs)
- **Touchpoints**: #7 (packaging/installs)
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: none (additive). Previously the first install with no configured registry could fail or hang on an unreachable default.
- **Migration recipe**: no plugin action. On first install with no source configured, the host now probes and prefers the most responsive accessible npm registry; manual selection and private-registry settings are preserved. Air-gapped or proxy environments that relied on the old default should verify which registry gets selected (or pre-configure one).
- **Verification**: perform a first install on a clean profile; assert it succeeds without manual registry selection and the chosen registry is recorded.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2).

cards.title: Web pages reconnect automatically after a server restart; client bundles are cached at host boot
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-A2-04 · Web pages reconnect automatically after a server restart; client bundles are cached at host boot

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: fleet verification workflows after a host upgrade (all client plugins)
- **Touchpoints**: none (host transport and module serving behavior)
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: (1) After a Web-server restart, an already-open page now reconnects and resumes displaying replies automatically — the old manual refresh is no longer required for connectivity. (2) Client plugin bundles are read and cached when the host boots: editing a served `lib/client.js` on disk NO LONGER takes effect on page refresh alone (0.1.6-era behavior); only a host restart serves the new bytes.
- **Migration recipe**: no plugin action. Two workflow consequences for anyone patching or hot-fixing client bundles in the install tree (first-hand 2026-09-23 evidence across the 0.1.7 window): a client-bundle edit requires a host RESTART before the page sees it — a refresh-only verification reports stale content and can mislead a diagnosis; and the auto-reconnect means an open page may keep working across a restart even while it is running pre-restart client bytes, so verify the served bundle content itself (fetch the combo URL and inspect), not just that the page responds.
- **Verification**: edit one byte of a served client bundle; refresh the page and assert the change is NOT served; restart the host, refresh, and assert it IS served. For the reconnect: restart the host and assert the open page resumes receiving replies without a manual refresh.
- **Source**: [dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2 release notes](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases/tag/dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2); first-hand install-tree observation 2026-09-23 (combo route served pre-edit bytes after refresh, post-edit bytes only after host restart).

cards.title: DSH peer ranges are enforced at install and at startup; `^0.1.7` does not admit `0.1.7-rc.1`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-RC1-01 · DSH peer ranges are enforced at install and at startup; `^0.1.7` does not admit `0.1.7-rc.1` - **Type**: breaking - **Applies to**: every plugin package and plugin bundle that declares a `peerDependencies` key named `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`; fleet install scripts that drive `dsh plugin add` / `install` - **Touchpoints**: none (packaging/dependencies special surface — pre-flight §0 `peerDependencies` inventory); #7 when a script parses `dsh plugin` exit status or stderr - **Action level**: required-if-hit - **Symptoms**: - **What is checked.** Up to alpha.2 a DSH peer range was advisory. From rc.1, app-boot compares each DSH peer range against the one runtime version (the app-boot `package.json` version, `0.1.7-rc.1`). The check is `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`, using the `semver ^7.8.5` app-boot depends on. - **Install time.** `dsh plugin --profile

add ` refuses a mismatching plugin before pnpm runs and exits 1. stderr shows `dsh: installation rejected: Plugin @ is incompatible with dsh 0.1.7-rc.1: peerDependencies {...}. Running it may cause crashes or data loss. …`, then `dsh: nothing was installed.`, then a ready-made `allow-version` command. - **Startup.** An already-installed mismatching plugin row is disabled in the launcher's in-memory copy: stderr shows `dsh: disabling profile plugin row "": Plugin … is incompatible …`. The profile files are not modified, so the row silently stops mounting. - **The semver 7.8.3 trap.** Starting with semver 7.8.3, `^0.1.7` under `includePrerelease` expands to `>=0.1.7 <0.2.0-0`; 7.8.0–7.8.2 and 7.7.x still expanded it to `>=0.1.7-0 …` and admitted `0.1.7-rc.1`. So on a host that resolves semver ≥ 7.8.3 (app-boot declares `^7.8.5`), a plugin whose floor is already written as `^0.1.7` is refused by every 0.1.7 prerelease. Only the caret form depends on the semver version: `~0.1.7` and `>=0.1.7` are refused by every semver version, with or without `includePrerelease`. Measured against `0.1.7-rc.1` with semver 7.8.5 and `{ includePrerelease: true }`: | Result | Ranges | |---|---| | Refused | `^0.1.7`, `~0.1.7`, `>=0.1.7`, `0.1.7`, `0.1.7-alpha.2` (exact prerelease pins), `^0.1.8`, `""` | | Admitted | `^0.1.7-0`, `~0.1.7-0`, `^0.1.7-rc.1`, `^0.1.7-alpha.2`, `^0.1.6`, `~0.1.6`, `^0.1.5`, `^0.1.5-rc.2`, `0.1.x`, `>=0.1.5`, `>=0.1.5 <0.1.7`, `<0.2.0`, `*` | - **Migration recipe**: 1. **Inventory.** List every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` key in the plugin's `peerDependencies`. Other `@deepseek-ai/*` keys (for example `@deepseek-ai/cordis`), `dependencies` and `engines` are not checked, and a plugin with no DSH peer is never refused. 2. **If the target host is a 0.1.7 prerelease**, rewrite each refused floor so it admits prereleases: - `^0.1.7` / `~0.1.7` / `>=0.1.7` → `^0.1.7-0` (or `^0.1.7-rc.1` to exclude older alphas); - exact pins → a caret range. This relaxes the "no `-rc` suffix survives" rule in [precision-checklist.md](precision-checklist.md#peer-version-floors--exact-values-not-newer-carets): that rule was written for a final-release target cohort. When the target is itself a prerelease, the floor must carry a prerelease tag or sit below the target minor. 3. **Keep `workspace:^` / `workspace:~` / `workspace:*`** in source launches. They are treated as the running version and always pass. 4. **Keep every peer value a string.** A non-string value makes the manifest unverifiable, and the plugin is refused. 5. **Only if you deliberately run a mismatching build**, grant an exemption for the exact plugin version and the exact DSH version: ```sh dsh plugin --profile

allow-version @ --dsh-version 0.1.7-rc.1 --accept-risk ``` Then retry the install or restart. Grants are stored in `/compatibility.json` as `{ "@": [""] }`. They are not carried over when either the plugin or DSH changes version. - Review grants with `dsh plugin --profile

version-exemptions`; revoke with `revoke-version @ --dsh-version `. - In the plugin manager, the matching `plugin_manager` tool actions are `list_version_exemptions` / `set_version_exemption` (`acceptRisk: true`), and the Remote methods are `listVersionExemptions()` / `setVersionExemption(...)`. - An exemption does not authorize dependency scripts. - **Verification**: `--dump-config` is not enough to prove a plugin still mounts. - **The trap.** After a denial the row still appears in `dsh --profile

--dump-config` exactly as before, and nothing is written to stderr. Only an incompatible plugin **bundle** drops out of the dump (it is skipped like an unreadable bundle). - **Instead:** - boot the target host once and assert its stderr has no `disabling profile plugin row` line for your ids; - for install paths, assert `dsh plugin add` exits 0 with no `installation rejected`. - This also applies to the `plugin-release` skill's step 1.4, whose `--dump-config` row check cannot detect a denial on rc.1 and later. - **Source**: [2c67633990](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/2c67633990) `feat(plugins): enforce DSH peer compatibility with exact exemptions`, [747c98b0db](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/747c98b0db) `fix(plugins): deny incompatible bundles and clarify compatibility refusals`, [51d70c5f5c](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/51d70c5f5c) `feat(plugins): report incompatible versions as typed refusals`, [f64c57dbb2](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/f64c57dbb2); [`packages/boot/app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts), [`packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-compatibility.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-compatibility.ts), [`packages/boot/app-boot/src/compatibility-preflight.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/compatibility-preflight.ts) and [`packages/boot/plugin-manager/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/boot/plugin-manager/README.md) ("Version compatibility and exemptions") at `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1`. - **Field note** (first-hand, 2026-09-23): `npm i @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.7-rc.1` in a clean directory resolved `semver@7.8.5`. In an isolated `DSH_HOME`, four local fixtures, each declaring only `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, were installed with `dsh plugin --profile probe add ./fixture`. | Fixture peer | Install result | |---|---| | `>=0.1.5 <0.1.7` | installed | | `^0.1.7` | refused, exit 1, profile `package.json` untouched | | `~0.1.7` | refused, exit 1, profile `package.json` untouched | | `0.1.7-alpha.2` | refused, exit 1, profile `package.json` untouched | - `allow-version … --accept-risk` wrote `compatibility.json`, after which the `^0.1.7` install succeeded. - With the `^0.1.7` row inserted through `cordis.patch.yml` and the grant revoked, `--dump-config` still printed the row with an empty stderr, while a real boot printed `dsh: disabling profile plugin row "probe-caret": …`. - The same semver matrix under 7.7.4 and 7.8.0–7.8.2 admits `^0.1.7` (`~0.1.7` and `>=0.1.7` stay refused in every version). Any compatibility pre-check a fleet runs with its own semver copy must use semver ≥ 7.8.3 (ideally the host's own `^7.8.5`) **and** call it the way the host does, `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`. With an older copy it passes `^0.1.7` plugins the host then refuses; without `includePrerelease` every range is checked against prerelease-excluding rules and the admitted column above no longer matches the host.

cards.title: `tool.call.toolview` owners become a phase union; `RunningToolCall` splits into preparing and started calls
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-RC1-02 · `tool.call.toolview` owners become a phase union; `RunningToolCall` splits into preparing and started calls

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that register a keyed `tool.call.toolview` entry, or that read `RunningToolCall` / `ToolCallBlock` from `ui-conversation` / `ui-chat`
- **Touchpoints**: #5 (UI slots / tool views)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**:
  - **New preparing stage.** Tool calls now render in three stages: `preparing` (the model has named the tool but its arguments are still streaming), `start` and `result`. Registered keyed views are rendered during `preparing` too.
  - **Record type split** (`ui-conversation` `contract/records.ts`). `RunningToolCall` used to be one interface that always carried `argsRaw`. It is now `PreparingToolCall | StartedToolCall`, discriminated by `phase: 'preparing' | 'start'`, and `argsRaw` exists only on `StartedToolCall`.
    - Both variants share `callId`, `parentCallId?`, `name`, `turn`, `step`, `subCalls`, and `time` (now "when this stage began").
  - **Owner props** (`ui-tool` `contract/slots.ts`). `ToolCallOwnerProps` used to be one interface with `block: ToolCallBlock`. It is now `ToolCallCommonProps & ToolCallPhaseProps`, where the phase part is `{ phase: 'preparing', block: PreparingToolCall } | { phase: 'start', block: StartedToolCall } | { phase: 'result', block: ToolResultNode }`.
  - **What breaks.**
    - A view that reads `block.argsRaw` without narrowing no longer typechecks.
    - At runtime during live streaming, the same view receives a preparing block whose `argsRaw` is `undefined`. `JSON.parse(undefined)` throws, and so does `argsRaw.length`.
    - Preparing calls render no sub-calls.
    - Reloaded history goes straight from start to result, so a view that only looks correct on reload can still crash live.
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. Narrow on `props.phase` before touching `block.argsRaw` or dispatched-call material.
  2. Render a light placeholder (tool name, spinner) for `'preparing'`.
  3. To show arguments as they stream, add `inject: { hooks: { toolCallArgumentsPartial } }` to the toolview entry. Then call the injected hook `useToolCallArgumentsPartial()`: it returns the raw argument prefix (a partial JSON string, so do not `JSON.parse` it blindly) and an empty string outside `preparing`.
  4. Existing argument/result components that never want the preparing stage can be typed with the new `StartedToolCallViewProps`, which excludes it; gate their use on `props.phase !== 'preparing'`.

  New exports: `ToolCallCommonProps`, `ToolCallPhaseProps`, `StartedToolCallViewProps`, `ToolCallHookContext`, `ToolCallInjected`, `UseToolCallArgumentsPartial` from `ui-tool`; `PreparingToolCall`, `StartedToolCall` from `ui-conversation` (re-exported by `ui-chat`).
- **Verification**: typecheck against the rc.1 `ui-tool` / `ui-conversation` types. Then trigger your tool live with arguments large enough to stream for a visible moment, and assert that the view shows the preparing placeholder with no page error, and that the start and result views match the pre-upgrade rendering.
- **Source**: [d3086e6571](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/d3086e6571) `feat(chat): present tools in preparing, start, and result stages`; [`.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-22-tool-call-three-phases.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-22-tool-call-three-phases.md); [`packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/records.ts), [`packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/contract/slots.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/contract/slots.ts), [`packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/tool/tool-call-arguments-partial.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/tool/tool-call-arguments-partial.ts) at `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1`.

cards.title: Conversation Definitions: transient events may start a Context; a repeated start becomes an update
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-RC1-03 · Conversation Definitions: transient events may start a Context; a repeated start becomes an update

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that implement a custom `ConversationNodeDefinition` (`UiConversation.events`)
- **Touchpoints**: #5 (UI conversation nodes); #2 when the Definition matches plugin-owned session events
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**:
  - **Transient starts accepted.** `ConversationStartMatch` changes from `ConversationMatchOf<SessionEvent, 'start'>` to `ConversationMatchOf<SessionEventLike, 'start'>`: a Client-only transient event (for example a live chunk) may now start a Context. alpha.2 rejected transient starts.
  - **Later starts become updates.** The earliest currently loaded start initializes State. Every later Match, including another `role: 'start'` for the same id, goes to `update()`. The assembler no longer throws on a second start, so accidental id reuse across logically distinct nodes is no longer detected — the two merge silently into one Context.
  - **Settlement.** Settlement recomputes a Context from its remaining earliest start. A Context whose only start was transient and has been removed has no State.
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. Make `update()` accept a Match whose role is `start`: treat it as a restatement, not an error.
  2. If `start()` assumed a durable `SessionEvent` (for example reading `seq` ordering or durable-only fields), handle the transient `SessionEventLike` shape, or return `null` from `match()` for transient events you never want as a start.
  3. Make Definition ids unique per logical node, since collisions are no longer reported.
- **Verification**: stream a turn that produces your node live; assert a single node is rendered. Reload the session and assert the same node and state rebuild from durable events alone.
- **Source**: [d550f1c4af](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/d550f1c4af) `feat(conversation): initialize contexts from transient start matches`; [`packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/conversation.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/contract/conversation.ts) and [`packages/client/ui-conversation/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/client/ui-conversation/README.md) at `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1`.

cards.title: Work-detail setting gains four modes; the default moves from `compact` to `standard`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-RC1-04 · Work-detail setting gains four modes; the default moves from `compact` to `standard`

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: Web Client plugins that read or write the chat `transcriptView` setting, or branch on `TranscriptViewMode`; fleet screenshots/snapshot baselines of the chat transcript
- **Touchpoints**: #5 (UI settings consumers)
- **Action level**: conditional
- **Symptoms**:
  - **Mode list.** In `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ui-chat` `chat-settings.ts`, `TRANSCRIPT_VIEW_MODES` goes from `['compact', 'detailed', 'expanded']` to `['compact', 'standard', 'detailed', 'verbose']`.
  - **Default.** `DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_VIEW_MODE` goes from `compact` to `standard`.
  - **Legacy values.**
    - A saved `expanded` is read as `detailed` and never written back (`LEGACY_EXPANDED_TRANSCRIPT_VIEW_MODE`).
    - The two-mode legacy value `normal` is read as `standard` (`LEGACY_TRANSCRIPT_VIEW_MODE`).
    - Missing or unrecognized values fall back to `standard`.
  - **What breaks.**
    - Code with a `switch` over the old three modes has no `standard` or `verbose` branch.
    - Code that writes `expanded` no longer gets an offered mode.
    - Screenshots of users with no explicit preference change, because the default is no longer `compact`.
- **Migration recipe**:
  - Handle all four modes.
  - Write only values from `TRANSCRIPT_VIEW_MODES`.
  - Import the constants instead of hard-coding strings.
  - Re-baseline transcript snapshots taken under the old implicit `compact` default, or pin `transcriptView` explicitly in the test profile.
- **Verification**: open settings and cycle all four modes with your plugin's UI mounted; assert no fallback branch is hit. Start a profile with no saved preference and assert it renders as `standard`.
- **Source**: [015a9b202c](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/015a9b202c) `feat(chat): add four work detail modes and legacy mappings`; [`packages/client/ui-chat/src/chat-settings.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/client/ui-chat/src/chat-settings.ts) at `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1`.

cards.title: Plugin Manager bounds silent pnpm runs and prechecks GitHub reachability before installing
cards.text:
### DSH-0.1.7-RC1-05 · Plugin Manager bounds silent pnpm runs and prechecks GitHub reachability before installing

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: service-driven plugin installs (plugin manager tool / Remote); plugins installed from GitHub specs; automation that interprets install failures
- **Touchpoints**: #7 (subprocess output and failure classification)
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**:
  - **Silent-run timeout.** A service-driven pnpm run whose captured output stays silent for `idleTimeoutMs` (default `600000`) is terminated along with its whole process tree. It reports `timedOut`, is classified `timeout` whatever exit status the signal left behind, is not retried on the next registry, and restores the profile files.
    - A run now completes when its process exits; the pipes then get a bounded drain, so a lifecycle-script descendant can no longer hold the operation (and the profile lock) open.
    - `dsh plugin` on the CLI inherits the terminal and remains unbounded.
  - **GitHub precheck.** Installs from GitHub repository specs first run `git ls-remote`, bounded by `githubConnectionTimeoutMs` (default `5000`), with credential helpers and prompts disabled.
    - Only network failures and timeouts stop the install; they report `failedAt: 'spec-host'` and offer mirror recovery.
    - Authentication and lookup failures are still left to pnpm, including its HTTPS-to-SSH fallback.
    - Registry, path, tarball and non-GitHub Git specs skip the check.
- **Migration recipe**: no plugin action.
  - Plugins whose install runs a long, silent postinstall (native builds, large downloads without progress output) should print progress or document raising `idleTimeoutMs`.
  - Automation that retried on generic failures should treat `timeout` and `failedAt: 'spec-host'` as distinct, non-transient-by-registry outcomes.
- **Verification**: for a plugin with a heavy postinstall, run the service-driven install once and assert it completes without a `timeout` classification. For a GitHub spec behind a blocked network, assert the failure names `spec-host` within about 5 s rather than hanging.
- **Source**: [ccaa0dc11c](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/ccaa0dc11c) `fix(plugin-manager): bound pnpm runs so a silent child cannot hold the profile lock (#4982)`, [0edfe83573](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/0edfe83573) `fix(plugin-manager): bound GitHub connection checks before installation`, [d6e5b7e41a](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/d6e5b7e41a), [75d74a055e](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/75d74a055e); [`packages/boot/plugin-manager/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1/packages/boot/plugin-manager/README.md) (configuration table and operations section) at `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1`.

---

## Coverage notes

Checked on this edge and deliberately left without a card (host-internal, or no plugin-facing contract change):

- 1dc518f217: the experimental `agent-team` Web Team panel is now driven by a durable-only `agentTeam` projection. Its refresh button and Remote mount are removed; the `agentTeams/view` Remote remains.
- 4aa207c5fe: the preset creator skill gains a `references/practices.md` on plugin practices (waterfall delegation, `agent.ctx` ownership, session projections, slot-based UI with theme tokens). This is guidance only; no runtime change.
- 4cfd292a7b gateway stream-cancellation retention bound; 68e43b173e Windows `native-command` path opening via the shell; 5e25475857 bundled LibreOffice Kit 0.1.0 CLI; i18n and UI polish.

cards.title: Host packages cross to 0.2.0-rc.1; every `^0.1.x`-floored DSH peer is refused, and `^0.2.0` does not admit `0.2.0-rc.1`
cards.text:
### DSH-0.2.0-RC1-01 · Host packages cross to 0.2.0-rc.1; every `^0.1.x`-floored DSH peer is refused, and `^0.2.0` does not admit `0.2.0-rc.1`

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: every plugin whose `peerDependencies` declares `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` (the enforcement mechanism itself shipped in 0.1.7-rc.1 — [DSH-0.1.7-RC1-01](v0.1.7-rc.1.md); what is new here is the version boundary)
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging/dependencies special surface — pre-flight §0 `peerDependencies` inventory)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**:
  - Upgrading the host from any 0.1.x to `0.2.0-rc.1` disables every installed plugin whose DSH peer floor is `^0.1.x`: stderr shows `dsh: disabling profile plugin row "<id>": Plugin … is incompatible with dsh 0.2.0-rc.1: peerDependencies {...}`. The profile files are unchanged; the row silently stops mounting.
  - **The naive fix is refused too.** `^0.2.0` expands (semver ≥ 7.8.3, `includePrerelease: true`) to `>=0.2.0 <0.3.0-0`, and `0.2.0-rc.1 < 0.2.0` — so the rc host itself does not satisfy it. Measured against `0.2.0-rc.1` with the shipped `semver`:

    | Result | Ranges |
    |---|---|
    | Refused | `^0.1.0`, `^0.2.0`, `^0.1.0 \|\| ^0.2.0` |
    | Admitted | `^0.2.0-rc.1`, `>=0.1.0 <0.3.0`, `>=0.1.0 <0.3.0-0`, `*`, `workspace:*` / `workspace:^` (treated as the running version) |

    `^0.2.0-rc.1` also admits the future `0.2.0` final and 0.2.x patches, so it is the recommended floor form for the whole 0.2 window.
- **Migration recipe**:
  1. Rewrite each DSH peer as `^0.1.0 || ^0.2.0-rc.1` (keeps 0.1.x hosts installable) or `^0.2.0-rc.1` (0.2-only).
  2. Ship the peer fix as a plugin release; the host re-reads the installed `package.json` on the next boot — no exemption needed.
  3. If you must run a mismatching build now, `dsh plugin allow-version <name>@<version> --dsh-version 0.2.0-rc.1 --accept-risk` (profile-scoped, exact-version; see [DSH-0.1.7-RC1-01](v0.1.7-rc.1.md#dsh-017-rc1-01--dsh-peer-ranges-are-enforced-at-install-and-at-startup-017-does-not-admit-017-rc1) for the full grant mechanics).
- **Verification**: restart the host and assert stderr has no `disabling profile plugin row` line for your ids; `--dump-config` cannot detect a denial (see the rc.1 card's Verification section).
- **Source**: all `packages/*/package.json` version bumps at `dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1`; checker unchanged from rc.1 ([`packages/boot/app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1/packages/boot/app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts)).
- **Field note** (first-hand, 2026-09-28): `@dsh-external/dsh-vision` (registers `view_image`) was disabled twice on the upgrade path — v0.1.0 with `^0.1.0`, then v0.1.1 with `^0.2.0` — and mounts again after shipping v0.1.1 with `^0.1.0 || ^0.2.0-rc.1`. The other six fleet plugins carry no DSH peers and were never refused.

cards.title: Web work-details default moves to `detailed`; the saved `transcriptView` setting becomes optional
cards.text:
### DSH-0.2.0-RC1-02 · Web work-details default moves to `detailed`; the saved `transcriptView` setting becomes optional

- **Type**: behavior
- **Applies to**: plugins that read the Chat settings schema (`transcriptView`) or assume the `standard` default; browser surfaces rendering transcripts
- **Touchpoints**: #5 (UI — Chat settings schema) if your plugin mirrors the field
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: fresh Web clients (non-Desktop) now render `detailed` work details; the schema field becomes optional (`transcriptView?`) and the schema no longer carries a `.default(...)` — absence defers to the client default (`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_VIEW_MODE = 'detailed'`, or `standard` when `dshDesktop` is present). The legacy saved value `normal` now maps to `detailed` instead of `standard` (`expanded` already mapped to `detailed`).
- **Migration recipe**: plugins that hard-code a `standard` fallback should not assume a schema default any more — treat an absent value as "client default" (`DEFAULT_TRANSCRIPT_VIEW_MODE` on Web, `standard` on Desktop); plugins that persist the field may now omit it.
- **Verification**: fresh profile + fresh browser: transcript renders `detailed` without a saved setting.
- **Source**: [47db27a73](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/47db27a73) `fix(ui-chat): resolve work-details defaults in client code`, [b066690f7](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/b066690f7) `fix(web): default fresh work details to detailed`, [a03e63d1e](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/a03e63d1e) `fix(ui-chat): map legacy normal work details to detailed`.

cards.title: Schedule/time-context/ui-schedule rows leave the default web-app bundle; they ship as an optional bundle
cards.text:
### DSH-0.2.0-RC1-03 · Schedule/time-context/ui-schedule rows leave the default web-app bundle; they ship as an optional bundle

- **Type**: breaking
- **Applies to**: plugins and user patches that insert rows before/after the `schedule`, `time-context`, or `ui-schedule` ids, or that assumed those services exist in a default web profile
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging/composition special surface — profile patch row ids)
- **Action level**: required-if-hit
- **Symptoms**: the three rows were already shipped `disabled: true` at `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2`, so default profiles see no runtime change; they are now removed from `packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml` entirely and ship in the optional bundle `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle`. The real break is for user patches or plugins that re-enabled these rows by id (`disabled: false` on `schedule`/`time-context`/`ui-schedule`) or inserted relative to them: there is no such row to override any more, and the Schedule service they turned on is gone.
- **Migration recipe**: install `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-schedule-bundle` where the feature is wanted (and drop the by-id re-enable patch), or drop the dependency. Bundle authors: re-run your row-id inventory against the new patch files before inserting.
- **Verification**: `dsh --profile web --dump-config` contains no `schedule`/`time-context`/`ui-schedule` rows on a default profile.
- **Source**: [41c29fa83](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/41c29fa83) `feat(schedule): ship the Schedule switch as an optional bundle` and the schedule-bundle commit series; [`packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1/packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml).

cards.title: Bundle composition gains telemetry rows: `otel` (base) and desktop-gated product analytics (web-app)
cards.text:
### DSH-0.2.0-RC1-04 · Bundle composition gains telemetry rows: `otel` (base) and desktop-gated product analytics (web-app)

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: bundles and plugins that insert into the same composition, plugin-manager duplicate-id diagnostics
- **Touchpoints**: none (packaging/composition special surface — profile patch row ids)
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: `dsh-base` gains an `otel` row; `dsh-web-app` gains `desktop-product-telemetry` and `product-analytics` rows, both `disabled: !!js` unless the profile is `desktop`. A plugin or user patch inserting an id `otel` / `product-analytics` now shares an id with a bundle row; expect the composition to treat it as the same row (an override) or the loader to reject the duplicate id at boot — the exact failure text was not verified.
- **Migration recipe**: rename colliding ids; if you mirror the rows, gate them the same way.
- **Verification**: boot once and `--dump-config`; check that your inserted row and the bundle row are not merged or rejected.
- **Source**: [b1cf871b2](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/b1cf871b2) `feat(desktop): collect product analytics through OTel`; [`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml).

cards.title: `ISessions.fork` gains an optional `onCreated` callback
cards.text:
### DSH-0.2.0-RC1-05 · `ISessions.fork` gains an optional `onCreated` callback

- **Type**: capability
- **Applies to**: client plugins that fork sessions and want to observe the child before the optional rename
- **Touchpoints**: #3 (services/Remote — client `ISessions` contract)
- **Action level**: informational
- **Symptoms**: `fork(opts)` accepts `onCreated?: (childId: SessionId) => void` (existing calls unaffected); it observes the catalogued child before the optional rename.
- **Migration recipe**: none required for existing calls; pass `onCreated` where the pre-rename child id is needed.
- **Verification**: fork and assert the callback fires before rename.
- **Source**: [b1cf871b2](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/b1cf871b2) `feat(desktop): collect product analytics through OTel` (introduces `onCreated` for the desktop fork path); [`packages/api/session-controller/src/client/contract/sessions.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1/packages/api/session-controller/src/client/contract/sessions.ts#L136) at `dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1`.
- **Not a plugin change**: [3e6c10444](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/3e6c10444) and [f2af03539](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/f2af03539) are `perf(settings)` changes to `ConfigEditor.configuration()` (the settings UI read path): entries without a profile `config:` override share one composition, entries with their own `config:` key keep the existing per-entry `inherited()` path. The accompanying README text documents existing loader behavior, not a new override rule — no migration needed.

cards.title: Explorer path-opening spawns visible; the native-command runner gains a visibility argument — retire local reveal hotfixes
cards.text:
### DSH-0.2.0-RC1-06 · Explorer path-opening spawns visible; the native-command runner gains a visibility argument — retire local reveal hotfixes

- **Type**: fix
- **Applies to**: fleet installs carrying local patches to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-native-command` that passed raw paths or forced `windowsHide: false` so reveal/open shows a window
- **Touchpoints**: #7 (subprocess) if your plugin opens paths natively
- **Action level**: optional
- **Symptoms**: `runExplorer` now passes `'visible'` and `openInBrowser` passes `'hidden'` as a new runner argument; `explorerTarget` keeps the comma encoding that already shipped at 0.1.7-rc.1 ([95611fbc6](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/95611fbc6)). A local patch that rewrites `explorerTarget` to return raw paths now conflicts with the visible-window fix and can double-apply.
- **Migration recipe**: delete local reveal patches; the upstream form covers both the raw-path and window-visibility symptoms. Verify with a real `reveal` on Windows: an Explorer window opens with the file selected.
- **Verification**: reveal a file via the host tool; assert a visible Explorer window and no lingering headless `explorer.exe` process.
- **Source**: [a89506644](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/a89506644) `fix(windows): keep Explorer path-opening windows visible` ([#5223](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/pull/5223)); [`packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1/packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts) at `dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1`.
- **Field note** (first-hand, 2026-09-28): the local fleet hotfix (raw-path + `windowsHide: false`, carried since 0.1.7-alpha.2) was retired on this upgrade; the upstream form was verified by code inspection and the rc.2 empirical reveal test.

---

## Field notes outside this edge (observed on 0.2.0-rc.2, not yet carded)

> These two first-hand findings were observed on DeepSeek Harness **Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2** (Windows), not on `dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1`, and `apps/desktop-host` already exists at `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2`, so neither can be attributed to this edge. They are kept here as uncarded notes for a future `dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1 → dsh-v0.2.0-rc.2` card set; they carry no card IDs and are not counted in `cardCount`.

### Desktop note A — Desktop host: the plugin-visible `ctx.sessions` registry is empty — plugins resolving the session cwd through `sessions` fail on Desktop while working on Web

- *Type*: breaking
- *Applies to*: every plugin whose host half resolves the running session (or its workspace cwd) via `ctx.sessions.get(sessionId)`; install flows that rely on such plugins on the Desktop profile
- *Touchpoints*: #3 (services — service resolution), special surface: the Desktop runner (`dsh-desktop-host` → `runProfile`) instead of the CLI app-boot
- *Action level*: required-if-hit
- *Symptoms*:
  - On the Desktop host, `ctx.sessions.get(id)` returns `undefined` for **every** id, including a session the same host is actively running (its `session.v4.jsonl.zstd` is being appended at that moment). The plugin's cordis `inject: ['webServer', 'loader', 'sessions']` still resolves and the plugin activates — a service named `sessions` exists, but its live-session registry reads empty from a plugin fiber.
  - The Web host with the identical dsh version, profile bundles, and plugin tree works: the same probe flow (batch → file PUT → commit) completes and files land under `<workspace>/.dsh/tmp/attachments/`.
  - User-visible: a paste/attachment plugin's chips render but resolve "unavailable" (no file is ever written) and sending fails.
  - Unverified suspicion: the Desktop runner boots the composition with a different cordis fiber/isolate layout than the CLI app-boot, so the `sessions` service a plugin resolves is not the registry the agent runtime populates.
- *Migration recipe*: plugin-side workaround, verified first-hand — no host changes needed.
  1. **Session resolution fallback**: when `ctx.sessions.get(sessionId)` misses, resolve the workspace through `ctx.get('workspaceRegistry')` — the registry maps header-validated `sessionIds` to canonical workspace `path`s (`resolve(workspace.path)` is the cwd). Still entirely server-side: no client-supplied path enters the resolution, so the original security model holds. Keep the canonical lookup first; the fallback changes nothing on Web.
  2. **Binary request bodies do not survive `dsh-app://` forwarding either**: a Blob PUT arrives with a declared `Content-Length` that no longer matches the received bytes (the body is re-encoded in a text-safe way), so any size/content validation rejects it. Ship a base64-JSON transport for the Desktop origin (`location.protocol === 'dsh-app:'` detection; e.g. `POST .../files/<n>/base64` with `{ "data": "<base64>" }`, server decodes and checks the decoded length against the declared size) and keep the binary fast path on Web. Verified end-to-end: paste → upload → commit → file lands under `<workspace>/.dsh/tmp/attachments/`.
  3. Track the upstream reports: [discussion #8303](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8303) (includes the confirmed workaround) and the companion issue in the dsh-external beta channel.
  4. Re-verify after every Desktop release: one `POST` against the plugin's session-resolving endpoint with a live session id is enough to see `200` vs the `live session not found` family of failures; once the host registry is fixed the fallback simply stops firing.
- *Verification*: on the Desktop host, with one session running, call a plugin endpoint that starts from `ctx.sessions.get(sessionId)`; assert the resolved session and `session.header.cwd`. `--dump-config` cannot see this: the plugin mounts and serves; only the session lookup fails.
- *Source*: observed first-hand on DeepSeek Harness Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2 (Windows) against the bundled runtime; [`packages/api/session-controller`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1/packages/api/session-controller) and the Desktop runner entry at `dsh-desktop-host` at `dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1`.
- **Field note** (first-hand, 2026-09-29): unauthenticated probes against the Desktop host (127.0.0.1:19387): `GET /dsh-paste-input/v1/latest → 200` (host half mounted), `POST /dsh-paste-input/v1/batches → 400 "live session not found: <id>"` for both a live and a persisted session id. Same probes on the Web host (port 3080, same rc.2) complete the whole upload flow. Reported upstream as [discussion #8303](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8303).

### Desktop note B — Desktop host spawns tool subprocesses with a minimal `PATH`; `pwsh` is not resolvable on Windows

- *Type*: behavior
- *Applies to*: plugins and skills whose host-side code shells out to platform tools resolved from `PATH` (package managers, shells, git); anything assuming the CLI login-shell environment on Desktop
- *Touchpoints*: #7 (subprocess)
- *Action level*: conditional
- *Symptoms*: subprocesses spawned by sessions on the Desktop host see a minimal `PATH` — `System32` tools resolve, but `pwsh` does not (`spawnSync pwsh ENOENT`). The 0.2.0-rc.2 release notes fix the missing login-shell environment for macOS/Linux graphical launches; Windows Desktop appears to still need the equivalent.
- *Migration recipe*: resolve executables by absolute path when the environment is known (derive from well-known install locations), or degrade with a clear message instead of relying on `PATH` lookup on the Desktop profile.
- *Verification*: from a Desktop-hosted session, spawn `pwsh -Command `$PSVersionTable.PSVersion`` and observe ENOENT; the same spawn from a Web-hosted session succeeds.
- *Source*: observed first-hand on Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2 (Windows); [`apps/desktop/README.md`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1/apps/desktop/README.md) and the macOS/Linux login-shell fix in the [rc.1 → rc.2 compare](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/dsh-v0.2.0-rc.1...dsh-v0.2.0-rc.2) (`fix(desktop): supply login shell environment on macOS and Linux graphical launches`).
- **Field note** (first-hand, 2026-09-29): a tool subprocess under the Desktop host failed `spawnSync pwsh` with ENOENT while `netstat`/`wmic` (System32) resolved normally; the identical spawn from the Web host worked.
